title: Iraq PM hails new era of 'sovereignty' after US-led coalition exit
author: AFP
description: Coalition troops were deployed to Iraq and Syria in 2014 to fight IS; Pentagon will continue to provide targeted training and intelligence support to Iraq.
text: A US-led coalition deployed in Iraq more than a decade ago to fight militants concluded its mission on Wednesday, a move celebrated by the country’s leaders. Coalition troops were deployed to Iraq and Syria in 2014 to fight the Islamic State group, which had seized large swathes of territory, committing massacres and forcing thousands of women and children into slavery. The group was defeated in Iraq in 2017 and in Syria in 2019, but coalition forces stayed on to battle the group’s remnants. The United States and Iraq agreed in 2024 to wind down the coalition’s mission, and its troops withdrew gradually from bases across the country, restricting their presence to the autonomous northern Kurdistan region. On Wednesday, the US announced the mission’s formal conclusion. “Today, the United States and our Coalition partners formally concluded Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq, consistent with the September 2024 US-Iraq joint statement and US national interests,” the Pentagon said in a statement. The US Department of Defence, however, added that it would “continue to provide targeted training and intelligence support to our Iraqi partners”. The US-led coalition did not defeat IS alone. Kurdish Peshmerga fighters played an important role in crushing IS, as did powerful Iraqi factions. The Iraqi government, which celebrated the withdrawal, believes it will deprive armed factions of the excuse they have used to retain their arsenal. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi hailed the end of the mission as the start of a new chapter. “A new phase has begun, defined by Iraq’s sovereignty, the strength of its institutions, the readiness of its forces, unity of decision-making, and balanced partnerships with its friends,” Zaidi said at a ceremony on Wednesday. He had also declared that October 1 would be celebrated as Sovereignty Day. It is “a national occasion that affirms the completion of Iraq’s path toward sovereignty and consolidates the presence of the state and its institutions”, the heads of Iraq’s executive, legislative and judicial branches said on Monday. They added that “the presence of weapons outside state authority must be addressed… in line with timelines set by the government, in a manner that strengthens state sovereignty”. Zaidi, who came to power this year with the US’s blessing, has vowed to reinforce the state’s monopoly on arms and ensure that armed factions hand over their weapons to the state. His government initially set September 30 as the deadline for factions to disarm, but later withdrew the time limit as talks continued to “regulate” weapons — an issue that has fuelled division and is expected to take much longer to resolve. With several powerful groups refusing to disarm, senior politicians have intervened and are now hoping to work out a compromise deal. Factions have put forward conditions that include not only the withdrawal of foreign troops, but also an end to American political and economic interference. The powerful Kataeb Hezbollah group said the withdrawal of “the occupation forces… is a start towards achieving full sovereignty”. But the group also threatened Zaidi’s government. “A government that doesn’t work for the good of its people will be brought down by all possible means,” it said. Many armed groups have long demanded the withdrawal of US troops and have begun targeting them with drones and missiles, triggering US retaliatory strikes that killed several faction commanders over the years.

title: CM okays plan to enhance Sindh police’s counterterrorism capabilities
author: APP
description: With an estimated cost of Rs9.5bn, the government will build a new SSU headquarters and training academy at Chaukhandi.
text: KARACHI: Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Tuesday approved a Rs9.5 billion project to establish a state-of-the-art Special Security Unit (SSU) Headquarters and Security Training Academy at Chaukhandi in a bid to transform Sindh Police’s specialised security and counterterrorism training capabilities in line with national and international standards. Chairing a meeting here, he directed the Planning and Development and Home Departments to review their master plan and submit their recommendations for placing the project before the relevant forums for approval. The chief minister reviewed the comprehensive proposal for the integrated security complex and directed the Home Department, Police Department, Planning & Development Department and Finance Department to expedite all procedural requirements so that Phase-I of the project could commence during the current financial year. Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar, Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah, Home Secretary Iqbal Memon, Inspector General of Police Javed Alam Odho, Principal Secretary to CM Agha Wasif, Chairman P&D Najam Shah, Finance Secretary Asghar Memon, and senior police officers attended the meeting. With an estimated cost of Rs9.5bn, the government will build a new SSU headquarters and training academy at Chaukhandi The proposed project seeks to consolidate command, training, accommodation and support infrastructure of the SSU at a single purpose-built campus spread over approximately 29.43 acres at Chaukhandi, providing modern facilities for more than 3,000 male and 300 female personnel. The CM was briefed that existing police training facilities in Sindh were designed for an earlier era and no longer adequately address modern security challenges, particularly specialised commando training, urban warfare preparedness, simulation-based exercises and advanced tactical operations. The proposed academy will include a dedicated headquarters building, academic and administrative blocks, auditoriums, research and development facilities, libraries, computer laboratories, classrooms, indoor and outdoor firing ranges, tactical training complexes, simulation rooms, combat training zones, K-9 training facilities, a SWAT challenge obstacle course, sports and fitness infrastructure, accommodation blocks, officers’ residences and comprehensive welfare facilities. Speaking on the occasion, CM Shah said that strengthening the capacity of Sindh Police remained one of the government’s foremost priorities. The nature of security threats has evolved significantly over the years. Our security institutions must be equipped with modern infrastructure, advanced training systems and specialised capabilities to effectively respond to emerging challenges, he said. The chief minister observed that the proposed facility would serve as a centre of excellence for specialised security training and would substantially enhance the operational readiness of the SSU. This project is not merely about constructing buildings; it is an investment in the long-term security architecture of Sindh. It will strengthen institutional capacity, improve professional standards and ensure sustained preparedness against evolving threats, he said. He emphasised that a dedicated training academy would enable SSU personnel to receive continuous professional development through modern simulation-based training and specialised tactical exercises aligned with international best practices. The meeting was informed that the master plan also envisages accommodation facilities for thousands of personnel, dining halls capable of serving 1,000 persons at a time, an indoor sports and training complex with a swimming pool and gymnasium, a medical dispensary, conference facilities, armoury storage, driving simulators, parade grounds and secure parking areas. Special security features including a CCTV command centre, controlled access systems, watch towers and bomb-proof perimeter walls have also been incorporated into the design. Reviewing the financial framework, the chief minister was informed that the total estimated project cost stands at Rs9.497bn, while Phase-I, costing approximately Rs4.483bn, has been proposed for implementation over the next two financial years. The Home Department proposed an initial reappropriation of Rs500 million to commence priority works. Mr Shah endorsed the phased implementation strategy, observing that it would allow the government to undertake critical development works while maintaining fiscal discipline and safeguarding funding for other priority projects. The chief minister directed the Finance Department and Planning & Development Department to complete technical and financial scrutiny of the project on priority and report to him. He granted in-principle approval to the project and directed the concerned departments to initiate the necessary procedures to commence Phase-I within the current financial year. text: KARACHI: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Tuesday sentenced a man to death on two counts in a case pertaining to the kidnapping and murder of a lawyer after his ransom demand was not fulfilled. Deceased advocate Syed Farhat Ali Askari, 70, was abducted by some criminals in 2020. Later, his wife received a ransom call demanding Rs40 million, otherwise the kidnappers threatened to kill her husband and as she failed to fulfil their demands, the kidnappers killed him by strangling him. On a lead provided by the accused, the body of the slain advocate was recovered from a suitcase that had been thrown into a nullah in Surjani Town near Taiser Town. The police had arrested four accused — Awais Ali Hashmi, Muhammad Faizan, Muhammad Saeed and Iftikhar Ahmed Khatri — and they were tried by an ATC, where all four accused were convicted in 2023. ATC exonerates three co-accused from charges of abducting septuagenarian advocate for Rs40m ransom in 2020 However, the verdict was challenged before the Sindh High Court, which remanded back the case to the trial court with directions to record the statements of the convicts afresh. After recording the statements and examining the evidence, the ATC-1 Judge, found Awais guilty on two counts and sentenced him to hang till death and imposed a fine of total Rs500,000. “I would like to observe that the act of the accused, whereby he kidnapped Syed Farhat Ali Askari, demanded ransom amount Rs 4 Crore from his wife for releasing her husband, and due to non-fulfillment of demand committed murder of Syed Farhat Ali Askari, who was practicing advocate, and threw his dead body in a dirty/polluted Nala (drain), in such a brutal manner, squarely falls within the definition of “terrorism” as defined under Section 6 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, as such act definitely created panic and fear in the minds of the general public as well as the locality and the legal fraternity. Therefore, the accused is convicted and sentenced under the provisions of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997,” the judge observed. However, the ATC acquitted remaining accused —Faizan, Iftikhar and Saeed — as prosecution failed to prove its case against them. They were implicated in the case on the basis of confessional statement of Awais to the police; however, the court noted “the confessional statement of co-accused can only be used against other accused, if there is other evidence, direct or circumstantial connecting the accused with such crime. It is well-settled that if confession made by one accused can be taken into consideration against another accused, not as a substantive piece of evidence but as a corroboratory piece of evidence which requires independent corroboration”. A case was registered at the Shahrah-i-Noor Jahan police station under Sections 302 (murder) 365-A (kidnapping) 34 (common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code, read with Section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997. title: Ahead of deal on Hormuz, US and Iran ramp up the rhetoric again
author: Agencies
description: Tehran awaiting formal reply to its proposal to reopen troubled strait; Qatari mediators trying to find common ground.
text: • Tehran awaiting formal reply to its proposal to reopen troubled strait; Qatari mediators trying to find common ground • Ghalibaf warns of fresh strikes if provoked; IRGC urges American voters to oppose war • Oil prices fall as Saudi Arabia resumes loading at Yanbu port; US offers 40m barrels from strategic reserve to rein in soaring fuel prices • Turkiye seizes Iranian plane; Iraqi airlines granted exemption to ferry pilgrims to Najaf WASHINGTON / TEHRAN: Ahead of a possible agreement over the Strait of Hormuz, both the US and Iran turned up the rhetoric against each other, with President Donald Trump once again expressing confidence that the war in the Middle East will end “very, very soon”. Iranian state media quoted Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi as saying that he expected a formal answer on Tuesday to Tehran’s proposal to open the troubled waterway. The remarks came as the British maritime agency reported that an “unknown projectile” struck a ship in the strait, sparking a fire on board that was subsequently extinguished. Qatari intermediaries “presented ideas, and we discussed them; they are set to raise the matter with the American side once more, after which the final US response will be conveyed to us”, Araghchi had said late on Monday night. Mr Araghchi, who is in New York for the UN General Assembly, said the current focus was solely on the Strait of Hormuz, and the reopening of the strait was contingent upon the fulfilment of certain conditions that they have communicated to “the other side”. Earlier, US and Iranian officials spoke separately with mediators on Monday as part of a renewed effort to end the seven-month war, according to officials of both countries. On Tuesday, Qatari foreign mi­n­­­i­stry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said there had been “several meetings and messages have been exchanged, including some in New York and earlier. Current efforts are focused on building com­mon ground between the parties.” As a precondition for ending its blockade, Iran is demanding a seven-day ceasefire across the Middle East, including in Lebanon, where its ally Hezbollah is regularly bombed by Israel. It is also demanding the unfreezing of its assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade on its ports. However, President Trump claimed that he had offered Iran no concessions, rejecting media reports that cited US officials saying he was willing to ease sanctions and release frozen funds for “concrete” steps regarding Iran’s nuclear programme. Axios and CNN both reported, citing unidentified US officials, that Trump was willing to give Iran sanctions relief and free Iranian funds as part of a final deal on the condition that Iran showed “concrete progress” on the nuclear issue. “This is untrue. I offered them NOTHING,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday. On Tuesday, the Revolutionary Guards said “the US claim that it remains open is false”. “Sneaking a few hundred barrels of oil through under the cover of darkness — with transponders turned off and at great cost — does not constitute the strait being open,” said spokesperson Hossein Mohebi. “A truly open strait is one where, as in the past, at least 125 vessels would pass through daily, transporting a minimum of 20 million barrels of oil and petroleum products. “Any vessel attempting to pass through sustains damage — either we strike it, or it hits a mine,” he added. Meanwhile, Tehran’s chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf threatened fresh attacks, saying no infrastructure in the region would be safe if his country’s security was not guaranteed. “In a region where we cannot sell oil, no one else will sell oil either; or if our security is not guaranteed, no infrastructure will remain safe,” Ghalibaf, who is also Iran’s parliament speaker, said according to a video released by state TV. Separately, the Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) appealed to US midterm voters to reject President Trump’s policies and accept an offer of peaceful coexistence. The assertions were made on Tuesday in a 25-page open letter addressed to the American people, urging them to oppose US support for Israel and foreign wars and arguing that Iran and the US could coexist if US policy changed. The letter accused Trump of concealing the peaceful nature of Iran’s nuclear programme, which Israel in particular sees as an existential threat, and the effectiveness of Tehran’s blockade of Gulf oil. IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebi told reporters he did not expect the letter to affect the US administration’s behaviour some five weeks before the elections, but that voters might hear the message. Oil prices declined on Tuesday as Saudi Arabia resumed oil tanker loadings from its Red Sea port of Yanbu after restarting operations on the East-West Pipeline, improving the outlook for oil exports from the Middle East. Brent crude futures were down $1.38, or 1.3pc, to $103.88 a barrel at 1703 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was down $2.04 or 2.16pc at $90.58. Brent and WTI are headed for monthly gains of around 15pc and 5.7pc, respectively. The resumption of Yanbu loadings, halted earlier this month after a drone attack on the pipeline, which weighed on global oil prices, was notified by state oil giant Saudi Aramco as it unveiled its October loading schedule. “ESA satellite imagery captured over the Red Sea on September 27 shows Saudi Arabia loading nearly 10 million barrels of crude oil at Yanbu and Al Muajjiz,” vessel-tracking firm TankerTrackers.com wrote in a post on X on Tuesday. Al Muajjiz is a terminal south of Yanbu. The White House has urged the European Union to draw down diesel emergency inventories in a bid to lower global prices, sources said. Several European Union member countries have not released as much oil and refined products from reserves as they promised, President Donald Trump’s administration said. Meanwhile, the Trump administration said on Tuesday it is offering to loan energy companies 40 million barrels of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, in an effort to control soaring fuel prices that have jumped on the widening war with Iran and Russia’s war on Ukraine. The US has granted Iraqi Airways, the national carrier, a sanctions waiver allowing it to fly to Iran so it can ferry pilgrims travelling between Iran and Iraq’s holy city of Najaf. The transport ministry said flights were set to start from Najaf in October, “once the necessary organisational requirements have been fulfilled”. Meanwhile, Turkish authorities have seized a plane belonging to Iran’s Caspian Airlines at Istanbul Airport , with Turkish and Iranian media linking it to an unpaid three-million-euros($3.4 million) debt. The seizure took place on Monday after passengers had boarded the Boeing 737, which was waiting to take off when officials detained it on the basis of a court-issued seizure order, Anadolu Agency reported. Separately, Washington sanctioned 10 individuals and entities that allegedly procured weapons and weapons components for Iran’s Ministry of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics, the US Treasury Department’s website showed on Tuesday. title: The unholy alliance
author: Zahid Hussain
description: Its close military cooperation with Israel has drawn the UAE directly into the war on Iran.
text: THE Israeli prime minister’s reported secret visit to Abu Dhabi last Sunday has reinforced the growing nexus between the UAE and the Zionist state. It was not the first time that Benjamin Netanyahu had made an unannounced trip to the Gulf country. In March this year, at the height of the Iran war, he travelled there to meet UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed al-Nahyan. During the same period, the head of Mossad, Israel’s main intelligence agency, made two trips to the country to apparently coordinate military operations. And last week, while 77 nations boycotted the Israeli prime minister’s speech at the UN General Assembly, the UAE delegation remained seated — a clear show of solidarity with the Zionist state. Since joining the Abraham Accords in 2020, the UAE has not only established diplomatic relations with Israel but has gone much further, elevating the relationship into a de facto alliance — even as the Israeli state was carrying out a genocidal war in Gaza. That relationship deepened as the US, along with Israel, imposed an unprovoked war on Iran. The extraordinary relationship between the two countries marks a developing unholy alliance in a rapidly changing regional order, as America’s war on Iran drags on. The UAE has reportedly carried out its own strikes on Iran and has also borne the brunt of retaliatory strikes — with devastating effect — despite the deployment of the Iron Dome air defence system, run by Israeli military personnel. Its close military cooperation with Israel has drawn the UAE directly into the war on Iran. It is the first time this highly advanced system has been deployed outside Israel and the US, signalling the critical role of the Emirates in a potential Israeli-led regional defence alliance. It is also the first Arab-Israeli relationship to acquire real military and industrial substance. And this Israel-UAE nexus goes beyond the ongoing Iran war: the UAE appears to be a critical part of Israel’s plan to build what Netanyahu calls the “hexagon of alliances”. That idea was pitched by the Israeli prime minister early this year. Speaking at a cabinet meeting on Feb 22, 2026, days before the visit of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Netanyahu presented his vision of creating “a hexagon of alliances around or within the Middle East” — a bloc against what he described as the “radical Shia and emerging Sunni axis”. He named four members — Israel, India, Greece and Cyprus — and left the remaining slots (Arab, African and Asian states) unnamed. But it is widely assumed that the Emirates is one of the six, given its close diplomatic and defence ties with Israel. Netanyahu also pointed to intelligence-sharing and counterterrorism cooperation with India as the core of the project. Modi’s February visit produced a Special Strategic Partnership between the two countries, which have long cooperated on defence and intelligence. Israel is one of India’s largest arms suppliers. The UAE, too, has built close defence ties with New Delhi. All three are part of the four-nation I2U2 grouping, alongside the US, and of IMEC, the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor. This web of alliances, bound together by bilateral defence relationships, is shaping the emerging security landscape in West Asia and beyond. Although the Israeli-proposed hexagon alliance has not yet taken formal shape, it is widely seen as a potential counter to the Makkah alliance — which Israel portrays, wrongly, as a ‘Sunni alliance’. Netanyahu has repeatedly called Turkiye a greater threat than Iran and a major challenge to his ‘Greater Israel’ ambition. Against this background, the growing Israel-UAE diplomatic and defence cooperation is alarming. Over the past few years, the UAE has drifted away from its Gulf allies on a range of regional and foreign policy issues, above all by widening its differences with Saudi Arabia. The Emirates is accused of arming and financing a separatist group in strife-torn southern Yemen, bringing the UAE into conflict with Riyadh. It is also widely believed to be arming and funding an armed group involved in Sudan’s civil war, one accused of mass atrocities. And it backs Somaliland , a breakaway region of Somalia recognised only by Israel — while every other Arab state supports a united Somalia. A few months ago, at the height of the Iran war, the Emirates pulled out of Opec, the Saudi-led oil cartel, severely damaging the organisation. Its close military cooperation with Israel has drawn the Emirates directly into the war on Iran, endangering its own security in the process. Any participation in an Israeli-proposed alliance could prove extremely destabilising for the region. Pakistan’s own relations with the Emirates have hit a low over the past few years. Early this year, the UAE withdrew a $3 billion deposit from the State Bank of Pakistan, and once-close ties have become significantly strained. With a large Pakistani workforce in the Emirates, the shift has put Pakistan in a very difficult position, which requires a delicate balancing act. The widening regional divide — in the middle of the Iran war, Israel’s continuing genocide in Gaza and its military actions in Lebanon — is extremely troubling. Israel’s idea of a ‘hexagon alliance’ that also includes India is dangerous for Pakistan’s security, particularly as Israel and India are already tied in a strategic relationship. It is certainly not good news for the Middle East and the wider region, which is being rocked by America’s unending war on Iran. The situation has become much more complicated with the escalating conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi rebels in Yemen. Last week, the military chiefs of the three allied countries met to discuss the deteriorating situation, and there is talk that Article 5 of the alliance — under which an attack on one member is considered an attack on all — could be activated. Any such move could draw Pakistan directly into the conflict. With a resolution to the Iran war still far off, an expansion of the conflict could render the situation far more explosive. Against this backdrop, the unholy alliance between Israel and the UAE could further destabilise the region, with far-reaching implications. The writer is an author and journalist. title: Saudi Arabia resumes Yanbu oil loading after pipeline restart
author: Reuters
description: Two trade sources separately estimate crude loadings from Yanbu at about two million barrels per day since last week.
text: Saudi Arabia has resumed oil tanker loadings from its Red Sea port of Yanbu after restarting operations on the East-West Pipeline, according to trade sources and shipping data, improving the outlook for oil exports from the Middle East. The resumption of Yanbu loadings, halted earlier this month after a drone attack on the pipeline, weighed on global oil prices on Monday as it added to signs of increased flows from the Middle East, from which the US war with Iran has throttled oil shipments. State oil giant Saudi Aramco notified customers on Monday evening of its October loading schedule from Yanbu, an Asian refining source said. The refiner loaded a cargo from Yanbu late last week. Drone attacks, which Saudi Arabia blamed on the Houthis, forced the kingdom to shut the pipeline on September 11, halting crude exports from Yanbu. Pipeline operations resumed last Tuesday. Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment. European Space Agency satellite pictures also pointed to a resumption of loading. “ESA satellite imagery captured over the Red Sea on September 27 shows Saudi Arabia loading nearly 10 million barrels of crude oil at Yanbu and Al Muajjiz,” vessel-tracking firm TankerTrackers.com wrote in a post on X on Tuesday. Al Muajjiz is a terminal south of Yanbu. “We also observed refined-product loadings. In total, we visually identified 40 tankers, regardless of their activity or proximity to these terminals.” Two trade sources separately estimated crude loadings from Yanbu at about two million barrels per day since last week. Oil throughput on the pipeline is about 2m barrels per day, according to an industry source, and around 2.65m bpd according to ship-tracking firm Kpler. This is far short of the pipeline’s 7m bpd capacity. Throughput will climb to between 3m and 4m bpd in the coming days, Kpler said. A full return to the pre-attack rate of roughly 5.5m bpd could still take another month, it said in a note on Monday. Crude inventories at the Yanbu terminal rose by roughly 1m barrels on Sept 22, the first build since the attack, according to Kpler. The restart of crude loading at Yanbu added to signs of rising Middle East oil shipments following a recovery in exports via the Strait of Hormuz. Crude oil loadings at Egypt’s Sidi Kerir resumed on Sept 22 after a 10-day hiatus, but tankers remain queued offshore as restrictions continue to limit access for much of the commercial fleet, Kpler said in the note.

title: Trump unveils AI chatbot for US government services
author: AFP
description: America.gov will eventually be able to process all sorts of complicated tasks involving the government, such as applying for a new passport or accessing health and retirement benefits, US president says.
text: US President Donald Trump unveiled an AI-powered website on Tuesday aimed at becoming the first stop for Americans to access federal services, hailing the initiative as a “reinvention” of government. The “ America.gov ” platform was developed under Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia, who joined the Trump administration last year in the newly formed role of chief design officer. Like other websites using AI-powered chatbots, users type in queries and converse with the system online. While its functions are currently limited, Trump said that America.gov will eventually be able to process all sorts of complicated tasks involving the government, such as applying for a new passport or accessing health and retirement benefits. “We’re making it dramatically easier, faster, and more convenient to get what you need exactly when you need it,” Trump said at a launch event for the platform in Washington, attended by top government officials. “It’s a restoration of America’s founding promise and it’s a reinvention of your government for the 21st century and beyond,” he said. The president also signed an executive order directing all government agencies to integrate their websites with America.gov. The launch of the new US government platform comes the same day that Trump is to meet with an array of top tech executives to discuss the AI sector’s rapid development. A growing list of cyber incidents revealed in recent weeks has raised concerns around the world about risks posed by uncontrollable AI, with some executives urging a slowdown for safety. Trump has dismissed those concerns as a conspiracy to undermine US economic growth and hamper competition with China. AI and the rapid buildout of data centres have become a significant issue in the November midterm elections. A recent poll published by CNN showed 82 per cent of Americans expressed concern about the pace of AI development.

title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs1.49 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Rs2.73
author: News Desk
description: Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs387.54 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs402.24 per litre.
text: The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs1.49 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.73 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs387.54 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs402.24 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Sept 30 (Wednesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Sept 29 appreciated the success of the scheme , saying that it reflected a “whole of government” approach. Chairing a meeting of the National Steering Committee on Fuel Subsidy to review the implementation of the scheme, the deputy premier noted that the information, IT and petroleum ministries, as well as the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra), the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and all provinces, had made “concerted” efforts for the scheme. It was noted that to date, around 7.60 million registrations have been successfully made, and the token redemption process has entered the second week. Moreover, 7.71m tokens have been redeemed. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

description: Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal on Tuesday called for transforming CAREC transport routes into next-generation economic corridors by integrating infrastructure, logistics, digital connectivity, energy cooperation and climate resilience. Participating in a session of the 25th Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) Ministerial Conference in Ulaanbaatar, the Minister said Pakistan viewed CAREC Corridors 5 and 6 as an opportunity to connect Central Asia with the Arabian Sea and generate economic activity along the routes, according to a ministry statement. “The question is no longer simply, ‘Can a truck travel this route?’ It is, ‘Can a business use this route reliably, competitively and profitably?’” he said. The CAREC programme focuses on the development of six primary multimodal transport corridors that link north, south, east, and west across Eurasia. Iqbal said the transformation of regional corridors required completion of the transport chain through upgraded CAREC roads, modern border facilities at Torkham and Chaman, stronger rail freight capacity through the proposed ML-1 upgrade, and efficient links to dry ports and seaports. He stressed the need to establish logistics and production hubs along strategic locations, saying cold storage, packaging, warehousing and light manufacturing could transform transit traffic into exports, jobs and value for communities along the corridors. The minister also called for building a digital corridor across the CAREC region, noting that Pakistan Single Window (PSW) provided a foundation for phased digital integration with regional partners. “A consignment’s documents should be checked before it reaches the border,” he said. Highlighting the importance of regional energy cooperation and climate resilience, Iqbal said initiatives such as CASA-1000 demonstrated the potential of cross-border energy connectivity, while new roads, railways and logistics infrastructure must be designed to withstand floods and extreme heat. “The transformation occurs when a corridor carries more than cargo: it carries investment, technology, energy and opportunity,” he said. Responding to a question on regional actions needed to ensure shared benefits, the minister emphasised coordinated planning of entire corridors, stronger cross-border cooperation and measuring the impact of connectivity on businesses and communities. He said CAREC countries should identify priority cross-border projects, prepare them to common standards and coordinate investment and construction schedules, with the Asian Development Bank playing a role in mobilising financing, including private investment where appropriate. The minister called for treating borders as a shared service, with compatible operating hours, advance electronic information, coordinated procedures and fewer repeated checks. He also emphasised the need to measure border delays, delivery times, local employment, SME participation and opportunities for women and youth. “Regional cooperation succeeds when a trader can predict the journey, a farmer can reach a distant market without losing the harvest, and communities along the corridor share in its prosperity. That is how we move from connectivity to competitiveness,” Iqbal said. Earlier, addressing the opening session of the 25th CAREC Ministerial Conference under the theme 25 Years of Partnership, Shaping the Future Together, the minister said Pakistan looked forward to assuming the CAREC Chairmanship in 2027 and hosting the 26th Ministerial Conference. He said Pakistan, located at the intersection of Central Asia, South Asia and maritime routes, sought to turn its geographical position into an engine of shared regional growth through stronger connectivity, trade, digital integration and regional value chains. On the sidelines of the 25th CAREC Ministerial Conference in Ulaanbaatar, he witnessed the signing of a memorandum of understanding between the CAREC Capital Markets Development Forum (CMDF) and the ASEAN Capital Markets Forum (ACMF). The MoU aims to strengthen cooperation and facilitate greater connectivity between the capital markets of CAREC and ASEAN member countries, creating opportunities for knowledge sharing, regulatory cooperation and deeper regional financial integration.

title: Somali forces recover oil tanker carrying Pakistani crewmen over 5 months after hijacking by pirates
author: News Desk | Shazia Hasan
description: “The naval and ground units of the Puntland Maritime Police Force conducted a planned operation in the Dharin-Bar area of Bandar Beyla district,” police statement says.
text: KARACHI: Somali maritime police said on Tuesday that they had recovered an oil tanker, the MT Honour 25, which was hijacked by armed pirates off the coast of Puntland, Somalia on April 21. The Honour 25 — a Palau-flagged oil tanker — had 19 crew members on board, including 10 Pakistanis. “The naval and ground units of the Puntland Maritime Police Force conducted a planned operation in the Dharin-Bar area of Bandar Beyla district,” the maritime police said in a statement. The Honour 25 had 18,500 barrels of oil onboard when it was hijacked, it added. Reuters reported, citing Puntland’s state television, that the pirates holding the vessel had been detained and would be brought to court. Dawn has contacted the Foreign Office (FO) for a comment. Meanwhile, Ayesha Ameen, the wife of a fitter on the ship, told Dawn between sobs that there were reports of casualties among Pakistanis on the ship. She said that they were not able to confirm the names of the deceased yet, but her husband, Ameen Bin Shams, was reportedly among the injured. “We don’t know how bad the injuries are,” she said. “We are trying to establish contact with the ship’s captain on the numbers that we have. But our calls are not being answered. “As far as we know, the bodies are still on the ship, as are the injured. There is no one to tell us if they will be moved. We are going mad here,” she added. Initial reports attributed to the crew suggest that there have been five deaths and four people have been injured. Apart from Pakistanis, the vessel’s crew also included seven Indonesians, an Indian and a Sri Lankan. After its hijacking in April, months had passed with no progress either in negotiations or the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for the recovery of the hostages. The hostages were said to be victims of an “ ownership crisis ”, as it was not clearly established who owned the ship — the man previously thought to be an owner was later revealed to be more likely a middleman who hired them. Since its hijack, the crew had made several emotional videos and audio appeals , reporting that they had run out of clean water, food and medicine. Meanwhile, their families launched an international appeal, calling on foreign governments, the United Nations (UN) and the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) to take coordinated action to help secure the release of their loved ones. For its part, the FO maintained that it remained “actively engaged” to secure the release of the sailors. Last month, in a meeting with the International Maritime Organisation’s head, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar pressed for “urgent and effective institutional intervention” for the return of the Pakistani sailors. Earlier that month, he had also directed “stakeholders” to intensify diplomatic engagement with national and international partners to facilitate the release. Somali piracy has seen a resurgence, with at least 15 attacks since April, the highest since 2013. This is a developing story that is being updated as the situation evolves. Initial reports in the media can sometimes be inaccurate. We will strive to ensure timeliness and accuracy by relying on credible sources, such as concerned, qualified authorities and our staff reporters.

title: Govt to establish largest facilitation centre for CNIC, passport services in Karachi:Naqvi
author: BR Web Desk
description: The federal government will establish the country’s largest public facilitation centre under the Federal Ministry of Interior in Karachi, offering multiple citizen services under one roof. Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who visited the Ministry of Interior office on I.I. Chundrigar Road on Tuesday, directed authorities to prepare and submit the master plan for the Grand Facilitation Centre within 10 days, according to a press release. The minister said counters of all departments and organisations working under the Interior Ministry would be available at the centre. Citizens will be able to access services including passports, CNICs, arms licences and various no-objection certificates (NOCs) at one location. Naqvi directed the authorities to incorporate all necessary requirements into the master plan and take immediate measures for establishment of the centre. Separately, 21 new vehicles for Islamabad Rescue 1122 and the Fire Brigade arrived at Karachi Port from China, marking the biggest expansion of Islamabad Rescue’s fleet since 2009. Naqvi inspected the vehicles at Karachi Port and said the new fleet would strengthen emergency response in Islamabad. The vehicles are expected to reach the capital within five days. The new fleet includes four aerial fire trucks, six fire towers and five fire tenders, with the vehicles equipped with modern firefighting and rescue equipment. According to a briefing, the vehicles can conduct rescue and firefighting operations at heights of up to 256 feet. The new fleet will remain available round-the-clock at six stations across Islamabad. Naqvi thanked the Chinese government for expediting the supply of the vehicles, describing their arrival as a welcome development for Islamabad’s emergency response system.

title: Tax returns: Pakistan banks to extend working hours on Sept 30
author: BR Web Desk
description: Commercial banks in Pakistan will keep all their branches open until 10:00pm on Wednesday, September 30, to facilitate over-the-counter (OTC) payment of government duties and taxes. According to a statement from the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), the decision was taken at the request of the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to facilitate taxpayers in making payments on the last day of September. The SBP also advised banks to keep concerned branches open for as long as required to facilitate special clearing of government transactions conducted by the National Institutional Facilitation Technologies (NIFT). It further directed banks to ensure uninterrupted availability of online payment channels, including internet banking, mobile applications, ATMs and other digital platforms, for payment of government duties and taxes. It may be noted that September 30 is the deadline for filing tax returns in Pakistan. On Monday, Atif Ikram Sheikh, President of the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FPCCI), urged the government and the FBR to extend the deadline for filing income tax returns by one month – moving the cutoff date to October 31, 2026 – to facilitate trade, industry, and other tax filers.

title: Saudi Arabia resumes Yanbu oil loading after pipeline restart
author: Reuters
description: SINGAPORE: Saudi Arabia has resumed oil tanker loadings from its Red Sea port of Yanbu after restarting operations on the East-West Pipeline, according to trade sources and shipping data, improving the outlook for oil exports from the Middle East. The resumption of Yanbu loadings, halted earlier this month after a drone attack on the pipeline, weighed on global oil prices on Monday as it added to signs of increased flows from the Middle East, from which the US war with Iran has throttled oil shipments. State oil giant Saudi Aramco notified customers on Monday evening of its October loading schedule from Yanbu, an Asian refining source said. The refiner loaded a cargo from Yanbu late last week. Drone attacks, which Saudi Arabia blamed on Iraqi militias, forced the kingdom to shut the pipeline on September 11, halting crude exports from Yanbu. Pipeline operations resumed last Tuesday. Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Mideast oil exports rebound in September as Saudi Arabia boosts shipments Oil products are also being loaded, tracker says European Space Agency satellite pictures also pointed to a resumption of loading. “ESA satellite imagery captured over the Red Sea on September 27 shows Saudi Arabia loading nearly 10 million barrels of crude oil at Yanbu and Al Muajjiz,” vessel-tracking firm TankerTrackers wrote in a post on X on Tuesday. Al Muajjiz is a terminal south of Yanbu. “We also observed refined-product loadings. In total, we visually identified 40 tankers, regardless of their activity or proximity to these terminals.” Two trade sources separately estimated crude loadings from Yanbu at about 2 million barrels per day since last week. Saudi Arabia restarts East-West oil pipeline, sources say Oil throughput on the pipeline is about 2 million barrels per day, according to an industry source, and around 2.65 million bpd according to ship-tracking firm Kpler. This is far short of the pipeline’s 7 million bpd capacity. Throughput will climb to between 3 million and 4 million bpd in the coming days, Kpler said. A full return to the pre-attack rate of roughly 5.5 million bpd could still take another month, it said in a note on Monday. Crude inventories at the Yanbu terminal rose by roughly 1 million barrels on September 22, the first build since the attack, according to Kpler. The restart of crude loading at Yanbu added to signs of rising Middle East oil shipments following a recovery in exports via the Strait of Hormuz. Crude oil loadings at Egypt’s Sidi Kerir resumed on September 22 after a 10-day hiatus, but tankers remain queued offshore as restrictions continue to limit access for much of the commercial fleet, Kpler said in the note.

title: Saudi crown prince, UAE vice president meet in Riyadh: report
author: AFP
description: The two met to “review brotherly bilateral relations and regional developments”, the Saudi Press Agency says.
text: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Riyadh on Tuesday, Saudi official media reported, months after the two countries fell out over Yemen. The meeting comes as the kingdom reels from weeks of attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels on its tankers, oil facilities, airports and even its capital, after the group took control of the Red Sea coast from Saudi-led Yemeni government forces. Riyadh has for weeks been reaching out to international allies for help against the Houthis. The crown prince and the vice president met to “review brotherly bilateral relations and regional developments”, the Saudi Press Agency said, adding the sit-down was also attended by Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman. Last December, Riyadh accused Abu Dhabi of threatening its national security by supporting southern Yemeni separatists who orchestrated a brief offensive in government-held areas. But in July, top officials and ministers from Saudi Arabia and the UAE began posting messages on social media about friendship and unity, signalling a rapprochement. That same month, Yemen’s civil war roared back to life when the Houthis launched a new campaign against Saudi-led government forces, taking over a swath of territory and launching attacks on Saudi soil. The group has also declared a maritime blockade on Saudi ships in the Red Sea. Riyadh has been carrying out strikes on the Houthis, while for weeks reaching out to international allies for help. Saudi Arabia and the UAE have been at odds on foreign policy for some time, from Yemen and Sudan to the Horn of Africa, where they have supported rival forces.

title: PM Shehbaz meets global financial firms in London, invites them to invest and expand services in Pakistan
author: Syed Irfan Raza
description: Premier holds meetings with senior officials from JP Morgan, Barclays, Rothschild & Co; becomes first Pakistani PM to open trading at London Stock Exchange.
text: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday met with senior executives from leading global financial institutions in London and invited them to invest and expand their services in Pakistan. During a busy day in the UK capital, the premier held a series of meetings with top officials of Barclays, JP Morgan, Citi, BlackRock and Rothschild & Co. Earlier in the day, he also became the first Pakistani prime minister to open trading at the London Stock Exchange, according to his office. In a statement, the PM’s Office (PMO) said the premier’s engagements with the global firms “underscored growing international financial sector interest in Pakistan’s economic reform trajectory and improving investment climate”. In his meeting with a high-level JP Morgan delegation led by its co-CEO for Europe, Middle East and Africa Matthieu Wiltz, PM Shehbaz invited the firm to expand its footprint in Pakistan. He discussed deepening the partnership across capital markets, trade finance and investment banking. According to PMO, the JP Morgan delegation “reaffirmed its interest in sovereign debt capital markets and corporate banking opportunities”. Meeting with Mohammad Kamal Syed, head of Private Bank and Wealth Management UK at Barclays, PM Shehbaz briefed him on the government’s macroeconomic stabilisation measures and encouraged Barclays to explore opportunities in the country’s financial sector. The prime minister welcomed the bank’s “interest in Pakistan”, PMO said. PM Shehbaz also met with Rothschild & Co, represented by Chair of Geostrategic Advisory Lord Mark Sedwill and Head of UK Investment Banking Majid Ishaq. “Discussions centred on Pakistan’s geo-economic priorities and potential advisory collaboration on capital markets and investment strategy,” PMO said. The premier also met a group of senior officials of Citi, led by Chief Client Officer David Livingstone, encouraging the bank to expand its “corporate and institutional banking services” in Pakistan. The prime minister commended Citi’s long-standing presence in Pakistan, the statement added. In his meeting with a BlackRock delegation, PM Shehbaz “invited increased allocations to Pakistani equities and fixed income within the firm’s frontier markets strategy, with both sides emphasising the importance of sustained policy consistency in building investor confidence”. The delegation comprised the co-heads of Emerging Markets and Frontiers, Gordon Fraser and Sam Vecht, along with Portfolio Manager and Research Analyst Emily Fletcher. “Across all engagements, the visiting executives expressed confidence in Pakistan’s economic reform momentum and reaffirmed their institutions’ commitment to deepening engagement with the country’s financial sector,” PMO said. It asserted that the meetings reflected the “growing traction of Pakistan’s economic reform programme among the world’s leading financial institutions”. The engagements also “mark a significant step in the government’s broader effort to strengthen international investor confidence and attract sustained capital flows into the country”, the statement highlighted. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and Adviser to PM on Privatisation Muhammad Ali, who also heads the Privatisation Commission, were present in the meetings as well. In an earlier statement, PMO noted that PM Shehbaz became the first prime minister from Pakistan to open the London Stock Exchange’s (LSE) trading session. He also formally inaugurated Pakistan’s landmark $3 billion dual-tranche sovereign Eurobond, raised earlier this month. LSE’s market opening ceremony is held at its headquarters in Paternoster Square and formally marks the start of the trading day in London. London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) Chief Executive Officer David Schwimmer and senior officials of the group welcomed the prime minister on his arrival. Aurangzeb, the LSEG CEO, the Privatisation Commission head, Pakistan High Commissioner Tipu Usman, members of the Pakistani delegation and relevant British authorities attended the ceremony. “Pakistan in recent years has worked very hard to strengthen its economy,” PM Shehbaz said while addressing the audience, terming the country’s improved macroeconomic indicators as “promising” for the future. He went on to praise Aurangzeb and his team for arranging the Eurobond sale, which he said explained “our hard work” in volumes. The premier claimed that if the Middle East conflict had not erupted, Pakistan would have “taken off like other emerging economies”. He also highlighted Islamabad’s role as a mediator in the war between the United States and Iran . “Now is the time, because of this Gulf crisis, new lessons have to be learnt,” PM Shehbaz stressed. “Investors are now trying to evaluate and assess safer markets and Pakistan is a market where we can easily attract foreign investments, which are highly profitable, mutually beneficial, safe and secure,” he noted. The prime minister expressed “his happiness on his participation to open London Stock Exchange session” and termed it a step towards “rebuilding their wonderful connection” with LSE, PMO said. Addressing the LSEG CEO, the premier said that they would like to seek his guidance and advice on how to further engage international financial markets to play a role in Pakistan, not just in terms of sovereign debt but through very attractive investments. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb met Standard Chartered Bank’s CEO Bill Winters in London on Tuesday, according to a statement by the finance ministry. Aurangzeb “appreciated SCB’s continued support to Pakistan and its cooperation in various financing and capital market transactions”, the statement said. The ministry said that the two discussed Pakistan’s ongoing structural reforms and the latest macroeconomic developments. They also discussed future areas of collaboration, including “tokenisation, international Sukuk and other financing opportunities”, according to the statement. “SCB’s strong investor network across Europe, the Middle East and Asia can play an important role in facilitating continued investor outreach and enhancing market visibility for Pakistan,” the ministry said. The discussions also included potential capital market transactions to support the privatisation programme of the government, covering opportunities on both the buy-side and sell-side, it added. Advisor to the Prime Minister on Privatisation Muhammad Ali and Advisor to the Finance Minister Omer Khan were also present in the meeting.

title: Karachi to get one-stop facilitation centre for CNIC, passport services; Naqvi seeks master plan in 10 days
author: News Desk
description: 21 new vehicles arrive at Karachi port from China for Islamabad's rescue, firefighting fleet.
text: Karachiites would be able to access passport, CNIC and other services under one roof at the “Pakistan’s largest public facilitation centre” planned for the city, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi announced on Tuesday. He made this announcement during a visit to the Ministry of Interior’s office located on Karachi’s I.I. Chundrigar Road, according to a statement issued by the ministry. The statement quoted Naqvi as saying that the counters of all departments and organisations under his ministry would be set up centre, the statement said. “The citizens will be able to access passport, CNIC, arms licence, various NOCs and other services under one roof,” he added. The minister directed that the master plan for the facilitation centre must be prepared and submitted within 10 days. ‎“The master plan will be prepared while taking into account all necessary requirements,” he said, adding, “The facilitation centre will provide citizens with a range of services under one roof.” ‎The statement said that Naqvi also directed the authorities to ensure all necessary measures for the establishment of the facilitation centre. Naqvi also with the Karachi Port, where ‎‎21 new vehicles for Islamabad Rescue 1122 and the fire brigade had arrived after 17 years, the interior ministry said in a separate statement. During the visit, the statement said, Naqvi inspected the new vehicles that arrived from China. ‎“The new rescue vehicles will reach Islamabad from Karachi within five days,” the ministry said. ‎Speaking on the occasion, Naqvi said the arrival of the new vehicles for Islamabad rescue and fire brigade services was a welcome development, according to the statement. “The addition of new vehicles to Islamabad rescue was the biggest expansion since 2009,” he was quoted as saying. “We are grateful to the government of China for expediting the supply of these new vehicles,” he added. ‎The ministry’s statement said that the modern rescue vehicles would remain available round-the-clock at six stations across Islamabad. The new rescue vehicles were capable of conducting operations at heights of up to 256 feet, the statement said. ‎It further said that the new fleet included four aerial fire trucks, six fire towers and five fire tenders.

title: PM Shehbaz seeks greater investment in Pakistan from global financial giants
author: BR Web Desk
description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday sought greater investment in Pakistan from leading global financial institutions during a series of meetings with senior executives of Barclays, J.P. Morgan, Citi, BlackRock and Rothschild & Co in London, his office said. The meetings focused on Pakistan’s economic reform programme, investment opportunities, capital markets, trade finance and the expansion of financial services, according to the Prime Minister’s Office. During his meeting with Mohammad Kamal Syed, Head of Private Bank and Wealth Management UK at Barclays, the prime minister highlighted the government’s macroeconomic stabilisation measures and encouraged the bank to explore opportunities in Pakistan’s financial sector. In talks with a J.P. Morgan delegation led by Matthieu Wiltz, Co-CEO for EMEA, Shehbaz discussed greater cooperation in capital markets, trade finance and investment banking. The delegation reaffirmed its interest in Pakistan’s sovereign debt capital markets and corporate banking opportunities. The prime minister also met senior Citi officials led by Chief Client Officer David Livingstone and encouraged the bank to expand its corporate and institutional banking services in Pakistan. During a meeting with BlackRock representatives Gordon Fraser and Sam Vecht, Co-Heads of Emerging Markets and Frontiers, and Portfolio Manager and Research Analyst Emily Fletcher, Shehbaz invited the investment firm to increase allocations to Pakistani equities and fixed-income instruments under its frontier markets strategy. Both sides also highlighted the importance of policy consistency in strengthening investor confidence. In his meeting with Rothschild & Co representatives Lord Mark Sedwill, Chair of Geostrategic Advisory, and Majid Ishaq, Head of UK Investment Banking, the prime minister discussed Pakistan’s geo-economic priorities and potential advisory cooperation in capital markets and investment strategy. The executives of the financial institutions expressed confidence in Pakistan’s economic reform momentum and reaffirmed their commitment to deepening engagement with the country’s financial sector, according to the PM Office. The meetings form part of the government’s efforts to strengthen international investor confidence and attract sustained capital flows into Pakistan. Finance Minister Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb and Adviser to the Prime Minister on Privatisation and Chairman of the Privatisation Commission Muhammad Ali also attended the meetings.

title: Karachi mayor says FWO, CBC working with Sindh govt on road and water projects in DHA
author: News Desk
description: Murtaza Wahab says one intervention to ease commute for those travelling to Phase 7, 8; announces 10m-gallon water line for Lyari.
text: Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab on Tuesday said the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) and the Cantonment Board Clifton (CBC) were collaborating with the Sindh government on road and water projects in Defence Housing Authority (DHA). These schemes were floated by the mayor during an interactive meeting with DHA residents on Saturday, where he promised to build a water pipeline from Dummlottee to Masjid-i-Ayesha on the edge of DHA phases 6 and 7. Speaking at an event in the city, Wahab said CBC would partner with the provincial government and the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC), so water could be delivered “directly to people’s homes” in DHA. The mayor noted that CBC had been “very forthcoming” when approached about the project and extended gratitude to the board for its assistance. Mentioning FWO chief Brigadier (retd) Adnan Akhtar Ali, Wahab said that although the project timeline was 18 months, authorities expected it to be finished within 12 months — by next September or October — so DHA residents could receive 10 million gallons of water daily. In another piece of “good news” for Karachiites, the mayor announced that the FWO and Sindh government were collaborating on a series of road projects to alleviate the issue of traffic congestion. “There is an intervention at the intersection of Khayaban-i-Ittehad and Khayaban-i-Hafiz in the form of an underpass or a flyover,” Wahab said. “Those travelling to Khayaban-i-Ittehad, [DHA] Phase 8 and Phase 7 will receive great relief,” he asserted. “The Sindh chief minister and Sindh cabinet have given their approval, and we are working on the finality, then we will initiate the project.” Wahab added that the FWO and the provincial government were also working on another flyover at the intersection of Khayaban-i-Shahbaz and Khayaban-i-Hafiz. “The government has given its permission and approval and funding has been allocated. Once things are finalised, we will execute the contract and work on the ground to remove the traffic bottleneck for DHA residents,” the mayor elaborated. He further said that to address traffic congestion on Khaliquz Zaman Road — namely from the Lily Bridge signal to the Bacha Party intersection — the local government would build a flyover, with the design to be finalised next week. “Once it is approved, procurement will begin immediately so that the entire stretch from [II] Chundrigar Road to Creek Club to Khayaban-i-Ittehad will be one thoroughfare, and you will be successful in avoiding signals,” he added. The Karachi mayor also announced that a 10-million-gallon elevated water line for Lyari promised by the PPP would be completed by Oct 20, and that Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari “will tell you more on that”. Touching on Shahrah-i-Bhutto , Wahab noted that the road benefited citizens and cut down traffic congestion, but acknowledged that motorists at Qayyumabad could face heavy traffic in one direction towards DHA. “I am grateful to the Sindh CM and the Sindh local government minister for approving another intervention, under which Shahrah-i-Bhutto will be extended towards Ayesha Manzil,” he announced. “From where we are standing, there will be connectivity to the expressway and people can avoid the Qayyumabad and Baloch Colony Expressway — and the Defence police station shortcut — and come straight onto the expressway,” Wahab added. The mayor said: “We have always reached out to people, so let’s sit together to solve these issues. Finally, a process of engagement is starting where every institution is conversing and coming together to provide the people of Karachi with long-term relief.” Earlier this month, KWSC and FWO signed an agreement to complete the laying of a dedicated pipeline from Dumlottee within 12 months to ease the chronic water problem in the salubrious vicinities of the city. Karachi’s residents have faced water shortages for years, with residents resorting to getting water from tankers. Earlier this month, a power breakdown at the Dhabeji pumping station, the city’s primary water intake point, left part of the city without water, KWSC said. Similarly, on July 27, the city faced a shortfall of 48m gallons of water following a breakdown at Dhabeji, affecting areas including parts of North Nazimabad, Nazimabad, Gulberg Town, New Karachi, Landhi, Korangi and Scheme 33.

title: Iraqi Airways to resume Iran flights in October after securing 'special exemption'
author: Reuters
description: BAGHDAD: Iraqi Airways is preparing to resume flights to Iran in October, Iraq’s transport ministry said on Tuesday, following a suspension of flights amid US sanctions restricting services to Iranian airlines. The ministry said Iraq had secured a special exemption allowing Iraqi Airways to operate services to Iran. Iraq halted flights to and from Iran on Friday in line with US sanctions, and the government had sought exemptions for travel related to pilgrimage, medical treatment and education. The transport ministry said services next month would initially operate from the Shi’ite holy city of Najaf once regulatory and technical requirements were completed. A source in the Iraqi transport ministry said the exemption was provided by the US Treasury and would run for one month. The number of allowed flights has not yet been determined, the source said. Three Iraqi airports suspend Iranian flights starting Friday, sources and state media say The announcement comes after Reuters reported on Monday that the Trump administration was set to grant a one-month US Treasury waiver allowing Iraqi Airways to fly between Iran and Najaf, with a more permanent exemption potentially following. Baghdad had offered safeguards including passenger screening and information sharing, as well as measures to prevent the flights being used to transport weapons, sanctioned individuals or illicit money, a source with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

title: Sri Lankan shares fall as real estate, utilities stocks weigh
author: Reuters
description: Sri Lankan shares closed lower on Tuesday, hurt by broad-based losses led by real estate and utilities stocks. The CSE All Share index settled down 0.60% at 20,817.82. York Arcade Holdings Plc and Serendib Land Plc were the top percentage losers on the CSE All Share index, falling 22.5% and 19.9%, respectively. Trading volume on the CSE All Share index rose to 69.6 million shares from 32.1 million in the previous session. The equity market’s turnover rose to 1.01 billion Sri Lankan rupees ($3.05 million) from 596 million rupees in the previous session, according to exchange data. Foreign investors were net buyers, purchasing stocks worth 25.7 million rupees, while domestic investors were net sellers, selling shares worth 1.00 billion rupees, the data showed.

title: The pioneer behind Pakistan's new era of automotive experiences
author: Press Release
description: Pakistan’s automotive industry doesn’t look like it did two years ago. New global brands have arrived. Electric mobility has gone from novelty to momentum. And as audiences become more discerning, they no longer show up just to see a car. They show up to experience what the brand stands for. That shift has turned launches into theatre. Product unveilings have become immersive brand experiences, built to engage, educate, and inspire. Few people have shaped that transformation as decisively as Hasan Daudpota, Founder & CEO of Keys Productions, an experience design agency shaping some of the country’s most talked-about live events. As the creative force behind some of Pakistan’s most prominent automotive launches, Hasan has helped rewrite the rules of how brands meet their audiences, through experience design, technology, and storytelling working in concert. As Pakistan’s auto sector expanded, Keys brought a new level of ambition to the category, creating automotive experiences designed to meet global standards while being built for the Pakistani audience. “Consumers today don’t just want to see a vehicle; they want to experience what the brand stands for,” he says. “The role of experiential design is to create that emotional connection before someone even gets behind the wheel.” The résumé backs up the philosophy. Over the past two years, Hasan and Keys Productions have delivered a run of high-profile automotive experiences, among them the Toyota Fortuner launch, Toyota Revo launch, Toyota Yaris launch, Dewan Shahzore launch, BYD Pakistan launch, BYD Shark 6 launch, Suzuki Every launch, BYD Atto 2 & Sealion 7 launch, Suzuki Fronx launch, BYD Sealion 6 launch, Kia Stonic launch, Master Deepal launch, and Chery Tiggo launch, alongside a steady stream of test drive events, customer engagement activations, plant events, and other brand collaborations. That range extends well beyond automotive. Keys Productions has also been behind some of the country’s biggest cuisine shows, award shows, corporate events, and music festivals, proof that the same rigor in design, technology, and storytelling travels across industries, not just cars. The defining moment came in 2024, with the BYD Pakistan launch, when BYD Global and its Pakistan partners chose to trust Keys Productions over the international options recommended by headquarters. That launch disrupted auto marketing in Pakistan entirely, proving that a global-standard experience could be built and executed locally. It didn’t go unnoticed: every major car brand studied it, and agencies across the industry began reaching out to understand how it was done. Across this body of work, what sets Hasan apart is a conviction that technology is a means, not a spectacle. He was making that argument before “experiential marketing” became an industry catchphrase, pushing for an integrated approach that fused design, innovation, storytelling, and human behavior into moments people actually remember. “Technology is most powerful when it enhances the experience without becoming the experience itself,” he says. That discipline has made Keys Productions one of the country’s leading experiential agencies, and put it at the center of a wider conversation about where experience design in Pakistan is headed. The journey hit an international marker in 2026, when Hasan led Keys Productions to become the first independent private Pakistani agency to represent itself at the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity. It was a milestone for the company, but also a statement for the industry: Pakistani creative talent can compete and win attention on a global stage. Hasan’s work has also taken him beyond Pakistan’s borders. He has previously spoken and presented at platforms including Burning Man, TED, the World Bank, and the World Business Dialogue, experiences that have shaped his approach to storytelling and design on home ground. Today, as automotive brands compete as much on experience as on product, Hasan Daudpota is among those defining what that competition looks like. His work points to something larger than any single launch: a Pakistan where creativity and experience design aren’t just locally admired but globally recognized. As the industry evolves, Hasan and Keys Productions aren’t chasing global trends, they’re helping set them.

title: Bangladesh eyes Airbus deal for 10 aircraft after Boeing order
author: Reuters
description: DHAKA: Bangladesh is looking to buy 10 aircraft from France’s Airbus for Biman Bangladesh Airlines, a minister said on Tuesday, as the government pushes ahead with plans to expand the national carrier’s fleet days after signing a deal for 11 additional Boeing jets. The government could sign an agreement with Airbus as early as October, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M. Rashiduzzaman Millat said. The proposed purchase includes four A350-900 wide-body aircraft and six A321neo narrow-body jets. Bangladesh to buy 11 more Boeing jets as it seeks closer US trade ties The proposed Airbus acquisition would add to Biman’s Boeing commitments, which now total 25 aircraft, including the latest order for five 787-10 Dreamliners and six 737-8 MAX jets. The planned A350s would mainly operate high-demand routes to the Middle East and long-haul services to Europe and North America, while the A321neos would be deployed on regional and shorter-haul routes. Biman, whose fleet of 19 aircraft consists mainly of Boeing jets and Dash-8 turboprops, serves slightly more than 20% of the country’s air passengers, according to Millat.

title: Tata leadership transition, IPO unlikely to impact ratings, S&P Global says
author: Reuters
description: Potential leadership transition and listing of Tata Sons would not immediately affect the ratings of the companies in the salt-to-software conglomerate, S&P Global said on Tuesday, saying that changes to the financial policies are likely to be gradual. The comments by the ratings agency come amid a deepening boardroom rift at India’s Tata group, with controlling charities at odds with management over the reappointment of Chairman N Chandrasekaran and the response to a listing mandate for the holding company. Tata Trusts have proposed a restructuring that could help Tata Sons avoid a listing after the central bank rejected the company’s request to surrender its status as a large non-bank finance company. Investors are closely tracking developments as a potential listing could unlock value for shareholders of group companies that have stakes in the unlisted parent. S&P said the group’s rated companies are run by independent professional management teams, although Tata Sons continued to influence strategy. Tata Group firms shed $4 billion in market value amid holding company rift S&P currently rates Tata Steel, Tata Motors, Tata Power, Tata Power Renewable Energy and Tata Capital at “BBB” with a stable outlook, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles has a “BBB” rating with a negative outlook. Jaguar Land Rover is rated “BBB-” with a negative outlook. A routine listing of Tata Sons would be credit-neutral in the near term, the ratings agency said. However, over the longer term, public shareholding could lead to greater scrutiny of capital allocation, shareholder returns and support for weaker group companies, potentially affecting its assessment of group support, S&P said.

title: Copper steadies as mine strike threat offsets dollar, oil strength
author: Reuters
description: Copper steadied on Tuesday as the prospect of a mining strike in top producer Chile offset concerns that a strong dollar and elevated oil prices will hurt demand. Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 0.2% to $14,447 per metric ton in official open outcry activity. It lost 1.4% on Monday, hitting its lowest since September 17 on weak Chinese industrial profits data. Despite signs of deteriorating economic growth due to the Iran war and oil above $100 a barrel, copper still has some upside risk, said Panmure Liberum analyst Tom Price. “And that’s really because the global market has been starved of inventory because it continues to be transferred into the US,” Price said, adding that underperforming production in Chile was a secondary driver. LME copper stocks dipped by 875 tons to 251,350 tons, although only around half are available to the market. In the US, COMEX inventories have risen for six straight days to over 700,000 metric tons for the first time as the possibility of an import tariff next year remains. In Chile, workers at two unions at Antofagasta’s Centinela copper mine rejected a collective contract offer on Monday, paving the way for a strike. Meanwhile, one of the unions at the giant Escondida mine last week rejected BHP’s attempt to delay contract talks. The dollar tested several-month highs on Tuesday, making greenback-denominated metals more expensive for investors using other currencies. Markets were pricing in more than a 70% chance of another Federal Reserve rate increase in October, which would be negative for base metals. Traders are also awaiting manufacturing purchasing managers’ data in China this week for further demand signals. Restocking ahead of the country’s week-long National Day holiday from Thursday has largely been completed, analysts at Galaxy Futures said. Aluminium fell 0.6% to $3,231 a ton, zinc gained 0.5% to $3,870, lead edged up 0.2% to $1,906, nickel shed 0.7% to $16,065, touching its lowest since September 16, and tin added 0.4% to $54,025.
