title: Most Gulf equities end lower amid cautious response to renewed US-Iran talks
author: Reuters
description: Most Gulf markets ended lower on Tuesday as investors weighed renewed diplomatic efforts to end the conflict between the United States and Iran. US and Iranian officials held separate talks with mediators on Monday, officials from both countries said, in a renewed push to end the war. Any further negotiations are expected to centre on an amended version of the seven-day proposal Iran presented last week on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, according to an official briefed on the talks. Saudi Arabia’s benchmark index declined 1.2%, dragged lower by a 1.4% decline in oil giant Saudi Aramco. Meanwhile, the kingdom has resumed oil loadings from its Red Sea port of Yanbu after restoring operations on the East-West Pipeline, trade sources and shipping data showed, bolstering prospects for Middle Eastern crude exports. Regional uncertainty continued to weigh on investor sentiment. Although US-Iran talks are being conducted through mediators, the absence of a clear diplomatic timetable and limited evidence of tangible progress have kept investors cautious, said Joseph Dahrieh, managing director at Tickmill. At the same time, subdued shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and persistent maritime disruptions continue to heighten market concerns, Dahrieh added. Qatar’s benchmark retreated 1.1%, with Qatar National Bank , the Gulf’s largest lender, losing 1%. Sentiment was also clouded by continued disruption to LNG flows. QatarEnergy has extended force majeure notices and will be unable to deliver liquefied natural gas cargoes to Italian utility Edison and certain Asian customers, while the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, Edison and trading sources said on Monday. Dubai’s main share index fell 0.2%, hit by a 1.6% slide in toll operator Salik Co . In Abu Dhabi, the index was down 0.3%. Outside the Gulf, Egypt’s blue-chip index lost 0.3%. title: PPP 'welcomes' opposition's invite to multiparty moot, says will forward it to Bilawal to consider
author: Ikram Junaidi
description: TTAP spokesperson says the JI and ANP will also be invited to the multiparty conference, which will be held after PTI's Oct 4 protest.
text: ISLAMABAD: Opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Tuesday invited the PPP, a key ally of the ruling PML-N in the Centre, to attend a multiparty conference that is being planned by the opposition. For its part, the PPP said it “welcomes the move” and would forward the invitation to the party’s chairperson, Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. The TTAP would then be informed of his stance. The development was confirmed in separate but similar statements by the two sides. The opposition had first announced its intention to hold a multiparty moot on Sept 11, with the PTI leading the initiative. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan had outlined plans to hold the conference, saying that “the current law and order situation, the economy, inflation, lawlessness, and the creation of new provinces issue” called for such measures. His statement to the media came after a meeting with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) leaders, who have agreed to attend the opposition’s moot. A delegation of the TTAP, led by Barrister Gohar, called on PPP Secretary General Nayyar Hussain Bukhari at the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad and formally invited his party to the moot as well, statements by the two sides said. The delegation also included Leader of Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Senator Zeeshan Akhunzada and TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai. The TTAP delegation briefed Bukhari on the objectives and purpose of the planned multiparty conference, the statements said. They also discussed the political situation in the country, supremacy of the Constitution, strengthening of democratic institutions, contacts between political parties and other matters. The statements quoted Bukhari as saying that the PPP considered “engagement and consultation with political parties on constitutional and democratic matters important”. Speaking to Dawn after the meeting, TTAP spokesperson Yousafzai said the multiparty conference would be held after PTI’s protest, which is scheduled for Oct 4 to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. “We have started a meeting with the representatives of political parties so that the date and venue for the moot is finalised,” he said, adding that since the PPP had taken a clear stance over the creation of new provinces, the opposition had decided to invite it as well. In the recent past, the proposal for the creation of new administrative units was first floated by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in July. The proposition drew strong reactions from government ministers, while the country’s leading lawyers’ bodies adopted divergent positions . The PPP, which rules Sindh, has strongly opposed any division of the province and maintains that any decision to create new provinces must be taken through the constitutional and parliamentary process and with political consensus. Meanwhile, the relationship between the PPP and the PML-N had also been strained lately during acrimonious election campaigns in Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan . The TTAP also plans invite other parties to the opposition’s moot. Yousafzai said Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI), Awami National Party (ANP) and Jamaat-i-Islami would also be invited to the moot, but the ruling PML-N and its ally in the Centre, Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan, would not be extended an invitation. Barrister Gohar also spoke to the media after the meeting with Bukhari. He said the role of political parties was important for the “strength of democracy”. “Democracy becomes strong when public’s voice is valued … and their mandate is valued,” he noted. Gohar added that coordinated efforts were required from all political parties, such that they could have a “one-point agenda” on matters such as a “free election commission, provincial autonomy or other discussions about the provinces”. He expressed his hope for a positive response from the PPP on the invitation for the multi-party conference. The TTAP has also formed a six-member committee to hold consultations with political parties and reach an agreement on the agenda for the proposed MPC.

title: Red Bull wins India court reprieve to use 'energy drink' label
author: Reuters
description: NEW DELHI: An Indian court on Tuesday quashed the food regulator’s order to stop Austrian beverage firm Red Bull using the label “energy drink” on its cans, saying the decision had been taken without allowing the company to explain its position. The decision will come as a major relief for Red Bull, but also Pepsi, Monster Beverage and billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance, which in private had all criticised India’s move, fearing the removal of the category label could damage their brands. The other companies did not take legal action. The regulator ordered makers of high-caffeine beverages sold as “energy drinks” to stop using the description in June, rejecting efforts to stall the move in a market expected to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028. Hearing the Red Bull challenge, the Delhi High Court on Tuesday set aside the order, saying it agreed with the company that the regulator took the decision “without affording any opportunity” to the company to provide its views. Red Bull sues Indian regulator over ‘energy drink’ label ban The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India will appeal against the court’s decision on public health grounds, a government official with direct knowledge of the plans told Reuters on condition of anonymity. The regulator did not respond to requests for comment. Red Bull’s India unit had argued the prohibition of the label “introduces substantial regulatory uncertainty and adversely affects” its existing and planned commercial investments. “Abrupt prohibition” Energy drinks have sparked health concerns among regulators in several countries around the world who worry they contain significant amounts of caffeine, sugar and taurine, an amino acid, which research suggests can contribute to health problems including high blood pressure and heart problems. They will be banned for under-16s in England from April next year. The energy drink market in India boomed after Pepsi launched Sting in 2017, with its 20-rupee ($0.21) plastic bottles proving popular among 15- to 19-year-olds and in rural areas, according to consumer research firm Euromonitor. India tightens proposed food warning labels in setback to industry In its court filing, Red Bull argued India’s decision was against the country’s stated policy to facilitate “international trade, promote investment and provide greater certainty to businesses,” as the “abrupt prohibition” of the descriptor was issued without any change to the underlying product standard.

title: India's SP Group arm taps dollar debt to meet another unit's dues
author: Reuters
description: MUMBAI: An unit of India’s Shapoorji Pallonji Group, Mercury Finance, is raising $125 million through the reissue of a U.S. dollar bond maturing in nearly three years, three sources aware of the matter said on Tuesday. Mercury Finance will raise the funds by reopening its zero-coupon dollar bonds due July 2029, with the company retaining the right to redeem them after one year, the sources said. The real estate conglomerate plans to use the proceeds to invest in rupee-denominated bonds to be issued later by a local group entity, they said. The dollar sale would be followed by another reissuance. The sources declined to be identified as they were not authorised to speak to the media. Shapoorji Pallonji Group did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. Eqyizen Investment, another SP group unit, will reissue a zero-coupon, rupee-denominated bonds maturing in July 2029. The firm had raised 213.50 billion rupees via the original issue at 18.95% yield in July. SP Group opens debut dollar debt issue after multiple delays, sources say The funds arising from this dollar-rupee fundraising deal will be used for meeting a payment obligation of Porteast Investment, another subsidiary, that is due to pay around 35 billion rupees for debt raised in May 2025, and the group has sought an extension to the deadline to October 31. “The current arrangement is a miniature version of what we saw in July, as the magnitude is much smaller,” one of the sources mentioned above said. In July, Mercury Finance raised $650 million, which was invested in rupee debt sold by Eqyizen Investment, whose bonds are secured by SP Group’s stake in Tata Sons, held through Cyrus Investments. The outlook for SP Group’s debt has improved after Tata Trusts, Tata Sons’ controlling shareholder, said earlier this month that SP Group had proposed selling 250 billion rupees worth of its stake.

title: Pakistan clinch eSports bronze at Asian Games
author: BR Web Desk
description: Pakistan won a bronze medal in the battle royale eSports competition at the Asian Games in Nagoya on Tuesday, taking the country’s medal tally at the event to five, the Pakistan Olympic Association said. Thailand secured the gold medal and China finished with silver after the 12-match competition at Aichi Sky Expo Hall D. Pakistan’s bronze-winning eSports lineup featured Mohammad Huzaifa, Shayan Asad, Falak Sher Memon, Hasnain Rahman and Syed Sameer. The latest medal adds to Pakistan’s bronze-medal haul in women’s cricket, MMA through Asim Khan, and squash through Noor Zaman and Ashab Irfan. Pakistan’s men’s cricket and hockey teams have also advanced to the semifinals, keeping the country in contention for further medals. Meanwhile, Pakistan’s women’s squash team suffered a 3-0 defeat against South Korea in the team event. Hwayeong Eum opened the tie with an 11-2, 11-4, 11-7 victory over Mahnoor Ali in 18 minutes at Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena. Minggyeong Heo extended South Korea’s lead by beating Sana Bahadar 11-5, 11-5, 11-8, before Dami Kim completed the clean sweep with an 11-3, 11-8, 11-5 win over Mehwish Ali. Earlier, Mahnoor also suffered a 3-0 defeat against Macao’s Yeung Wai Leng in the women’s team Stage 1 round-robin competition. Yeung won 11-9, 11-3, 12-10 in a 25-minute match.

title: Pakistan reports ongoing year's fifth polio case
author: Ikram Junaidi
description: Case reported from Bannu, where four of this year's five cases have been detected.
text: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan reported its fifth polio case of the ongoing year on Tuesday, with the virus affecting a 17-month-old girl in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bannu Division. The affected girl is from the Khandar Khankhel union council of Domel tehsil in the Bannu district, a National Emergency Operations Centre official told Dawn. He added that four of this year’s five cases in the country had been detected in the Bannu division and three among them were from the Bannu district. The development was also confirmed on the website of Pakistan’s polio eradication programme. The statement on the website said vaccination had reduced polio cases by 99.8 per cent, from an estimated 20,000 cases in the early 1990s to and five so far this year, but transmission remained persistent in southern KP. “This new case underscores the urgent need to maintain strong surveillance and vaccination efforts nationwide, because no child will be safe from polio until every child is vaccinated and safe,” it said. With four cases detected in KP and one Sindh in the ongoing year so far, the tally remains considerably lower than 31 cases recorded in 2025 and 74 in 2024. Officials expect a significant decrease in the 2026 polio tally compared to the past two years. Officials attribute the drop to improved vaccination campaign performa­n­­ce and the onset of winter, which is said to be as a low-transmission season because the virus becomes largely dormant in cold temperatures. “The ongoing calendar year has proved to be much better in terms of performance. More­over, as we have entered into the low-transmission season, there are fewer chances of polio cases,” Anwarul Haq, head of the Pakistan Polio Programme, told Dawn after the conclusion of the latest polio vaccination campaign in the country.* The weeklong sub-national polio campaign concluded on Sept 27, and more than 28.2 million children were vaccinated during the drive. But, severe security challenges threaten eradication efforts in the northwest, and the Bannu district remains a critical vulnerability. “There are severe security-related issues in Bannu where not only polio campaigns are stopped, but at times polio team workers are also kidnapped,” a polio expert earlier pointed out to Dawn . “There is a need to address the security-related issues in Bannu because it is the only place from where the polio virus can bounce back.” Data released by Pakistan’s Polio Eradication Programme showed that a majority of the environmental samples for poliovirus collected during the first two months of 2026 had tested negative. Moreover, a comparison of the first two months of 2025 with the current year shows a more than threefold reduction in positive environmental samples. However, it had warned that the ongoing Pakistan-Afghanistan tensions could create an opportunity for the virus to rebound during the upcoming high-transmission season. title: OGDCL inks deal with PINSTECH for lithium exploration
author: BR Web Desk
description: Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL), Pakistan’s largest exploration and production (E&P) company, has signed a contract with the Pakistan Institute of Nuclear Science and Technology (PINSTECH) for the hiring of advanced Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP) Element Profiling and Radioactive Element Profiling services. The signing ceremony was held in Islamabad and was attended by MD/CEO OGDC Ahmed Hayat Lak, senior management of OGDC, and representatives of PAEC and PINSTECH; the E&P shared it via a social media post on Tuesday. Under the agreement, PINSTECH will carry out ICP-based elemental profiling of produced water and brine from candidate OGDC wells, quantifying lithium, rare earth elements, precious metals and radioactive elements. More than 2,000 samples will be collected from candidate wells for the presence of lithium and other rare and critical earth metals, the company said. The exercise will build a comprehensive geochemical database of OGDC’s produced water, rank wells by lithium and rare earth content, and map areas of high to low concentration, providing the technical basis for evaluating the feasibility of Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE). OGDCL posts highest-ever annual profit, dividend OGDCL said that the expanded profiling effort is aimed at turning produced water, long treated as a waste stream from oil and gas operations, into a potential source of critical minerals. “The agreement comes as OGDC expands its diversification beyond conventional hydrocarbons into minerals and new energy resources, including lithium and rare earths recovered from produced water and geothermal brines,” read the statement. OGDCL said that the Wahid Bukhsh-01 well, its pilot well, has already identified geothermal brine containing 291 mg/L of lithium, a concentration comparable to leading geothermal-lithium brines internationally. OGDCL was established by an Ordinance on September 20, 1961, and is recognised for its operations including exploration, drilling, production, reservoir management, and engineering support. The company is pursuing diversification initiatives, including a 25% equity participation in the Reko Diq copper-gold project, progress on the Abu Dhabi Offshore Block-5, and steps towards shale gas and tight gas development.

title: India's Sun Pharma plans $1 billion local debt sale for loan takeout, sources say
author: Reuters
description: MUMBAI: India’s Sun Pharmaceutical Industries is planning to raise around 100 billion rupees ($1.04 billion) via a rupee-denominated debt sale to partly fund a bridge loan it took to acquire US healthcare firm Organon & Co., three sources said on Tuesday. Bridge loans are typically short-term loans taken before acquisitions to provide financing for the deal, which can later be replaced with more permanent funding via bonds or loans. The country’s largest drugmaker by market capitalization closed a syndication of a near-$12 billion, 18-month bridge loan earlier this year for Organon’s acquisition. The syndication also included State Bank of India, the country’s largest lender by assets, the sources said. The sources requested anonymity as they are not authorized to speak to media. Sun Pharma did not immediately respond to a Reuters email seeking comment. Bankers expect total domestic corporate debt issuances this year to hit a record as higher US yields make dollar funding costlier, pushing companies to explore funding within the domestic market, one of the sources said. India’s top drugmaker Sun Pharma beats profit view on strong domestic demand The 10-year US yield is hovering at its highest level since mid-June 2007, which has put pressure on global borrowing costs. Sun Pharma will sell shorter-duration bonds with maturities of two, three and four years, the sources said. The move comes as Indian companies have been trying to lock in borrowing costs ahead of a potential rate hike by the Reserve Bank of India, with about $3 billion worth of rupee debt issuances lined up over the next few days.

title: Indian rupee ends nearly flat as traders remain glued to oil moves, RBI caps fall
author: Reuters
description: MUMBAI: The Indian rupee closed nearly unchanged on Tuesday after hitting a two-month low earlier in the session as crude oil prices continued to dictate the currency’s momentum while likely central bank intervention limited weakness. The Indian rupee had declined 0.2% to 96.1475 in early trading but trimmed losses to close nearly flat at 95.98 as Brent oil prices turned lower on the day, after touching a peak of nearly $108 per barrel. India imports nearly 90% of its crude requirements, making the rupee one of the world’s most vulnerable currencies to the Middle East oil shock. Dollar sales by state-run banks, most likely on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India, helped limit the local currency’s fall early in the day and sentiment improved when crude prices cooled, traders said. The focus is squarely on oil and a break below $100 per barrel would take the rupee to 95.40-50 per dollar while current levels should keep it closer to 96, a trader at a foreign bank said. US and Iranian officials spoke separately with mediators on Monday as part of a renewed effort to end seven months of war, according to officials of both countries. Over the weekend, US President Donald Trump had said that he had rejected a peace proposal from Iran. The uncertainty has kept oil prices and US Treasury yields elevated, boosting the dollar. On the day, the US 10-year Treasury yield was a touch higher at 5.246% while the dollar index ticked up 0.3% to 101.5. “We need to see some stability in bonds for the dollar to correct lower. That relies heavily on oil, and the latest news isn’t encouraging. Upside risks are rising again for the greenback,” analysts at ING said in a note. Investor attention will also be on key US economic data this week, including job openings data due later on Tuesday, in addition to remarks from a number of Fed policymakers to gauge the future trajectory of interest rates in the world’s largest economy.

title: Indian shares extend losing run on elevated oil, bond yields
author: Reuters
description: Indian share benchmarks extended their losing run on Tuesday as the absence of a Middle East peace deal drove up oil prices and bond yields, stoking concerns about foreign investor outflows from the local market. The Nifty 50 lost 0.28% to 22,716.2 and BSE Sensex fell 0.33% to 72,529.07. The indicative closing level of the 50-stock index briefly slumped 2.5% during the closing auction session, amid volatility due to monthly expiry of derivatives contracts. The benchmark indexes have shed close to 2% so far in a holiday-shortened week, on top of a nearly 6% drop in the last seven weeks, one of their longest losing streaks on record. Brent crude futures hovered around $105 a barrel, while the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield spiked to a 19-year high above 5.27%. “Rising US Treasury yields have raised the risk-free return available to global investors, making the (premium) on offer in Indian equities relatively less compelling. This is prompting some foreign portfolio investors to shift capital out of India,” said Nitesh Arora, managing partner at Equirus Family Office. Foreign institutional investors sold Indian shares worth 53.53 billion rupees (about $558 million) on Monday, a four-week high. They have sold a net of $2.17 billion worth of shares in September so far, after two consecutive months of buying driven by the central bank’s measures to shore up dollar flows into the economy. The benchmark Nifty 50 index is down 5.7% so far in September, while MSCI’s broadest index for Asia Pacific stocks outside Japan is down about 1%. India’s under performance is primarily driven by its higher reliance on imported oil. Higher prices threaten to stoke inflation, widen the import bill and squeeze growth and corporate margins for world’s third-largest crude importer. Thirteen of the 16 major sectors logged losses on Tuesday. The broader small-caps and mid-caps dropped 0.8% and 1%. Heavyweight banks fell 0.4% and IT lost 1.5%. Most listed Tata group companies declined on the day, with Tata Chemicals dropping 4.5% and Tata Investment losing 2.9%, on dimming prospects of Tata Sons’ listing.

title: Nagoya organisers regret Pakistan and South Korea travel mix-ups
author: Reuters
description: NAGOYA: Organisers of the Aichi-Nagoya Games apologised for a travel mix-up on Monday, which saw Pakistan reaching a wrong venue ahead of their volleyball match against Uzbekistan, which eventually had to be delayed to salvage the situation. Pakistan captain Murad Jehan posted a video on Instagram to share what he called “another mismanagement” after they arrived at a wrong venue for a Pool A match. A Games spokesperson said the South Korean men’s team also missed their practice session after reaching a wrong venue. “Both teams boarded buses bound for the wrong destinations. We would like to offer our sincere apologies to both teams for the inconvenience this caused,” the spokesperson told reporters on Tuesday. Japan yet to catch Asian Games fever as Nagoya welcomes athletes “The Pakistan team was scheduled to head to Okazaki for their match, but their bus went toward Inuyama, where the practice venue is located. “The route was later corrected, and upon their arrival in Okazaki, the match was held after pushing back the start time. “While delaying the start time was undoubtedly a major inconvenience to the team, by adjusting the competition schedule, we were able to ensure that the match itself was conducted properly.” Pakistan brushed off the disruption and cruised to their second successive victory with a 3-0 win. The organisers had earlier apologised for the transportation and logistical issues that have plagued the Games.

title: Lahore court grants police 6-day remand of two suspects in Azeri woman's gang-rape case
author: Wajih Ahmad Sheikh
description: IO's request for 14-day remand denied; woman says suspects told her to drink alcohol and locked her in room.
text: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Tuesday allowed Defence C police a six-day physical remand of two suspects in a case against them over the alleged gang-rape of an Azeri woman. The 20-year-old Azerbaijan national had travelled to Pakistan for business purposes and was allegedly gang-raped by three men in a rented flat of a private housing society located near Raiwind on the night between Friday and Saturday. One of the prime suspects had been arrested on Monday, while another’s arrest surfaced on Tuesday. According to Lahore Deputy Inspector General (Investigation) Zeeshan Raza, police had identified the third suspect and were conducting raids to trace him. On Tuesday, the police produced the two arrested men before Magistrate Azhar Mahmood at Cantonment Courts. The investigating officer sought their 14-day physical remand for interrogation, collection of evidence and DNA examination. However, the magistrate approved a six-day physical remand of the suspects. Separately, a session’s court granted interim pre-arrest bail to a female suspect in the case, restraining police from arresting her till Oct 5. The Azeri woman had mentioned in her application to the police that two women had approached her for dinner and later they went to a cafe, where the three men accused of raping her had met them. One of the two women who allegedly approached the victim appeared before the court along with her lawyer on Tuesday. The lawyer argued that his client had been implicated in the case with mala fide intention. He said she wanted to join police investigation to prove her innocence. He further expressed fear that she would be arrested and requested the court to approve are pre-arrest bail. The court granted the suspect bail till Oct 5, with the directive to join the police investigation before the next hearing. The judicial proceedings came a day after the foreign woman recorded her statement before Judicial Magistrate Muhammad Sagheer under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC). Police Sub-Inspector Faryal Malik, the investigating officer, had produced the woman before the magistrate under strict security arrangements. In her statement, a copy of which is available with Dawn, the woman said she had arrived in Islamabad from Istanbul on Sept 13 and stayed in Faisalabad for five days before travelling to Lahore. “I had a plan to visit Skardu, but I could not go there because I was alone,” she said. According to her, on the day of the alleged incident, she messaged two women, asking them to meet her in Lahore. At around 11pm, she went to a cafe where she met one of them and later accompanied her to a house in Bahria Town to meet the other. The complainant told the magistrate that at around 2am, a white car arrived carrying two men, one of whom was sent on remand on Tuesday (first suspect). Later, they moved to an apartment where two more men arrived, one of whom was the second person sent on remand (second suspect), while she did not know the name of the other man. According to the complainant, in a separate room, one of the women took between Rs20,000 and Rs30,000 from the first suspect, saying the money was for a party, while the second woman also joined them. The Azeri woman said she made it clear that she “did not need money or alcohol”. She alleged that the first suspect tried to touch her and locked her in a separate room. When she asked about her friends, she was told that they had left. When she tried to leave, the complainant said she was told that she could not go because her friends had taken money. The victim said she offered to pay the men, but they told her that she would have to drink alcohol with them before they would let her go. She alleged that the three men raped her. She further stated that the suspects then put her in a car and threw her out at an unknown location, while threatening her with dire consequences if she approached the police. According to her statement, the suspects also took her handbag containing Rs200,000, an iPhone 13 Pro Max and another mobile phone. She then requested some people present there to help her call the police emergency number 15, following which the police arrived. The Defence C police had registered a case against three unidentified suspects on Sept 26 on the woman’s complaint. Police had also taken two close relatives and a domestic servant of one of the suspects into custody. The vehicle allegedly used in the incident had also been taken into custody. On Sunday, Lahore police had requested federal authorities to place the names of the three prime suspects in the case on the Provisional National Identification List (PNIL), saying they had fled Lahore shortly after the alleged assault. It is the second such case in which a foreign woman was reportedly gang-raped in the Defence C police station area during the last four months. In June, two foreign women, nationals of the Netherlands and Venezuela, were allegedly abducted and sexually assaulted in the Defence C police station area. According to the FIR, the women were abducted by five suspects, including a close relative of a senior political personality, who demanded ransom and subjected them to sexual assault during their captivity.

title: Pakistan rupee records gain against US dollar
author: Recorder Report
description: The Pakistani rupee extended its marginal gains against the US dollar, appreciating 0.01% in the interbank market on Tuesday. The local unit closed the day at 277.12, a gain of Re0.03 against the greenback. On Monday , the Pakistani rupee settled at 277.15 against the dollar. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb held a kick-off meeting with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission on Tuesday, read a statement released by the Ministry of Finance. “The IMF mission is in Islamabad for the fourth review of Pakistan’s Extended Fund Facility (EFF) arrangement and the third review of the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF),” it said. Internationally , the US dollar hovered near a two-month high on Tuesday as volatile oil prices and a rapid climb in Treasury yields lent support, although gains were limited as traders awaited US data this week for clues on the Federal Reserve’s rate path. The euro traded near its weakest level in three months at $1.1367 after the European Central Bank’s chief signalled measured steps to quell inflation. Sterling was steady at $1.3248, also not far from a three-month trough. The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of peers, was a touch higher at 101.2 and on track for a 1.8% advance this month, its best performance since June. Meanwhile, a deepening selloff in US Treasuries pushed yields to new peaks, with the 10-year benchmark at its highest since 2007 and the 30-year at its highest since 2004. The monetary policy-sensitive two-year yield also rose to its highest in more than two years, closing in on 5%. US data releases later in the week, including the PCE price index on Wednesday and nonfarm payrolls on Friday, are both expected to support the case for further Fed rate hikes. Markets are now seeing a more than 70% chance of a rate hike from the Federal Reserve at the end of October, up from 57% a week ago, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool. Oil prices , a key indicator of currency parity, declined on Tuesday as investors focused on signs of recovering crude exports from the Middle East and lingering concerns over potential supply disruptions in the region stemming from the US-Israeli war on Iran. Brent crude futures were down $1.96, or 1.86%, to $103.32 a barrel at 1306 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $90.65, down $1.95, or 2.11%. title: Three debt instruments worth Rs27.8bn listed on PSX in 1QFY27

description: Three new debt instruments worth Rs27.8 billion (approx. $100.34 million) were listed at the Pakistan Stock Exchange’s (PSX) debt market during the first quarter of FY26-27 across banking and corporate issuers. “Faysal Bank Limited listed Rs7 billion in Rated, Unsecured, Subordinated Sukuk (FABLSC); Bank Alfalah Limited listed Rs20 billion in Rated, Unsecured, Subordinated Tier-2 Term Finance Certificates (BAFLTFC9); and At-Tahur Limited listed Rs800 million in Rated, Secured Sukuk (PREMASTSC),” the PSX said in a notice on Tuesday. The Debt Capital Market involves borrowing money from investors for a specified period, with the issuer providing a payout at a fixed or floating percentage over the term. At maturity, the principal amount is repaid to the investor.

title: Afghan govt must move from ‘militant mindset’ to statesmanship: Tarar
author: BR Web Desk
description: Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Tuesday said the Afghan interim government needs to move from what he described as a “militant mindset” to a mindset of a statesman and a state for lasting peace and stability in the region. Addressing a gathering organised by the International Parliamentarians Congress (IPC), Tarar said Pakistan had repeatedly sought dialogue and negotiations with Afghanistan to achieve peaceful coexistence, but questioned whether there was sufficient will on the Afghan side to achieve peace. “The problem is that the mindset needs to be changed,” he said, adding that the Afghan interim government needed to move away from a militant mindset. Tarar said Pakistan and Afghanistan were neighbouring countries with longstanding links and that Pakistan had hosted around four million Afghan refugees over more than four decades. He said Pakistan had made several attempts to resolve outstanding issues through negotiations, with Pakistani delegations travelling to Afghanistan and talks being held in third countries, including recent meetings in Istanbul and Doha. According to Tarar, the main obstacles to peace included militancy and what Pakistan considers the presence of terrorist safe havens in Afghanistan. Pakistan has repeatedly criticised the Afghan authorities of allowing militant groups to operate from Afghan territory, while the Afghan Taliban authorities have rejected such allegations. Recent tensions between the two countries have also included cross-border attacks and Pakistani strikes inside Afghanistan. The minister said peace between the two countries could open opportunities for greater trade and regional connectivity, particularly by linking Central Asian states with Pakistani ports and warm-water routes through Afghanistan. He said Afghanistan had significant economic potential and argued that regional trade and investment could expand if peace and stability were established. Tarar also highlighted Afghanistan’s young population and raised concerns over restrictions affecting women’s participation in the workforce and access to basic rights, including education, assembly and association. “There is a disconnect between the Afghan interim government and sections of the Afghan population,” he said, adding that ordinary Afghans wanted peace, stability and economic prosperity. “Only peace can lead to prosperity,” Tarar said, adding that Afghanistan’s stability would benefit the wider region. He said Pakistan had continued to engage with Afghanistan through dialogue and negotiations despite security concerns. Tarar also warned that Pakistan’s desire for peace should not be interpreted as weakness, saying Islamabad had responded to attacks and would respond to any attempts to destabilise the country. “Pakistan’s desire for peace must not be misconstrued as its weakness,” he said, adding that Pakistan would continue to defend itself against attacks while pursuing peace. The minister said the people of Afghanistan deserved a more prosperous future and that they should have a voice in determining the country’s future.

title: 28 years of McDonald’s Pakistan: celebrating the local partners behind the golden arches
author: Press Release
description: To celebrate 28 years in Pakistan, McDonald’s shifted the spotlight away from the counter and onto the local craftspeople, farmers, and manufacturers who prepare the food behind the scenes. At an anniversary gathering held at the McDonald Etihad town in Lahore, the brand celebrated nearly three decades of service by honouring its domestic partners, including Big Bird, Nurpur, Packages Limited, Fresh & Freeze, Pronto Spaces, Saima Packaging and the Zaman Foundation. Rather than a routine corporate milestone, the event focused on the human craft and local industry behind every meal. From fresh milk supplied by local dairy farmers and poultry raised to strict bio-safety standards, to packaging engineered and printed in Lahore, the celebration highlighted the Pakistani hands behind the brand’s familiar taste. Over the last 28 years, close collaboration and technical training have enabled local partners to master international standards, ensuring that every meal is produced with domestic care and global precision. “This celebration is about the people who make our work possible every single day,” said a McDonald’s representative. The milestone served as a meaningful reminder that McDonald’s 28-year story in Pakistan is, at its heart, a story of Pakistani dedication and expertise.

title: 12 injured after school van catches fire in Murree
author: Muhammad Asghar
description: Injured persons include 10 students; Punjab CM seeks report on the incident, takes notice of "vehicle overloading".
text: ISLAMABAD: 12 people, including 10 school-going children, were injured after a school van veered off the road and caught fire in Murree on Tuesday. As per a statement from Murree police, the incident occurred near the Bara Hotar Link Road, where a Suzuki Bolan carrying school children veered off the road and caught fire. “Upon receiving news of the incident, police and rescue teams immediately arrived at the scene,” it said, adding that the children were rescued and rushed to the Tehsil Headquarters Hospital. According to an incident report issued by the THQ Hospital and a copy of which is available with Dawn, 12 individuals, including two adults and ten children aged five to 14, were brought to the hospital, with 10 of them having burns of varying degrees. Three of the children suffered severe burn injuries, with one sustaining burns to 42 per cent of the body, while the other two suffered burns to 38pc and 26pc, respectively, the report said. Murree police said the cause of the incident had not yet been ascertained and that necessary legal action would be taken. According to the statement, Murree District Police Officer Raza Tanveer Sipra visited the hospital to inquire after the injured children. “We are maintaining constant contact to ensure the provision of the best possible medical care to the injured children and treatment for those who have been referred,” DPO Sipra was quoted as saying. In an earlier statement, Rescue 1122 said that passengers, mostly schoolchildren, were safely evacuated from the vehicle and sustained only minor injuries. However, the vehicle was engulfed in flames. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz sought a report into the incident and took notice of the “vehicle overloading and lack of adequate fire safety measures”, state broadcaster PTV reported. Earlier this year, eight students were injured when a school van caught fire while moving along Karachi’s Shah Faisal Colony flyover. In February, a schoolgirl was killed , and six others were injured when their van was hit by a dumper in Okara. In March, two teenage sisters in Karachi died after suffering burn wounds when a fire erupted in their family van.

title: Blasphemy case: Prosecution asked to defend electronic evidence used for conviction
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
description: Defence alleged that the FIR was registered against Raza when a case for his abduction had been lodged in Lahore by his family.
text: LAHORE: A Lahore High Court (LHC) division bench on Monday sought arguments from the prosecution on the admissibility of electronic evidence relied upon by a Bahawalpur trial court to sentence a man to death in a blasphemy case. The bench comprising Justice Sadiq Mahmud Khurram and Justice Muhammad Jawad Zafar was hearing an appeal against sentence filed by Taimoor Raza through Advocate Asad Jamal. Previously, the appeal was pending at the Bahawalpur bench of the LHC. However, it was transferred to the principal seat on the request of the appellant counsel about a year ago. On Monday, Justice Khurram directed the prosecution to come up with its arguments on the questions raised in the appeal on the alleged contradiction in the evidence including electronic i.e. Facebook pages presented before the trial court. The appellant’s counsel requested the bench to adjourn the hearing for a short date. The bench is yet to announce the next date of hearing. The Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) of Bahawalpur had registered the FIR in 2016 under section 298A of Pakistan Penal Code, which criminalises the use of derogatory remarks, spoken or written words that defile the sacred names of holy personages, including the wives, family members, righteous Caliphs, or companions of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), and section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act 1997. However, an antiterrorism court had in 2017 sentenced Raza to death for offence under 295-C (the use of derogatory remarks against the Holy Prophet (PBUH) punishable by death or imprisonment for life). The defence alleged that the FIR was registered against Raza when a case for his abduction had been lodged in Lahore by his family. It alleged that Raza was abducted from his office where he worked as office assistant and taken to Bahawalpur and was roped in the case. The appeal argued that the trial court failed to refer to any evidence, which could form the basis of which the charge under section 295-C was made against the appellant. It said the prosecution procured an opinion from so-called religious scholars who never testified in the trial court and were never cross-examined. It argued that no independent witness was engaged or joined the investigation against the appellant. Published in Dawn, September 29th, 2026

title: Asian Games: Arshad Nadeem finishes fourth as Rumesh Pathirage strikes javelin gold in rainy Nagoya
author: Dawn Sport
description: The result caps a difficult season for Arshad, who has struggled to rediscover the form that saw him win Olympic gold in Paris with a record 92.97m throw.
text: Arshad Nadeem threw a season-best 80.29m but still finished fourth as Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Pathirage claimed javelin gold in a rain-soaked final at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Monday. The Olympic champion, competing under heavy skies and on a slick runway, had a difficult start, managing 76.69m on his first attempt before a foul on his second. He improved drastically on his third with 80.29m to climb to fourth, but could not build on it — three consecutive fouls followed, ending his challenge. Pathirage, the World No. 1 and heavy favourite, lived up to his billing. Third after three throws with 83.56m, he unleashed 88.33m on his fourth attempt, beating his chest in delight as he moved ahead of both Indians. He improved again in the sixth with 88.55m. The Sri Lankan’s dominance is all the more remarkable given the disruption to his season. Just two weeks before the Games, all five of his javelins — the same implements he used for every 90m throw this year — were found shattered after a flight from Budapest, where he had won the World Athletics Ultimate Championship. India’s Yashvir Singh took silver with a personal-best 85.72m on his final attempt, while compatriot Rohit Yadav claimed bronze with 84.35m. Yashvir had set the tone early with 83.56m on his first throw, before Rohit briefly moved ahead with 84.35m in the third round. Pakistan’s Mohammad Yasir finished ninth, his best effort 73.50m. The result caps a difficult season for Arshad, who has struggled to rediscover the form that saw him win Olympic gold in Paris with a record 92.97m throw. He finished ninth at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow and fifth at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest. Pathirage, by contrast, has been unstoppable. The 23-year-old has won 11 of his 12 competitions this year, thrown beyond 90m three times, and claimed the Diamond League Final, Commonwealth gold and the World Ultimate title.

title: Red Bull sues Indian regulator over 'energy drink' label ban
author: Reuters
description: NEW DELHI: Austrian beverage maker Red Bull has sued India’s food regulator for prohibiting the use of the “energy drink” descriptor without issuing any warning notice, which it claims is impacting its investments in India, its court filing showed. Red Bull is one of a number of globally recognized brands to have sued the Indian regulator in recent months amid an unprecedented food standards enforcement drive, which has included surprise raids and scrutiny over legal compliance impacting companies like Diageo. India in June ordered makers of high-caffeine beverages sold as “energy drinks” to stop using that description, rejecting efforts to stall the regulatory intervention in a market expected to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028. The move has triggered a standoff, as Pepsi, Red Bull, Monster Beverage and billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance fear removing the category label could damage brands built around instant-energy claims, Reuters has reported. India tightens proposed food warning labels in setback to industry In the first legal challenge against the move, Red Bull told the Delhi High Court on September 25 that legal processes were not followed in prohibiting use of the term “energy drinks”, which is globally recognized, according to the company’s filing seen by Reuters. ‘Against India’s policy’ Red Bull’s India unit said the “abrupt prohibition” of the descriptor, without any change to the underlying product standard, “introduces substantial regulatory uncertainty and adversely affects” its existing and planned commercial investments. The order is against India’s stated policy of facilitating “international trade, promote investment and provide greater certainty to businesses,” Red Bull said, adding that its “effect is to bring the petitioner’s entire business to a standstill”. A government source said the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India will defend its decision in court against Red Bull, saying the FSSAI historically never allowed the use of ‘energy drinks’ on the label. India wanted red flags on chip packets and soda. Big Food fought back India’s energy drinks retail sales are growing 12.6% annually, faster than in the US and China, Euromonitor estimates. The market in India boomed after Pepsi launched Sting in 2017, with its 20-rupee ($0.21) plastic bottles proving popular among 15- to 19-year-olds, Euromonitor says. Red Bull’s India revenue stood at $130 million in 2024, more than double the earnings recorded four years ago. Energy drinks have sparked health concerns among some regulators globally who worry they contain high caffeine, sugar and taurine, an amino acid. They will be banned for under-16s in England from April next year.

title: Aleema provided basic facilities, essential items in jail, Punjab govt tells LHC
author: Wajih Ahmad Sheikh
description: Aleema provided with a bedsheet, blanket, shoes, six suits, a towel and other essential items, according to the report.
text: LAHORE: The Punjab government on Monday told the Lahore High Court (LHC) that Aleema Khan, a sister of PTI founder Imran Khan, had been provided basic facilities and essential items in jail. Aleema was detained on Sep 20 after the Lahore deputy commissioner ordered her detention or arrest under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance. The detention has come amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party has postponed to Oct 4. The protest has been called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. Assistant Advocate General Farrukh Khan Lodhi submitted a report on behalf of the Kot Lakhpat jail superintendent during the hearing of a petition filed by Shahrez Khan, Aleema’s son. According to the report, Aleema had been provided with a bedsheet, blanket, shoes, six suits and a towel. She was also given face wash, a toothbrush, a skincare kit and a shawl, it added. In light of the government’s report, Justice Abher Gul Khan disposed of the petition. The judge also directed the home secretary to decide, in accordance with the law, on the petitioner’s request seeking permission to meet Aleema. At the last hearing on Sept 26, Barrister Taimur Malik had told the court that his client, Aleema, was facing difficulties in receiving her medicines and other essentials in jail. Aleema’s sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, have also been detained for 30 days ahead of the PTI’s protest and march to Islamabad. author: BR Web Desk
description: Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar has regretted that the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has neither taken practical steps against terrorism nor has the intention to do so. title: Irish players refuse handshakes, wear black armbands in Nation Leagues clash against Israel
author: Reuters | AFP
description: Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson says his team “raised awareness worldwide” about Gaza conflict; secures 3-0 win against Israel in Hungary.
text: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in a Nations League clash on Sunday amid an eerie and sombre atmosphere that saw the Irish players wear black armbands over the war in Gaza. Ireland’s players also bowed their heads as the Israeli national anthem was played at the near-empty Debrecen stadium in Hungary. The teams skipped the traditional pre-match handshakes and did not exchange pennants either. Troy Parrott made a heart sign with his hands after opening the scoring on 14 minutes, while Jack Moylan kissed the Irish badge on his jersey and his black armband after netting the third goal 25 minutes in. Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson said his team had “raised awareness worldwide” about the Gaza conflict after they chose not to shake hands with Israeli players. The game, in which Israel were the nominal hosts, had been in doubt earlier in the week until Ireland’s players voted overwhelmingly to fulfil the fixture, despite pressure from back home to boycott the match. Only one player, goalkeeper Gavin Buzunu, pulled out, saying “it would be wrong to participate” in either this match or the return fixture in Serbia on October 4 due to the “killing of innocent people”. “It has been so difficult for so many players,” Icelander Hallgrimsson told broadcaster RTE after the game. “I hope that will not be in the next game because they have shown support to the protest, they have raised awareness worldwide, not only in Ireland, on the subject and that is normally the reason for protesting, to raise awareness of a situation. “I think these players have done that with all their actions, with all that they have been saying. No more than Gavin Bazunu, but the others have done it here on the pitch and how they have shown their actions, so I hope people understand that.” Since Ireland were drawn in the same Nations League group as Israel in February, prominent Irish figures including sportspeople, fan groups and pro-Palestinian campaigners have protested against the matches going ahead. The Irish federation did not reserve any tickets for fans to attend the match and public broadcaster RTE was due to show it without commentary. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar accused Ireland of being “on the wrong side of history” over the players’ actions. In a lengthy post on X, Saar referenced the Irish team of 1939 giving the Nazi salute ahead of a match against Germany in Bremen. He also referred to Irish neutrality during the Second World War and the condolences offered by then-prime minister Eaemon de Valera to the German representative in Dublin following Adolf Hitler’s death. “Almost 90 years have passed. Ireland’s unique talent for finding itself on the wrong side of history remains intact,” he added. “Sports, soccer, basketball, everything is for the public, the people, and not for politics,” 31-year-old software development teacher Mol Michael, draped in an Israeli scarf, told AFP . “Once you decide, because of politics, to cancel the Irish audience, this is a really stupid move from Ireland, in my opinion.” Ireland has long been a strong supporter of the Palestinian cause, with sympathy often linked to the country’s own history of British rule. Dublin formally recognised a Palestinian state in 2024 alongside Spain and Norway, and has repeatedly criticised Israel over its relentless bombardment of Gaza.

title: Lahore ATC extends physical remand of PTI's Hammad Azhar for 7 days in Jinnah House attack case
author: Wajih Ahmad Sheikh
description: Govt lawyers inform LHC that Azhar's mother and wife have met him.
text: LAHORE: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Monday extended the physical remand of PTI leader Hammad Azhar for another seven days in the 2023 Jinnah House attack case . Sarwar Road police had booked several PTI leaders and workers on charges of attacking and vandalising the Jinnah House , which also serves as the residence of the corps commander, during the May 9, 2023 protests against the arrest of ex-premier Imran Khan. On Monday, police produced the former federal finance minister before ATC Judge Manzer Ali Gill upon the completion of his 21-day physical remand . During the hearing, a state prosecutor said police needed further remand to recover the suspect’s mobile phone and SIM, describing them as important pieces of evidence. He urged the court to extend the remand for a further seven days. Speaking before the court, Azhar questioned why further remand was being sought, saying he had already been kept on physical remand for 21 days in an alleged occurrence where he said he was not even present. “Even a murder suspect is sent on 14-day remand here. Has my offence become more serious than murder?” he asked. The former minister also complained that he had earlier not been allowed to meet his lawyers or family members — a concern also voiced earlier by his family before a court. The ATC then reserved its decision on the prosecution’s request for further remand, and later announced its decision, granting the police Azhar’s remand for another seven days. Separately, a two-member Lahore High Court (LHC) bench headed by Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi disposed of a petition filed by Azhar’s mother and wife against the alleged denial of access to him during police custody. A Lahore ATC had already disposed of a similar plea filed by the family, directing them to approach the police on the matter. A Punjab government lawyer informed the LHC bench that Azhar had been allowed to meet his mother and wife. The law officer further said that the PTI leader would also meet his lawyer at the trial court on Monday. Relying on the government lawyer’s statement, the bench disposed of the petition. According to his family , Azhar was arrested on Sept 5. However, police said the next day they were unaware of his arrest, prompting the PTI leader’s mother to approach the LHC on Sept 7, and he was produced before an ATC the same day. Azhar, the son of late former Punjab governor Mian Muhammad Azhar , has been declared a proclaimed offender by multiple anti-terrorism courts for not joining the proceedings against him in cases related to the May 9 riots . Azhar had reappeared in public on May 22, 2024, a year after he had gone into hiding when the state launched a crackdown against the party leadership following the violent incidents of May 9 . At the time, the PTI leader had evaded arrest when the Counter-Terrorism Department raided the party’s secretariat in Islamabad.

title: Palm oil falls for a second session on weak rival oils
author: Reuters
description: JAKARTA: Malaysian palm oil futures dropped for the second consecutive session on Monday, tracking rival vegetable oils on Chicago and Dalian exchanges, though stronger crude prices and a softer ringgit capped losses. The benchmark palm oil contract for December delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange fell 9 ringgit, or 0.19%, to 4,663 ringgit ($1,142.05) a metric ton at closing. The contract traded in a tight range between 4,642 ringgit and 4,720 ringgit, after dropping 4.61% last week. A Kuala Lumpur-based trader said the contract was supported by strong crude oil and a weaker ringgit —its currency of trade — “but weak Dalian and Chicago oils cap gains.” Dalian’s most-active soyoil contract fell 0.84%, while its palm oil contract lost 1.6%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade ticked down 0.24%. Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market. Brent crude rebounded more than 3% on Monday after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal from Iran to resolve their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock. The ringgit palm’s currency of trade, eased 0.25% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies. Palm oil may extend losses into a range of 4,588-4,622 ringgit per ton, as suggested by a projection analysis, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said. Exports of Malaysian palm oil products for September 1-25 likely fell between 15.1% and 24.3% from a month earlier, cargo surveyors Intertek Testing Services and AmSpec Agri Malaysia said. Indonesia’s palm oil exports in July stood at 3.19 million metric tons, down 9.87% from the same period of last year, palm oil association GAPKI said on Monday.

title: India's Aug industrial output jumps 8% as manufacturing output surges
author: Reuters
description: NEW DELHI: India’s industrial output grew at a stronger-than-expected pace of 8% in August, government data showed on Monday, boosted by a surge in manufacturing and electricity output even as mining output contracted. Economists polled by Reuters expected industrial output growth at 6.5% in August from a revised 7.4% a month earlier. “In a record performance, manfuacturing recorded growth of 8% or more in the last three consecutive months,” the statistics ministry said in an official statement. The government now uses producer prices for factory output calculation as against wholesale prices earlier, a change introduced earlier this year. Manufacturing output grew 9% year-on-year in August against a revised 8.2% in July. India’s July industrial output growth slows to 6.7% y/y as mining contracts Electricity generation rose 12.3% year-on-year in August against an increase of 8.7% a month earlier. Mining activity fell 5.6% year-on-year in August against a decline of 0.9% in July. Output of consumer durables, including cars and phones, grew 11.1% year-on-year in August against a revised 12% increase a month earlier. Output of consumer non-durables, such as food items and toiletries, rose 2.1% year-on-year in August against a revised fall of 0.8% in the previous month. Capital goods output rose 16.9% year-on-year in August against a revised 19% increase in July. Industrial output between April-August grew 6.7%, compared to an increase of 4.2% a year earlier.

title: Pakistan gets offers in 185,000 metric ton wheat tender, traders say
author: Reuters
description: HAMBURG: The lowest price offered in a tender from Pakistan to purchase and import 185,000 metric tons of wheat that closed on Monday was believed to be $339.36 a metric ton, cost and freight (c&f) included, European traders said in initial assessments. The offer was believed to have been submitted for around 60,000 tons by trading house Bunge, they said. The state agency Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) is still considering the offers and no purchase has been reported, traders said, adding a decision is expected in coming days. Reports reflect assessments from traders and further estimates of prices and volumes are still possible later. The tender comes at a difficult time for importers, with fighting bringing seaborne Black Sea exports of cheap Russian and Ukrainian wheat to a virtual stop with supplies from alternative origins more expensive. title: China, US agree tariff cuts on $60bn of goods including agriculture, household items
author: Reuters
description: BEIJING: China and the United States have agreed to cut tariffs imposed on $60 billion worth of goods imported from each other, on an array of products ranging from US corn to cosmetics, and from Chinese household appliances to toys. Under the US-China Board of Trade, both countries have each recommended $30 billion of trade in non-sensitive goods for more favourable tariff treatment, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement on Sunday. For the United States, that was “unlocking improved market access” for about 30% of US exports to China, he said. The reciprocal tariff reduction as well as an extension of a trade truce were among the key takeaways from the second summit this year between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, hosted in Washington last week. One of two lists from the White House showed that China planned to trim duties on a variety of US agricultural goods including corn, wheat, sorghum, meat, dairy, vegetable oils and meals. It did not include soybeans. Beijing will also look to reduce levies on US fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices. China says US trade truce extension creates space to advance talks In another list were Washington’s reciprocal tariff cuts for Chinese small appliances such as coffee makers and toasters, tableware, blankets and bed linens. The lists also included toys, fireworks, artificial flowers, Christmas tree lamps and other holiday decorations, and children’s car seats. Longer trade truce China’s commerce ministry said on Monday a two-month extension of a trade truce with the United States through to January 10 would provide room for both sides to evaluate their ongoing arrangement to resolve economic and trade issues, while considering how to advance on those fronts. The extension also provides a “relatively stable and predictable policy environment” for cooperation among companies and continued active discussions. Both sides will hold regular talks on potential investment opportunities and barriers, enhancing policy transparency and predictability, and responding to enterprises’ concerns, the ministry said. China, US agree to $30 billion tariff cut, AI dialogue during Xi visit Stocks fell sharply in China on Monday, with investors having few concrete details to cheer from the leaders’ summit and underlying tensions resurfacing. Technology stocks fell on a bipartisan US push to ban Chinese components from data centres and the benchmark blue-chip index .CSI300 slid more than 2% to a one-year low. Agriculture and coal China’s choice of products for tariff cuts looks designed to help Beijing meet what the White House says is a $17-billion commitment to buy agricultural goods. China has already resumed large-scale buying of US soybeans under a deal struck last year to buy 25 million metric tons annually. Both countries will set up an agriculture working group under a trade council, which will hold its first meeting before the year ends to discuss two-way market access and regulation, the commerce ministry said. The presidential summit also yielded an agreement for China to import 10 million metric tons of coal annually from the United States in 2027 and 2028, the White House release showed. That amount roughly equals 2% of China’s coal imports each year. China will also examine and approve foreign financial services institutions, including those with US capital, to conduct business and open branches in China. There will also be continued communication on increasing flights between China and the United States, the ministry statement said.

title: Rupee gains against US dollar
author: Recorder Report
description: The Pakistani rupee extended its marginal gains against the US dollar in the interbank market on Monday. The local unit closed the day at 277.15, a gain of Re0.01 against the greenback. title: Russian oil supply to India tightens on reduced exports, strong Chinese demand
author: Reuters
description: MOSCOW/NEW DELHI: Indian refiners expect Russian oil supplies to further tighten in October and November due to reduced exports and stiff competition from China, forcing the world’s third-largest crude importer to buy more costly alternatives for the rest of the year, four trade sources said. India has been the top buyer of seaborne Russian Urals crude since 2022, when Moscow diverted its energy flows away from Europe at deep discounts. However, in recent months, the world’s top crude importer China has ramped up purchases as supplies from the Middle East tightened due to the Iran war. Some Indian refiners would not be getting adequate Russian supplies in October and November, people familiar with procurement plans said. “Demand from China has been really high. They were willing to book cargoes in advance and to pay firmer prices compared to Indian refiners,” a source involved in the sale of Russian crude said. Russian oil arrivals to India are set to fall to around 1.75 million barrels per day in September, the lowest since April, according to analytics firm Kpler. They had already declined 16.5% to about 2.1 million bpd in August from July, trade data showed, although Russia remained India’s main supplier, ahead of the United Arab Emirates and Venezuela. Overall Russian export availability has contracted, notably from the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, where shipments have fallen by roughly half as drone attacks repeatedly suspended loadings. Oil India explores ways to get back Russian dividend India seeks alternatives from Mideast, West Africa Indian refiners have turned to pricier replacement barrels, traders said, seeking UAE Murban, a close substitute for Russia’s Urals grade, while also purchasing Iraqi Basrah and Angolan cargoes. Shipping dynamics have helped redirect flows, with seasonal navigation along the Arctic Northern Sea Route (NSR) providing a secure and cost-effective channel for Russian crude exports to China. In contrast, shipments to India via the Red Sea face heightened security risks linked to the conflict involving Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis. “It’s not so much about the price as ensuring the cargo actually reaches its destination,” a second trader said, adding that freight costs via the Arctic route to China are now broadly comparable with shipments through the Suez Canal.

title: Pakistan becomes first country to join Hong Kong's ValidAP trade verification platform
author: BR Web Desk
description: Pakistan has taken another step towards trusted digital trade with the operationalisation of Pakistan Single Window’s (PSW) integration with ValidAP, a blockchain-based digital document verification platform developed and hosted by the Customs and Excise Department of Hong Kong, China. According to a statement, the integration, which became operational on 25 September 2026, enables electronic trade documents issued through PSW to be independently verified for authenticity and integrity using cryptographic technology, without requiring the underlying document or its sensitive information to be transmitted to or stored on the verification platform. The initiative follows the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between Pakistan Customs and the Customs and Excise Department of Hong Kong on 18 May 2026, formalising Pakistan Customs’ participation in ValidAP. Pakistan is the first country to join the platform, and the integration marks Pakistan’s first implementation of ValidAP-based digital document verification, the statement read. ValidAP uses cryptographic technology to create a unique digital fingerprint, or “hash”, of an electronic trade document. This enables authorities to verify that a document is genuine and has not been altered, without the document itself or its sensitive information being transmitted or stored on the verification platform. Pakistan’s participation in ValidAP also connects its digital trade infrastructure with an emerging regional approach to trusted electronic document verification. For Pakistan, the integration represents a further step towards a digital trade environment in which documents can be issued electronically, verified digitally and trusted across borders. It can help reduce reliance on paper-based verification and support faster and more secure processing of international trade documentation, it added.

title: Indian firms ready $3 billion of debt issues with eye on potential RBI rate hike
author: Reuters
description: MUMBAI: Indian companies are rushing to lock in borrowing costs ahead of a potential rate hike by the central bank, with about $3 billion of rupee debt issuances lined up over the next few days. Large Indian conglomerates, state-run firms, infrastructure investment trusts and non-bank finance companies are preparing at least 290 billion rupees ($3.02 billion) of short- to long-duration bond sales ahead of the central bank’s October 7 monetary policy decision. Some ofthe prominent corporate borrowers issuing debt include Reliance Industries, Vedanta, Delhi International Airport, Adani Airport Holdings and JSW Energy , seeking an aggregate 185 billion rupees, while infrastructure-related firms Cube Highways Trust, Interise Trust and India Infradebt are eyeing 60 billion rupees. “Issuers who have a view that rupee interest rates will go even higher are locking in rates,” said Akshay Naik, India head of debt capital markets at Citibank. “We expect issuances, particularly from large, frequent and high-rated issuers to be absorbed by investors.” India RBI may increase debt sales to drain liquidity after first such auction in 9 years Likely rate hike A large majority of market participants expect the Reserve Bank of India to raise interest rates, with further liquidity-draining measures on the cards. If they’re right, it would mark the RBI’s first rate hike since February 2023. “With the October policy approaching, there is some uncertainty around the direction of interest rates and liquidity conditions,” said Harish Reddy, co-founder, Stable Money, a fixed income investment platform. The policy decision has as its backdrop signs of broadening inflation in India and hikes by major central banks globally, including by the US Federal Reserve. Expectations for RBI policy have shifted over the past month amid a pickup in inflation and stubbornly higher oil prices, bringing prospects of an October rate hike into focus. Several foreign banks, including Citi and Deutsche Bank, have brought forward their rate-hike calls from December to October, while market pricing reflects a higher likelihood of a longer tightening cycle. While a rate hike hanging over the market’s head is pushing up corporate issuance, there is also “a lot of liquidity in the (banking) system to absorb this supply,” said Ankit Gupta, founder and MD, Digifinn, an online bond trading platform.

title: FPCCI seeks one-month extension to the income tax return deadline
author: BR Web Desk
description: Atif Ikram Sheikh, President of the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FPCCI), has formally urged the government and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to extend the deadline for filing income tax returns by one month – moving the cutoff date to October 31, 2026 – to facilitate trade, industry, and other tax filers. According to a statement released on Monday, the apex trade body emphasised that this extension is not a concession but a practical necessity to ensure maximum tax compliance, broaden the tax base, and alleviate the immense pressure currently faced by the business community, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and individual taxpayers. Sheikh highlighted that as the September 30 deadline approaches, taxpayers and tax practitioners are facing severe systemic bottlenecks. The FBR’s IRIS portal has been experiencing frequent slowdowns, glitches, and downtimes due to heavy national traffic. These technical disruptions are preventing thousands of willing taxpayers from submitting their returns and wealth statements accurately and on time, he added. Sheikh explained that the business community of Pakistan remains committed to fulfilling its national duty and contributing to the national exchequer. However, penalising them for systemic inefficiencies and a highly congested and insufficient digital infrastructure is deeply unfair. Income tax returns, wealth statements: PM urged to extend deadline The FPCCI leadership outlined several critical reasons for the demanded extension, pointing first to the severe instability within the FBR’s digital infrastructure. Constant lagging and crashing of the IRIS system during peak hours have made it nearly impossible for tax lawyers, chartered accountants, and individual business owners to process filings efficiently. FPCCI chief maintained that a one-month extension will provide a much-needed breathing space for taxpayers to reconcile their accounts, navigate the recent complexities introduced in the tax code, and file their returns without the fear of system crashes. Sheikh highlighted that the recent complex amendments in tax laws and reporting requirements have created widespread confusion; meaning taxpayers require additional time to thoroughly understand these technicalities to avoid unintended errors in their wealth reconciliations. He stressed that, alongside these technical hurdles, the ongoing macroeconomic challenges, including high inflation and surging operational costs, have severely stretched the administrative capacities of SMEs. Many businesses are struggling to finalize their financial audits and gather the necessary documentation within the rigid timeframe. The FPCCI stressed that granting this extension directly supports the government’s own primary objective of increasing the number of active filers. Rushing the process will inevitably result in a lower volume of submissions, whereas an extended window will yield higher revenue collection and wider, more accurate compliance. Sheikh appealed to the Prime Minister of Pakistan, the Minister for Finance and Revenue, and the Chairman of the FBR to take immediate cognisance of the ground realities. The federation warned that failure to extend the deadline could force many legitimate businesses into the non-filer category, resulting in unwarranted penalties and disruption of commercial activities that the fragile economic conditions cannot sustain.

title: Oil woes push Indian rupee to over one-week low, RBI caps fall near 96/USD
author: Reuters
description: MUMBAI: The Indian rupee slipped to its weakest in more than a week on Monday as oil prices marched higher, dragging down regional stocks and currencies as investors fretted over the impact of high energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty. Dollar sales from state-run banks, most likely on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India, curbed losses with the rupee settling down 0.2% at 95.9825 per dollar. Brent crude rose nearly 4% to $108.2 per barrel. US President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s peace plan, but told Axios in a phone interview that he expected US negotiators to engage in more talks this week. Investors responded by pushing bond yields higher and stocks lower. MSCI’s gauge of Asian stocks fell nearly 1% while stocks in Mumbai declined nearly 1.5% to their lowest level since April. India imports nearly 90% of its crude requirements, making the rupee one of the world’s most vulnerable currencies to the Middle East oil shock. “Several investors just have an outright bearish view on all EM Asia high-yield currencies, including the PHP, IDR and INR, given their vulnerability to higher energy costs,” analysts at Goldman Sachs said in a note, summarising feedback from investors located in the UK. Goldman, meanwhile, says the RBI has the ability to keep the rupee within the 94-97 range, or at least manage the pace of its depreciation. A glut of capital inflows sparked by policy measures has given the Indian central bank ammunition to go against the tide but investors are keeping an eye on the persistence of that defence. Between June 8 and September 18, these measures drew in $143.6 billion. “For now, 96 is the floor under INR and it doesn’t seem like the RBI will allow a move past that,” a trader at a foreign bank said.
