title: Indian shares slide to near six-month low as US-Iran deadlock lifts oil prices
author: Reuters
description: Indian shares fell to near six-month lows on Monday, extending a seven-week losing streak, as oil prices rose after US-Iran peace talks reached a deadlock. US President Donald Trump said he rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the fighting, while Iran said only diplomacy could resolve its conflict with the United States and Israel. The deadlock raised concerns over oil supplies through the key shipping route, pushing Brent crude futures up 3.7% to $108 a barrel. For India, the world’s third-largest crude importer, higher oil prices risk stoking inflation, widening the import bill and squeezing corporate margins. The Nifty 50 fell 1.56% to 22,780.25, while the BSE Sensex shed 1.52% to 72,771.72. The indexes fell nearly 6% over the previous seven weeks, in one of their longest weekly losing streaks on record. “Markets came under renewed selling pressure on the day, with the rise in Brent crude remaining a major concern,” said Sachin Gupta, vice president of research at Choice Broking. “Another important factor is elevated global bond yields. Higher US Treasury yields can make dollar-denominated fixed-income investments relatively more attractive and increase global borrowing costs, potentially reducing foreign investment flows into emerging markets.” All 16 major sectors fell. The broader small-caps and mid-caps slipped 1.9% and 1.6%, respectively. High-weightage financials and banks lost 1.7% and 2%, respectively. Shares of top private lender HDFC Bank and oil-to-telecom conglomerate Reliance Industries slid 2.3% each, while ICICI Bank fell 1.9%. The three firms carry large weights on the benchmarks. Among stocks, Yes Bank fell 5.9% with brokerage Citi flagging near-term pressure on the stock due to weaker earnings, elevated credit costs. Bucking the broader trend, Borosil gained 6% after Investec reiterated “buy” on the consumer goods maker and hiked the price target, citing gains from anti-dumping duty on Chinese borosilicate table and kitchen glassware.

title: Special delivery: India's Tamil Nadu state hands out gold for newborns
author: AFP
description: Under the scheme, all babies born in public health facilities in the state are eligible for a one-gramme gold ring, worth some $143.
text: Authorities in India’s Tamil Nadu state gave babies born in government-run hospitals a free gold ring on Monday, an initiative aimed at boosting confidence in the public healthcare system. Under the scheme launched by actor-turned-Chief Minister Vijay, all babies born in public health facilities in the state are eligible for a one-gramme gold ring, worth some $143. Gold has immense cultural significance in India, featuring prominently in weddings and religious ceremonies, and seen as a safe generational asset. “The gold ring would give the child something valuable to keep for the years ahead,” said one mother at a government hospital in the state’s Madurai district, who declined to give her name. She was among dozens of mothers who cradled their newborns as they queued up to receive the gift. “This scheme feels personal,” another grateful mother, Stella Mary, told AFP. title: Three policemen killed in firing on police vehicle in Tank
author: BR Web Desk
description: Three police personnel were killed and two others injured when unidentified armed men opened fire on a police vehicle in Wazirabad area of Tank district, Aaj News quoted police as saying on Monday. According to police, the attack took place within the jurisdiction of SMA police station, where armed men targeted the police vehicle. Three personnel died at the scene, while two others sustained injuries. Following the attack, a heavy contingent of police reached the area and cordoned it off. Police teams also collected evidence from the crime scene. The bodies of the deceased and the injured were shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital, for medico-legal formalities and medical treatment, respectively. Police launched a search operation in the area to trace and arrest the attackers, while further investigation into the incident was under way. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi condemned the terrorist attack and expressed grief over the deaths of three police personnel. He extended condolences to the families of the deceased and paid tribute to the policemen for their sacrifice. Naqvi said the government stood with the families of the slain personnel and that their sacrifices in the fight against terrorism would not go in vain.

title: Imran Haleem Shaikh to take charge as BankIslami President & CEO from Sept 29
author: BR Web Desk
description: BankIslami Pakistan Limited, Pakistan’s leading Islamic financial institution, has appointed its Deputy Chief Executive Officer Imran Haleem Shaikh as President and Chief Executive Officer for a three-year term effective September 29, 2026. The bank informed the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) in a notice on Monday. “Please be advised that Imran Haleem Shaikh will take charge as President & CEO of BankIslami Pakistan Limited with effect from September 29, 2026,” read the notice. As per information available on LinkedIn, Shaikh joined BankIslami as Deputy Chief Executive Officer in January 2024, after spending more than 13 years at JS Bank, where he served as Chief Operating Officer from July 2020 to December 2023. At JS Bank, he was responsible for retail banking, consumer, product, marketing and administrative functions and was involved in the launch and expansion of Zindigi, the bank’s digital banking platform. Prior to becoming COO, Shaikh served as Chief of Staff and held several senior positions in marketing and brand management at JS Bank. He began his career at JS Group, where he worked in corporate affairs from 2006 to 2010. According to his LinkedIn profile, Shaikh holds a BBA in Marketing from the Institute of Business Management and a master’s degree with a specialisation in AI from HEC Paris. Last month, BankIslami’s Board decided that Rizwan Ata would continue to serve as the bank’s President and CEO until the completion of his current three-year term on September 28, 2026. “The Board recognised and appreciated the efforts of Rizwan Ata,” BankIslami said back then. BankIslami Pakistan appoints chairman, CEO The bank further announced the appointment of Imran Haleem Shaikh as the incoming President and CEO for a three-year term effective September 29, 2026. BankIslami Pakistan Limited was incorporated in Pakistan as a public limited company in 2004, founded by Jahangir Siddiqui & Company Limited and the Randaree family. Dubai Bank later joined as a founding shareholder in 2005. The bank was granted a license as a “Scheduled Islamic Commercial Bank” in 2005 under the Islamic banking policy of 2003 from the SBP, and it officially began operations on April 7, 2006.

title: Establish a gas market for boosting exports
author: Shahid M. Sattar
description: A functioning gas market would reward exploration at home and buy LNG abroad when its full delivered cost is competitive. Pakistan currently does neither. Pakistan’s gas debate is usually presented as a choice between indigenous gas and imported LNG. That framing hides the real problem: Pakistan does not yet have a market capable of telling either source where it is economical, where it is reliable, and where it should lose. The country needs both, but neither should be protected from competition. Local producers should be able to sell directly to creditworthy buyers at transparent market-linked prices. LNG should enter through the same open network whenever its full delivered cost is competitive. The cheapest reliable molecule should win; every subsidy, bottleneck and payment delay that prevents that outcome should be treated as an economic cost. That sounds obvious. Pakistan has managed to make it revolutionary because gas policy still treats molecules as instruments of allocation rather than commodities moving through a disciplined market. Gas is assigned administratively, transported by utilities that also trade it, priced through layers of cross-subsidy and used to rescue whichever part of the energy system is in trouble that month. Producers wait for allocations and payments. Private LNG suppliers wait for pipeline access. Consumers wait for gas. The only thing that moves promptly is circular debt. Exploration policy and LNG policy cannot succeed separately because both depend on the same missing institution: a functioning gas market. The indigenous decline is a market failure The policy debate therefore needs a different sequence. Pakistan should not ask first whether domestic gas or LNG deserves priority. It should ask what market design would make each source reveal its true cost, attract capital where supply can be developed, and exit where it cannot compete. Without that architecture, every new discovery risks becoming another administered allocation and every imported cargo risks becoming another liability on the public balance sheet. The official numbers are stark. During July–March FY2026, Pakistan consumed an average 2,929 mmcfd of gas: 2,316 mmcfd of indigenous supply and 613 mmcfd of RLNG. The Pakistan Economic Survey says depletion of indigenous reserves is a major concern and that no significant discoveries have been made. These figures show more than geological decline; they show a market that has stopped transmitting investable signals. Weak incentives, delayed decisions, payment risk, constrained marketing freedom and a downstream system that cannot reliably convert discovery into cash have turned exploration risk into policy risk. Exploration is risky capital. Investors spend first, often for years, and may find nothing. If they do find gas, they need a bankable route from the wellhead to a paying customer. A policy can offer an attractive headline price, but the incentive is meaningless if allocation is delayed, the buyer is insolvent, the pipeline is controlled by a commercial rival, invoices remain unpaid or government changes the rules after the investment has been sunk. The recent offshore round is encouraging but should be read honestly. Bids covered 23 blocks and about 53,510 square kilometres. The Petroleum Division reports roughly US$80 million of Phase-I commitments, with possible investment of US$750 million to US$1 billion if drilling proceeds. These are commitments, not discoveries. Serious drilling still requires a route from any discovery to a solvent market. Pakistan has done this before The lesson is not theoretical. I was involved in the producer-pricing reforms of the early 1990s that replaced discretionary, rate-of-return thinking with compensation linked to international energy values. The subsequent petroleum policy carried that logic forward through market-related producer pricing, clearer block awards and greater marketing freedom. Foreign and local companies brought capital, technology and management expertise, and national gas production rose from roughly 1,800 mmcfd to around 4,000 mmcfd within the following years. The evidence matters because it shows that geology responds to institutions: when investors can see price, access and payment discipline, capital follows. The point is not nostalgia for one policy formula. Oil linkage designed three decades ago is not automatically the right benchmark today. The point is that investors respond when economic terms are credible, rules are implemented and the route to market is clear. Pakistan later weakened that bargain through delayed payments, administrative allocation, distorted consumer prices and a utility structure that socialized inefficiency. Predictably, investment and production lost momentum. A new upstream policy should therefore offer more than a higher administered price. New, incremental, tight and marginal gas should have the right to be marketed directly to eligible buyers. Prices should be negotiated between willing parties within transparent rules. Producers should receive enforceable payment security and timely foreign-exchange convertibility for legitimate obligations. Exploration blocks should be awarded competitively, data should be accessible, approvals time-bound and contract sanctity treated as an investment requirement – not a favour granted by the government of the day. Imported LNG must compete, not dominate Supporting indigenous exploration does not justify excluding LNG. Domestic fields decline, discoveries arrive unevenly and industrial demand requires reliability. LNG can diversify supply, cover seasonal shortages and provide valuable flexibility. Pakistan’s two terminals are established assets with stated regasification capacity of about 1,200 mmcfd. They should be allowed to serve private suppliers and large consumers directly, not confined to a single state allocation chain. But LNG must pass an honest competitiveness test. The comparison is not the headline cargo price against the wellhead price of domestic gas; it is delivered gas against delivered gas. That means the molecule, freight, port, terminal, retainage, pipeline charge, balancing cost, losses, taxes and financing must all be visible in the same calculation. Contract flexibility and reliability also have value. A cheap cargo burdened by excessive domestic charges is not cheap. Nor is locally produced gas cheap if inefficient network losses and legacy debt are loaded onto every unit sold. Long-term LNG contracts can provide security against spot-market spikes. They should form a prudent core, not an inflexible entitlement that overrides demand. Future contracts need diversion, resale and seasonal flexibility, with limited dependence on any supplier or route. Spot purchases should supplement the portfolio when competitive. “Always term” and “always spot” are slogans; portfolio management is a profession. Separate the pipeline from the trader None of this can work while SNGPL and SSGC control the road and sell the cargo travelling on it. A market cannot discover the cheapest reliable molecule if the owner of the route can also favour its own trade. The network businesses must be separated from commodity trading and operated as regulated common carriers. Their task should be safety, pressure management, metering, balancing and transportation – not deciding which producer, importer or consumer is allowed to transact. Available terminal and pipeline capacity should be published by location and period. Standard firm and interruptible transport products should be offered under common contracts. Booked but unused capacity should be surrendered, reallocated or traded. Network and imbalance charges should be approved transparently. Producers, LNG importers, terminals and licensed suppliers should be free to contract with industrial, power and other qualified buyers. This is not deregulation by abandonment. OGRA should regulate the monopoly network more rigorously while stepping away from commercial allocation. Its job should be to make the market trustworthy: police discriminatory access, audit losses, approve efficient forward-looking transport tariffs, enforce transaction reporting and publish a delivered-cost dashboard. It should not choose the winning molecule. A regulator that allocates business becomes a participant; participants rarely regulate themselves with enthusiasm. Creditworthy demand is exploration infrastructure Pakistan often discusses exploration as if it ends at the wellhead. It does not. A creditworthy industrial buyer is as important to a gas discovery as a seismic survey. Export industries, especially value-added textiles, efficient combined heat and power plants and other qualified consumers should be able to sign enforceable gas-purchase agreements directly with producers or importers. Competitively priced gas is not a concession to such exporters; it is a pre-requisite for enhancing value-added textile exports, protecting margins in global markets and giving producers a bankable demand base. Different buyers may choose firm, interruptible, seasonal or index-linked supply. That diversity creates a market and gives producers a reason to explore. The captive-power levy moved in the opposite direction. It treated efficient cogeneration and inefficient simple-cycle generation alike, destroyed creditworthy gas demand and weakened the economics of both LNG and indigenous supply. Where the grid can provide reliable power and a plant wastes fuel, policy should encourage migration. Where combined heat and power supports exports and uses fuel efficiently, an indiscriminate levy converts an energy customer into an economic casualty. More importantly, none of the market principles proposed here – open access, direct contracting, price discovery, creditworthy demand or competition between local gas and LNG – can take root while the levy remains on its present course. A market cannot be formed by taxing away the demand base that would make it bankable. The problem is not confined to the captive-power levy. Pakistan has built a wider anti-export policy structure in which firms expected to earn foreign exchange are treated as a revenue base. Although exports are formally zero-rated, delayed sales tax refunds force exporters to finance the state interest-free while borrowing at high domestic rates; the delay becomes a hidden tax and, in practice, a form of double taxation when refunds are eroded by inflation or only partly realised. Other burdens include advance and minimum taxes on export proceeds, weakening of the Final Tax Regime, withholding taxes on inputs and services, duties on raw materials and spare parts, regulatory charges, high energy tariffs, cross-subsidies, withdrawal of regionally competitive energy rates, and uncertain duty-drawback or export-support schemes. Fixing the gas market is therefore only one reform among many needed to rebuild export competitiveness, but it addresses the most immediate and damaging constraint: energy costs that are materially higher than those faced by comparable exporting countries. Pakistan is perhaps among the few countries that discourages exports precisely when export earnings are its greatest macroeconomic need. The result is weaker competitiveness, lower investment, reduced capacity utilisation and a smaller foreign-exchange base. In short, policy has turned the export sector from Pakistan’s foreign-exchange engine into one of its most heavily burdened revenue targets. The balance sheet must also be cleaned. The IMF places gas circular debt at about Rs3.4 trillion by December 2025. New producers, importers and consumers cannot be asked to inherit that stock through inflated network charges. Legacy debt, excessive unaccounted-for gas and politically mandated subsidies must be ring-fenced. Lifeline households should be protected through explicit budget support, not by hiding subsidies inside gas prices and sending the bill to the shrinking pool of productive users. Let the molecule compete The reform sequence should be clear: first define open access to transport, then make capacity and charges transparent, then allow qualified buyers and sellers to contract, and only then let price competition reveal the least-cost portfolio. Reversing that order will not work. More LNG without access reform becomes another state procurement problem; higher producer prices without buyers and payment security become another upstream promise the market discounts. A functioning market would strengthen indigenous exploration precisely because it would give a discovery access to buyers and an economic price. It would also strengthen LNG security because terminals and suppliers could serve a broader customer base rather than depend on one state buyer. Competition would reveal when domestic gas is genuinely cheaper, when LNG is attractive and when neither source can support the intended use. Government still has legitimate jobs: award acreage transparently, enforce contracts, regulate safety and monopoly networks, protect vulnerable households and maintain emergency-security rules. It should not procure every molecule, allocate every customer, bury every subsidy and then wonder why exploration stalls while imported gas becomes circular debt. Pakistan’s objective should not be to maximise local gas at any price or LNG at any price. It should be to minimise the reliable delivered cost of gas while creating strong incentives to discover and develop indigenous resources. That requires a market capable of separating economical supply from protected supply, efficient demand from subsidised demand, and public-interest regulation from political allocation. It also requires a change of course on the captive-power levy, because creditworthy demand is not a side issue; it is the commercial foundation on which open access, direct contracting and price discovery depend. For value-added textiles, competitively priced gas is a pre-requisite for export growth, not a sectoral preference. Geology should determine what Pakistan can produce. Competition should determine what it buys. Bureaucracy should stop pretending it can do either better.

title: South African rand slips as US-Iran stalemate pushes oil prices higher
author: Reuters
description: JOHANNESBURG: The South African rand slipped half a percent in early trade on Monday as the US-Iran standoff continued to drive oil prices higher, weighing on risk-sensitive currencies in oil-importing economies. At 0734 GMT the rand traded at 16.40 against the dollar , about 0.5% weaker than its previous close. Oil prices climbed more than 3% on Monday with Brent crude futures last above $107 a barrel, after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal with Iran to resolve their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. South Africa imports most of its fuel, leaving the economy vulnerable to swings in global oil prices since the Iran conflict began in late February. “Volatility in the rand could be elevated this week as the data calendar is jam-packed with data out of the US, culminating in the US non-farm payrolls on Friday,” said Andre Cilliers at TreasuryONE. On the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, the Top-40 index fell 1.7% in early trade. Gold Fields led losses, dropping about 13% after Australia’s Northern Star Resources said it had rejected an unsolicited A$38.7 billion ($27.1 billion) takeover approach. South Africa’s benchmark 2035 government bond also weakened, as the yield rose 5.5 basis points to 8.855%.

title: Xavi pleased with first week as Netherlands coach, but wants more
author: Reuters
description: AMSTERDAM: Netherlands coach Xavi Hernández is pleased with his first week in charge but now wants his side to show an even more attacking game in their next two Nations League fixtures. The Spanish World Cup winner wants the Dutch side playing with more of the attacking intensity that paid off last Thursday when their persistent forays forced a late equaliser against Germany in Amsterdam. This was followed by their first victory under Xavi, a 2-1 defeat of Serbia on Sunday. “It is always most important to get the three points, I’m happy that we managed to do that. But we do need to play better, because, especially in the first half, we did not press well,“ he said. “Nevertheless, I’m very satisfied after a week of work.” Greece stun Germany 1-0 in losing home debut for Klopp Xavi singled out AZ Alkmaar striker Mexx Meerdink, who made his a debut as a substitute against Germany and then marked his first start for the Dutch by scoring both goals against Serbia. “Mexx is a very hard worker who understands how we want to play,“ Xavi said. “He helped the team with more than just his goals, although those certainly helped. The work he did for the team was fantastic.” The Dutch side face Greece next, in Thessaloniki on Thursday, then entertain Serbia in Eindhoven on Sunday. Xavi was clear about where improvements on last week were needed. “For example, there were many moments when we needed to attack the spaces, but we didn’t do it. That is something we need to improve. But also things such as making the pitch wider and moving the ball around more quickly,“ he said. “But the most important thing is that we are creating a lot of chances. The players feel comfortable on the pitch with the structure we are playing in, so a lot of things are also going well.“

title: AKD Securities warns of deepfake scam impersonating Dhedhi, Hina Junaid
author: BR Web Desk
description: AKD Securities Limited has warned investors about AI-generated and deepfake videos impersonating AKD Group Chairman Aqeel Karim Dhedhi and company Chairperson Hina Junaid, saying the content was being used to solicit funds through unauthorised investment schemes and stock-market advisory services. In a notice to the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Monday, the brokerage house said that unidentified individuals or groups had created fake social media accounts and pages, including on Facebook, using the names, photographs and voices of Dhedhi and Junaid, which “are being misused through AI-generated and/or deepfake video content”. “The purpose of this activity appears to be the solicitation of funds under the name of fake & unauthorized schemes/ advisory for investing in listed securities/stocks,” the company said. AKD Securities said it had filed a complaint with the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on September 16 seeking an investigation and registration of a case against those involved, as well as removal or blocking of the fraudulent content from the relevant platforms. “We are pursuing all available legal remedies against those responsible for such fraudulent activities.” “The company hereby categorically denies any connection to the fraudulent content, accounts, callers, or any website or application promoting such claims. Neither Aqeel Karim Dhedhi, Hina Junaid, the company, nor any entity within the AKD Group has launched, endorsed, sponsored, authorised, or otherwise been associated with any such investment scheme, platform, account, page or group,” the listed company said. The brokerage urged investors and the general public “to exercise caution and to refrain from engaging with, relying on, or acting upon any such unauthorised content or calls”.

title: Foreign woman allegedly gang-raped records statement before Lahore magistrate
author: Wajih Ahmad Sheikh
description: The Defence C police has registered a case against three unidentified suspects on the woman’s complaint.
text: LAHORE: A foreign woman who was allegedly gang-raped recorded her statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before a judicial magistrate at the Cantonment Courts on Monday. The 20-year-old Azeri woman had traveled to Pakistan for business purposes and was allegedly gang-raped by three men in a rented flat of a private housing society located near Raiwind on the night between Friday and Saturday. It was the second such case in which a foreign woman was reportedly gang-raped in the Defence C police station area during the last four months. The woman was brought to the court under tight security to record her statement before Judicial Magistrate Muhammad Sagheer. Before the proceedings began, the magistrate ordered all unrelated persons to leave the courtroom. The statement continued for more than an hour. The Defence C police had registered a case against three unidentified suspects on the woman’s complaint. On Sunday, Lahore police requested federal authorities to place the names of the three prime suspects in the case on the Provisional National Identification List (PNIL), saying they had fled Lahore shortly after the alleged assault. A police official said the location of one of the suspects had been traced to Sialkot. Police also took two close relatives and a domestic servant of one of the suspects into custody. DIG Operations Faisal Kamran said all three suspects had been identified and police teams were working to arrest them. He said the case was being investigated jointly by the Crime Control Department (CCD), operations and investigation wings. The vehicle allegedly used in the incident had also been taken into custody, he added. Cantt Division SP Investigation Asim Iftikhar was leading the joint police teams investigating the case, another police official said. In June, two foreign women, nationals of the Netherlands and Venezuela, were allegedly abducted and sexually assaulted in the Defence C police station area. According to the FIR, the women were abducted by five suspects, including a close relative of a senior political personality, who demanded ransom and subjected them to sexual assault during their captivity.

title: 'Hurting' badminton star Sindhu says Asian Games schedule 'took toll'
author: AFP
description: NAGOYA: India’s two-time Olympic badminton medallist P.V. Sindhu said Monday she was “hurting” after defeat following three matches in 18 hours at the Asian Games. The former world champion is the latest badminton player to take aim at the scheduling at the Games in Nagoya. Sindhu battled to defeat over three gruelling games against China’s Chen Yufei in Sunday’s quarter-finals. The 31-year-old played both her second- and third-round matches on Saturday, and was back on court the next day to face former Olympic champion Chen. Following the gruelling last-eight clash, which Chen won 11-21, 21-18, 21-10, Sindhu took to social media to voice her pain at her exit. “I needed a little time to put this into words. My Asian Games campaign is over, and I’m hurting,” she wrote on X to her three million followers. “Three points from closing out that quarter-final. I keep coming back to those three points.” Sindhu, who clinched Olympic silver in 2016 and bronze in 2021, added: “Letting it slip hurts. “Three matches in 18 hours. Back at 3:00 am, out again at 8:30 am. It took a toll.” Sindhu’s India teammate H.S. Prannoy has similarly condemned the scheduling for badminton players at the Games. “It’s cruel because everybody is aiming for a good Asian Games, which comes once in four years,” Prannoy said at the weekend. “To have two singles games in a day, I haven’t seen it like that in ages.”

title: CM Afridi strikes defiant tone as federal ministers rail against KP govt's counter-terror fight
author: News Desk
description: Chaudhry assails KP govt's lack of efforts; Tarar says PTI will have to decide if it is "with Pakistan or with Afghanistan".
text: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday struck a defiant tone and again panned the Centre’s counterterrorism policy as federal ministers railed against his government’s efforts to combat terrorism. Afridi, who was elected as the KP CM in October 2025, has repeatedly voiced his opposition to the federal government’s policies on counterterrorism and Afghanistan. Earlier in the day, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar held a press conference in Islamabad, where they highlighted flaws in the KP government’s “leadership” and governance. Meanwhile in Peshawar, addressing a meeting regarding law and order, the KP CM stressed that merely providing resources to the police would not solve the problem until there was a policy shift. “We repeatedly stated that the state’s current policy was flawed. The blood of our Pakhtuns will flow again,” Afridi said, regretting that federal ministers “dismissed our repeated warnings as propaganda and lies”. The chief minister highlighted that he had been consistently calling for a change to the “failed policy of 22 years”. Flanked by Tarar, Chaudhry said the PTI-led KP government had not made adequate efforts to combat terrorism. He noted that a political leadership could “provide three things in the fight against terrorism: leadership, resources and powers”. Chaudhry contended that the provincial administration in KP — where the PTI has been in power since 2013 — “did not provide leadership to the security forces over the past 14 years”. The interior official accused the PTI-led government of “creating space” for terrorists. “If Pakistan is burning in the fire of terrorism, it is because of KP’s incompetent leadership,” he maintained. Chaudhry then noted that it was the provincial government’s responsibility to allocate funds for counter-terrorism in the budget. “[Then], why did you not provide the resources?” he asked, adding that the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) was still not functional in the entire province. “Your forces cannot fight unarmed. You do not have bulletproof jackets, cars, training, CTD, Safe City [project], or a forensic lab,” he said, claiming that Safe City projects had been completed on the tehsil level as well in Punjab. The state minister sought accountability from KP over the usage of even one per cent of the National Finance Commission (NFC) Award, which he said amounted to Rs800 billion. Chaudhry pointed out that Afridi and his information minister did not attend the funeral prayers of the victims of the Sept 18 Kohat blast , but were rather “busy in their street movement or other matters”. He recalled that the KP CM held a “very lengthy” press conference in Dera Ismail Khan in the wake of Saturday’s suicide blast , which claimed 12 lives. “Why did they not condemn Afghanistan? Why do you have a soft attitude on Afghanistan? Why do you deliberately employ such ambiguity and demeanour, and do not openly condemn or name the real enemy or from where these proxies operate?” he asked. Chaudhry reiterated his criticism of the recent KP Police Act , which has been proposed to replace a 2017 version and is aimed at curtailing the powers of the provincial inspector general (IG). He also responded to PTI’s allegation that the party had not been included in discussions about war on terrorism, saying that the party leadership did not show up to meetings when invited. “You come to Islamabad to demand NFC funds , but your CM does not show up for anti-terrorism meetings,” Chaudhry said. Meanwhile, Tarar said PTI had not taken ownership of the fight against terrorism, again terming the party as the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan’s (TTP) “B team”. He alleged that PTI had facilitated terrorists in its over 12 years of governing KP and that it was not condemning them as it “suits PTI’s financial interests”. “Sohail Afridi organised a ceremony and two Afghans did not stand up to pay respect to the national anthem. If I was there, I would have dealt with them right then and there. I would have banned them,” Tarar said. Such an incident took place in September 2024 , when PTI’s Ali Amin Gandapur was serving as the chief minister. Tarar went on to highlight that the KP government had not ensured the registration of all vehicles yet, as doing so makes the “surveillance of terrorists easier”. He added that potential revenue generated from car registration could have been used for the benefit of the people of KP. “You sacrificed the security of the entire province for your political gains. “You will now have to decide if you are with Pakistan or with Afghanistan. It is as clear as that,” the information minister declared. During his press conference, Chaudhry also highlighted the Afghan Taliban’s support for terrorist activities in Pakistan. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded. The state minister noted that terrorist “proxies are financed by our eastern border and their hideouts are on the western border”. He emphasised that Islamabad had employed “every way” to convey its concerns to Kabul, including dialogue, dossiers and international forums, but to no avail. Referring to the recent attack on a rescue vehicle carrying DI Khan blast victims, Chaudhry said that attacking rescue teams was not allowed even during war. “This is their true face. Is this jihad? Even an enemy with some rules does not carry out such attacks.” He said such terrorist activities were carried out in exchange for receiving funds in dollars, which were proportional to the number of casualties. The interior official asserted that Pakistan had the “best systems” for investigating the identity of a suspected terrorist. “Very few countries have enough data that in less than a minute, any heinous crime or terrorist incident-related information can be accessed in Nadra and other databases […] we instantly find out whether they are Pakistanis [or not].” He then recalled that when authorities did not find any details in the database for a recent incident, they used open-source intelligence and geolocated a terrorist’s picture to Kabul’s Pashtunistan Square. September witnessed another bout of conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan, with the former saying it struck terrorist sites in the border region in response to a recent spate of terrorist attacks . Pakistan conducted “aerial and drone strikes” in another 10 locations across Afghanistan in retaliation for drones launched from across the border that were shot down in KP. The Foreign Office (FO) has said a demarche was also delivered to the Afghan side on Saturday on account of the Sept 23 airspace violation by drones. Meanwhile, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi urged the PTI to further postpone its long march now set for Oct 4 . “Fire is raging here,” he told the media while speaking on the province’s security situation. “I advise the provincial government to postpone their long march due to the law and order situation, call all stakeholders and political parties to discuss peace in the province, and fight terrorism on the frontline.” He contended that the PTI wanted to march on Islamabad and “spread chaos” even when terrorist incidents in KP were claiming people’s lives. On speculations regarding the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, Kundi said that in his opinion, such a move could be taken if the federal government deemed it necessary “to save the province”. He warned the PTI government not to “force the Centre” to impose governor’s rule.

title: 3 traffic policemen martyred in attack on vehicle in KP's Tank
author: Muhammad Irfan Mughal
description: An investigation into the attack was under way, with efforts being made to identify and arrest those involved, police say.
text: DERA ISMAIL KHAN: Three traffic policemen were martyred when unidentified armed men opened fire on their mobile van in the Wazirabad Bazaar area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Tank district, a senior police official confirmed. “Three traffic policemen travelling in the mobile van were martyred on the spot in the attack,” District Police Officer Abdul Samad Khan told Dawn , adding that the attackers fled the scene. Khan said the attackers had also taken away the traffic police vehicle after the incident. However, the vehicle was later recovered from the Garah Budha area, he added. He added that two passers-by were also injured in the firing and were shifted to a hospital for treatment. “Police have sealed the roads and other possible routes, including pedestrian tracks, to prevent the attackers from escaping,” the DPO told Dawn . He said efforts were underway to trace and arrest those involved. The attack triggered a security operation in the area, with police personnel deployed at various points and search efforts continuing. Further details about the identity of the attackers and the motive behind the attack were not immediately available. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi expressed deep sorrow over the attack and sought a report from the relevant senior authorities. In a statement, the governor conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families and colleagues of the martyred policemen. Kundi directed the authorities to ensure that all possible medical treatment was provided to the injured and prayed for their early recovery. Earlier this month, at least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to senior police and district health officials. On July 26, a terrorist attack on a joint police checkpost in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Tank district martyred 15 people, including 14 security personnel, the military’s media wing. Among those martyred were 12 soldiers, two policemen and a government official. In another attack during the same month, two cops were martyred and as many injured in what police suspected was an improvised explosive device (IED) attack. KP has been facing security challenges, and according to monthly data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), mainland KP recorded 54 terrorist attacks last month, marking a 50 per cent increase compared to July.

title: India, Pakistan on Asian Games collision course after cricket washout
author: AFP
description: NAGOYA: India and Pakistan stayed on course to meet in the Asian Games cricket final after both men’s quarter-finals were abandoned Monday because of rain and a sodden outfield in Nagoya. Pakistan went through first against Hong Kong without a ball being bowled under competition rules that say the highest-seeded side progresses. A few hours later, with rain in the air, India progressed against Afghanistan with no prospect of play for the same reason. It deprived spectators at the Korogi Athletic Park the chance to see India’s 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in action. The fearless teenager topped the T20 Indian Premier League batting charts earlier this year. “We are here for the match but unfortunately it rained. The rain started yesterday, so hard luck for us. We would have been happy to play here with India – our players are in form,” said Afghanistan’s Mohammad Akram. World T20 champions India on alert for Afghanistan after Japan scare “We played two matches here on this ground, so we know the condition very well. But unfortunately the rain has ruined everything. “We saw the rain on our mobile phones. Everyone was sad.” Sri Lanka play Nepal and Bangladesh face Malaysia, weather permitting, in the last two quarter-finals on Tuesday.

title: CM Murad approves request to extend Mir Raza judicial commission’s tenure
author: BR Web Desk
description: The tenure of the one-member judicial commission probing the death of young businessman Mir Raza Ali has been extended until October 15, as the panel continues examining alleged lapses in the investigation and medical examination of the case, Aaj News reported on Monday. The commission’s one-month term expired on September 27. According to its registrar, Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah has approved a summary to extend its tenure until October 15, while formal notification of the extension will require approval from the Sindh Cabinet. The commission, headed by Sindh High Court Justice Omar Sial, has currently adjourned proceedings until October 2 to allow completion of statements from remaining witnesses and work on its final report. During its proceedings, the commission has raised questions over the handling of evidence and the performance of the initial investigation team. It has also examined discrepancies in the first post-mortem and issues surrounding the constitution of medical boards. The commission has expressed concern over the handling of CCTV footage from the crime scene. During earlier proceedings, it was told that 52 cameras were installed around the area but footage from only one camera had initially been obtained. The commission also questioned the circumstances in which part of the crime scene was set on fire. Justice Sial has also questioned the performance of the first investigation team and summoned senior officials over issues relating to the investigation and medical examination. The commission has examined alleged discrepancies in Mir Raza’s first post-mortem report, with police surgeon Dr Summaiyya Syed pointing out deficiencies in the report. A subsequent post-mortem reportedly ruled out suicide, according to earlier court proceedings. The commission has also raised concerns over the constitution and functioning of medical boards and summoned senior health officials, including Health Secretary Tahir Hussain Sangi and Director General Health Shehryar Memon, according to the information provided by the commission. Mir Raza’s sister Alishba and family lawyer Jibran Nasir have said they would approach the court seeking the formation of an empowered joint investigation team (JIT) to identify and arrest those responsible for his death, citing shortcomings in the police investigation. Case background Mir Raza Ali, a young businessman, went missing on July 28, 2026, and his body was recovered the following day. Initial police reports suggested suicide, but his family insisted he was murdered. A second post-mortem, conducted after exhumation, revealed signs of torture, multiple fractures, and a gunshot wound from the rear, leading to a murder charge being added to the case. A new police investigation team was formed, and the Sindh High Court constituted a judicial commission to investigate his death. The investigation team has since confirmed that Mir Raza was murdered, ruling out suicide.

title: Belgium’s new boss Van Bommel relishing clash with Zidane
author: Reuters
description: BRUSSELS: Belgium coach Mark van Bommel is relishing the opportunity to pit his wits against Zinedine Zidane but is disappointed that Kylian Mbappe will be missing when they host France in the Nations League on Monday. Van Bommel got off to a dream start in his first game in charge of Belgium with a 2-0 away win over Italy in their Group A1 game on Friday and said he wants his side to keep up the attacking approach they showed in Rome. “I started (my coaching tenure) last Monday by emphasising intensity and willingness to work,” he told a press conference on Sunday. “The idea has to remain the same. Of course, you have to take the quality of the opponent into account, but that does not change our style of play. “If you are beaten in a situation, that’s not a problem. As long as everyone knows what they have to do.” It will also be a second game in charge for Zidane, whose France debut on Friday was a 1-0 win in Turkey where goalscorer Mbappe was injured. “It is special to coach against someone like that,” Van Bommel said. “He was an exceptional footballer and I played against him once, with Barca (Barcelona) against Real Madrid. If a dribbling move is named after you, then you must have done pretty well. As a coach too, of course. He is a good coach, that’s clear. “I think it’s a shame that Mbappe isn’t there, because you always want to have the best footballers playing against you. I don’t know exactly what injury he has, but I would have liked him to be there,” the Belgium coach added. The France captain has since returned to Real Madrid, who said he had suffered a hyperextension of the left knee. On the eve of his debut as Belgium coach, former Dutch international Van Bommel watched his son Ruben debut for the Netherlands and set up a dramatic last-gasp equaliser against Germany in Amsterdam on Thursday. “As a father, you see your son make his debut for the Netherlands, that is already something special,” Van Bommel told reporters. “We happened to be watching on the phone with a large part of the coaching staff, and then he provides an assist like that. It’s fantastic. I would have liked to have been in the stadium. We then also beat Italy. It was two wonderful days.”

title: 5 men held over bomb scare at England base used by US to attack Iran are UK nationals: police
author: Reuters | AFP
description: The five suspects — a 25-year-old, three men aged 24 and a 23-year-old — are all based in London, say police.
text: Five men held over a bomb scare at a British air base used by the US are all UK nationals aged in their mid-20s, British counter-terror police said Monday. The five — a 25-year-old, three men aged 24 and a 23-year-old — all based in London, have been detained since Sunday on suspicion of offences including “preparation of a terrorist act” under UK anti-terrorism laws, according to police. The five were questioned by the police on Monday. Officers detained the group in the early hours of Sunday after they received a tip-off that three large white vans had been seen heading to the military airfield of RAF Fairford in the west of England. US President Donald Trump said the suspects had been looking to do “big damage” and had been under investigation by British and US authorities. However, a local farmer said she had tipped off police after seeing a group of “hooded and masked men” running into the fields. British counterterrorism detectives have publicly shared little about the suspects but a source familiar with the investigation earlier said an Iranian-linked motive was considered the most likely, while a Russian sabotage operation or a terrorism plot were also being looked at as possibilities. Defence minister Wes Streeting told BBC News on Monday that he would not speculate about motives of a live investigation. But he added on the general Iranian threat to the country: “We know that Iran and their proxies wish to do us harm. We know that they hate our democracy, and we know that we regularly have to thwart Iranian attempts to threaten either our interests or indeed our allies.” The Iranian embassy in London said it “categorically rejects and strongly condemns” speculation that Tehran was involved in the bomb scare. In an X post, the embassy criticised “the recent unfounded and malicious speculations published by some British individuals and media outlets attempting to link Iran” to the incident. In May, Britain sanctioned 12 individuals and entities linked to Iran, accusing them of involvement in hostile activity including plotting attacks and providing financial services to groups seeking to destabilise the UK and other countries. Iran has repeatedly denied involvement in attacks or plots in the UK and elsewhere. The British government had given authorisation to the US to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The government has said Prime Minister Andy Burnham is being regularly updated on the incident and he cancelled attending at least two events at his Labour Party’s annual conference on Sunday. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards had warned Britain in July not to allow US bombers to fly from Fairford, saying any base used to launch attacks would be a legitimate target. In Fairford, police have imposed a 400-metre cordon around the base and evacuated residents from 85 homes. A bomb disposal robot could be seen on Sunday operating around the three white vans, while security was stepped up around the base. Armed police stood guard at the main entrance while large machinery was used to block other access points. Security was also stepped up at other US bases in Britain.

title: India's top court says need to fix accountability over Delhi rape cases, media reports
author: Reuters
description: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court of India on Monday pushed for accountability over a recent spate of rape cases in the national capital and neighbouring districts, saying they reflected a “failure of law enforcement”, local media reported. Hundreds of students protested in Delhi last week demanding better safety for women after a teenager said she was gang-raped by three men at a park in the city. Last month, a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped in a moving bus by the driver and conductor, local media reported. The Supreme Court said public spaces, including parks and buses, could not become “high-risk” zones because of poor lighting and surveillance, and other basic facilities, legal news website Live Law reported. The court said fixing accountability was necessary and directed its administration to file a public interest petition on the issue for the court to pursue, legal news website Bar and Bench said. India opposition lawmaker arrested on rape charges Sexual violence is a major problem across India, with more than 80 rapes reported to police every day, according to the National Crime Records Bureau. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta told a TV channel last week that there had been lapses and vowed to improve security, while Delhi Police said it had increased “visible policing” and intensified patrolling.

title: European shares rise as British homebuilders surge on buyer support scheme
author: Reuters
description: European shares edged higher on Monday , supported by a rally in British housebuilders, although gains were capped by a rebound in oil prices and elevated bond yields. The pan-European STOXX 600 was up 0.3% at 640.43 points by 0725 GMT. Most major regional bourses also traded higher. British housebuilders’ stocks surged after the government said it would confirm a new equity loan programme for first-time buyers in next month’s budget, reviving a policy designed at boosting home ownership and supporting home construction. Shares of Persimmon, Barratt Redrow, Taylor Wimpey, Vistry rose between 13% and 17%. However, broader market gains were restrained by a more than 3% jump in Brent crude prices after US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the conflict, keeping Middle East tensions in focus. European energy shares inched 0.5% higher, although miners slumped 2% as greenback-priced metals fell on the back of a stronger dollar. Investors’ focus will also be on speeches from European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde and Bank of England Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden later in the day, especially as markets price in further tightening by major central banks to tame inflationary pressures. Among individual stocks, Akzo Nobel gained roughly 1% after JPMorgan reinstated coverage with an “overweight” rating.

title: MIHAS Awards 2026 celebrates excellence and sets new benchmark for innovation, sustainability and digitalisation across the global halal ecosystem
author: Press Release
description: The MIHAS Awards 2026, one of the key highlights of the Malaysia International Halal Showcase (MIHAS) 2026, concluded today at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC), Kuala Lumpur, recognising outstanding exhibitors that are shaping the future of the global halal industry through excellence, innovation, sustainability and digital transformation. The 2026 edition marked an important evolution of the MIHAS Awards, with a stronger emphasis on future-ready business practices, emerging technologies, digitalisation, sustainability and inclusive growth. The awards recognised companies not only for what they have achieved, but also for how they are innovating, adapting and creating sustainable value in an increasingly competitive and technology-driven global marketplace. A total of 13 awards were presented across three core flagship categories, namely the Excellence Awards; Innovation, Sustainability & Digitalisation Awards; and, for the first time, the Women in Export (WiEX) Awards. Introduced for the first time in 2026, the WiEX Awards recognise exceptional women-led businesses across the Excellence and Innovation, Sustainability & Digitalisation categories, reinforcing MIHAS’s commitment to promoting greater inclusivity and recognising the important contributions of women entrepreneurs and business leaders to the growth and internationalisation of the halal economy. The 2026 awards placed greater emphasis on innovation, sustainability and digitalisation as drivers of competitiveness. In particular, the assessment recognised businesses that are leveraging digital solutions and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), to enhance products and services, improve business processes, strengthen market reach, and create new sources of value. This broader approach reflects the changing nature of the global halal industry, where competitiveness increasingly extends beyond product quality and commercial performance to encompass technology adoption, responsible business practices, innovation capability and the ability to respond to rapidly changing market demands. The MIHAS Awards 2026 were open to eligible Malaysian and international exhibitors participating in MIHAS 2026. Entries underwent a comprehensive and structured evaluation process, comprising pre-assessment and pitching sessions before an independent panel of judges. The pitching component provided applicants with an opportunity to demonstrate their business achievements, innovation capabilities, sustainability initiatives and use of digital technologies and emerging solutions. To further strengthen the integrity, transparency and credibility of the awards, an independent external auditor was appointed to observe and validate the evaluation process. The winners were announced at the official MIHAS Awards 2026 ceremony under the following award categories: ● Product / Service Excellence Awards; ● Product / Service Emerging Star Awards; ● Product / Service Innovation, Sustainability and Digitalisation Awards; ● WiEX Product / Service Excellence Awards; and ● WiEX Product / Service Innovation, Sustainability and Digitalisation Awards. Chairman of MATRADE, YB Dato’ Seri Reezal Merican Naina Merican, said the evolution of the MIHAS Awards reflects the changing priorities of the global halal industry and the need for businesses to remain future-ready. “The MIHAS Awards are no longer only about recognising excellence achieved today. They are also about recognising the capabilities that will shape the halal industry of tomorrow. This year, we have placed greater emphasis on innovation, sustainability, digitalisation and emerging technologies because these are increasingly important to how businesses compete and create value globally. “The winners recognised today have demonstrated the resilience, creativity and forward-thinking capabilities needed to navigate a rapidly changing global marketplace. Through the MIHAS Awards, we hope to inspire more companies to innovate, embrace technology, compete internationally and contribute meaningfully to the continued growth of the global halal economy,” he said. Chief Executive Officer of MATRADE, YBhg. Dato’ Indera Abu Bakar Yusof, said the quality and diversity of entries reflected the increasing sophistication and maturity of businesses within the halal ecosystem. “The entries received this year demonstrate that businesses in the halal ecosystem are continuously evolving, innovating and adapting to meet the demands of a rapidly changing global market. What stood out this year was the increasing recognition of sustainability, digitalisation and emerging technologies as integral components of business competitiveness and long-term growth”. “The introduction of the WiEX Awards and the strengthened assessment framework further broaden the scope of the MIHAS Awards, while the independent validation of the evaluation process by an external auditor, reinforces our commitment to credibility and transparency. Congratulations to all the winners and finalists for their outstanding achievements and for demonstrating the dynamism and diversity of the global halal industry,” he said. Looking ahead, the MIHAS Awards will continue to evolve in line with developments across the global halal ecosystem, with greater recognition for businesses that demonstrate measurable impact, technological adoption, responsible and sustainable growth, innovation and international market potential. The awards will continue to serve not only as a platform to celebrate achievement, but also as a catalyst for businesses to raise their standards, embrace new technologies, pursue sustainable growth and strengthen their global competitiveness. The MIHAS Awards 2026 therefore marks more than a celebration of this year’s achievements. It represents a continued commitment to shaping a more innovative, sustainable, digitally enabled and inclusive halal economy – and to recognising the businesses that are helping to build it.

title: Mir Raza murder case: Judicial commission proceedings adjourned as 30-day tenure ends
author: Ishaq Tanoli
description: The order sheet says that if the cabinet does not extend the tenure, no further witnesses will be called and the report will be submitted on the basis of statements recorded so far.
text: KARACHI: Proceedings of the judicial commission investigating the Mir Raza Ali murder case could not proceed on Monday after its 30-day tenure expired, with a request for an extension until Oct 15 awaiting a decision by the Sindh cabinet. According to the order sheet available with Dawn , the commission was informed that Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah had approved the summary seeking the extension and forwarded it to the provincial cabinet for a decision. The cabinet is expected to meet on Oct 1, the order sheet said, adding that “it was therefore appropriate to adjourn Monday’s proceedings until Oct 2 at 10am”. The order sheet said that if the cabinet decided not to extend the commission’s tenure, no further witnesses would be called and the report would shortly thereafter be submitted on the basis of the statements recorded so far. However, if the cabinet approved the extension, fresh notices would be issued to the witnesses. A questionnaire for three senior police officers would also be sent on Oct 2, it added. On Saturday, the commission had dismissed an application filed by the deceased’s family seeking the personal appearance of the Karachi police chief and the head of the investigation team before the commission. Last week, the judicial commission declined a request by Dr Osama Shaikh, the medico-legal officer who conducted Ali’s first autopsy, to record a further statement. In its order, the commission said it had enough information to determine the facts and circumstances of the case and attribute any negligence. It also cautioned investor Ahmed Bhardey against attempting to derail the proceedings through media statements. The commission had earlier questioned discrepancies in Dr Shaikh’s post-mortem reports. Ali’s body was later exhumed and a second autopsy was conducted, which concluded that he had been shot in the back and ruled out suicide. Ali’s body was found a day after he went missing on July 28. Since then, the case has been mired in controversy, with the deceased’s family accusing the police of trying to bury the facts while the investigators initially attempted to build the case around the possibility of a suicide. Days after the recovery of Ali’s body on July 29, Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed had told Geo News that the post-mortem findings in the case had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs. On August 6, a Karachi court took up an application by Ali’s father, allowed the exhumation of his body, ordered the formation of a medico-legal board for the purpose and directed that a second autopsy of Ali’s body be conducted. The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with police surgeon Dr Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department. While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed. But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, the counsel for Ali’s family, Nasir, accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts. The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on August 8. A day later, the Sindh inspector general of police’s (IG) office notified the reconstitution of the investigating team probing Ali’s death, while Karachi Additional IG Azad Khan transferred the investigation into Ali’s murder to Zaman Town police station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was registered under charges of kidnapping. The order for the probe team’s reconstitution also showed that a murder charge had been added to the first information report. The same day, the Sindh government decided to seek a judicial commission for the case’s investigation, only to defer the plan a day later after Ali’s family said they had made no such demand and had faith in the new investigation team. On Aug 19, Ali’s parents, Mir Hussain and Mariam Hussain, wrote to Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, seeking his “direct supervision of the murder investigation”. They also urged the chief minister to order an investigation and departmental inquiry into the previous investigation team and immediately suspend the officers involved. The provincial government acknowledged the letter and announced the decision on Aug 23 to form a judicial commission to determine whether the investigation in the case was being conducted impartially and to investigate the circumstances surrounding Ali’s death. However, the counsel for Ali’s family approached the SHC, objecting to the provincial government’s decision to form a judicial commission and seeking the formation of an independent and multi-agency JIT “comprising officers who have had no previous involvement in the case”. On Sept 2, the SHC dismissed that petition filed by Ali’s family, observing that constituting such a body was the “prerogative of the government”. Meanwhile, the final report of Ali’s second post-mortem for the Mir Raza Ali murder case confirmed that his death was caused by a gunshot wound to the back. “Death occurred due to cardiac rupture consequent to perforating firearm injury of the chest,” the report stated, adding that the entry wound was on the posterior thorax (back) and the exit wound on the anterior thorax (front of the chest). “The findings are inconsistent with suicide as the manner of death,” it confirmed.

title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 to end fractious weekend with Nations League win
author: Reuters
description: DEBRECEN: Ireland struck three times in the first half to cruise to a 3-0 Nations League victory over Israel on Sunday after a fraught weekend for the team following goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu’s withdrawal from the squad amid a dispute over whether to play the match. Ireland has been one of Europe’s most outspoken critics of Israel’s war in Gaza, and protests calling for the team to boycott the fixture prompted Bazunu to make himself unavailable. The game went ahead only after a majority of the Irish players voted to play. Shlomi Barzel, the Israeli Football Association’s communications chief, said on Saturday that “football has won” after the players decided to fulfil the fixture despite calls for a boycott. Bazunu’s withdrawal led coach Heimir Hallgrimsson to name defender Jimmy Dunne as Ireland’s emergency third goalkeeper. The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has also faced fierce criticism from fans and political figures, many of whom accused it of failing to provide the players with sufficient direction. With Israel’s home games taking place in Debrecen, Hungary’s second-largest city, the game unfolded in a subdued atmosphere reminiscent of the latter stages of the COVID-19 pandemic, when attendance restrictions left stadiums largely empty. There were a few hundred Israeli supporters and a handful of Irish fans in the ground, and the shouts of coaches and players could be clearly heard throughout. The Irish players wore black armbands in memory of all those killed in the conflict and bowed their heads during the Israeli national anthem. There was no exchange of pennants or pre-match handshakes. Striker Troy Parrott netted the opener in the 14th minute, with Adam Idah scoring two minutes later and Jack Moylan adding a well-taken third in the 25th minute. Black armband Moylan ran towards the corner flag after scoring and removed his black armband before kissing it and the badge on his shirt as supporters in the stand booed. After losing their opening game 1-0 to Kosovo on Thursday, Ireland enjoyed a much-needed boost. They are now third in the group on three points, three behind leaders Austria, who beat second-placed Kosovo 3-1 earlier in the day. Any relief provided by the victory, however, may prove short-lived. Angered by the decision to play, many Irish supporters chose not to watch the match. Public broadcaster RTE featured no studio panel and no analysis, nor did the station sell any advertising around its coverage. FAI chief executive David Courell said a significant majority of the squad had voted to fulfil the fixtures. “Based on that, the association took the decision on behalf of Irish football that this fixture would continue, as we have always intended to fulfil the fixtures,” he told a media conference on Saturday. Ireland are due to face Israel again on October 4 in a nominal home fixture that has been moved to Serbia and will be played behind closed doors, meaning the debate over whether the national team should face Israel is almost certain to reignite.

title: Islamabad-Peshawar motorway reopened to traffic following ‘indefinite’ closure
author: Syed Irfan Raza
description: Motorway police say restoration work is underway on M-14 between Hakla and Kundal; N-5 GT Road between Islamabad and Peshawar reopened for traffic.
text: ISLAMABAD: The National Highways & Motorway Police (NH&MP) on Monday said the M-1 Motorway between Islamabad and Peshawar has been reopened to all types of traffic in both directions. M-1, sections of M-14 (Islamabad-Dera Ismail Khan Motorway) and the GT Road (N-5) were closed to traffic last week for an indefinite period amid government pushback ahead of PTI’s long march towards Islamabad — initially scheduled for September 27, but later postponed to October 4. According to a Motorway Police spokesperson, restoration work remained underway on the M-14 motorway between Hakla and Kundal and on the loop connecting the M-1 motorway with the Hazara Motorway. Traffic travelling from Islamabad to Abbottabad via the M-1 can exit at Burhan Interchange, use the GT Road via Hasan Abdal and rejoin the Hazara Expressway at Jhuri Kas Interchange, the spokesperson said. The N-5, or GT Road, between Islamabad and Peshawar has also been reopened to all traffic, the spokesperson said. In a statement issued later, the spokesperson said M-14 had been reopened from Hakla to Kot Belian and from Isa Khel to Yarik. Meanwhile, restoration work on the section between Kot Belian and Isa Khel was still under way, the spokesperson added. In its Sept 22 directives, the motorway police announced that the M-1 was closed to all traffic in both directions between the Islamabad Toll Plaza and Chhachh Interchange, while the M-14 was closed between Hakla and Kundal. The GT Road was also closed at Attock Khurd. Security arrangements were also intensified in Attock, with containers and sandbags placed at key bridges and security tightened at major entry and exit points as authorities prepared for the PTI protest. However, on Sept 25, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said PTI’s long march towards Islamabad would now commence from Peshawar on Oct 4. The party was set to hold a nationwide protest and march towards Islamabad to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan, who is currently incarcerated in Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail. Ahead of the protest, the Punjab government imposed a ban on gatherings across the province for 13 days and prohibited inciting people to “unlawful assembly”. A similar ban under Section 144 has been enforced in Islamabad for two months. The Punjab government also sent a letter to the interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jammed on Sept 27. The federal government also approved the deployment of Rangers in Islamabad and several districts of Punjab from Sept 20 to Oct 5.

title: Foreign woman gang-rape case: Centre moved to place names of suspects on PNIL
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
description: Official says police had traced one of the suspect’s location in Sialkot city.
text: LAHORE: The Lahore Police have moved a request to federal authorities to place the names of three prime suspects, who had allegedly gang-raped a young foreign woman two days ago, on the Provisional National Identification List (PNIL). The 20-year-old victim had traveled to Pakistan for business purposes and was allegedly gang-raped by three men in a rented flat of a private housing society located near Raiwind on the night between Friday and Saturday. It was the second such case in which a foreign woman was reportedly gang-raped in the Defence C police station area during the last four months. Talking about the recent incident, a police official said that the suspects had escaped from Lahore soon after the sexual assault and the police had traced one of the suspect’s location in Sialkot city. He said the police also took two close relatives and one domestic servant of one of the prime suspects into custody. DIG Operations Faisal Kamran said that all the three suspects had been identified and police teams were working to track them down and arrest them. He said the case was being investigated jointly by the Crime Control Department (CCD), operations and investigation wings. The police had taken the vehicle allegedly used in the incident into custody, he added. Another police official said that the Cantt Division SP Investigation Asim Iftikhar was heading the joint police teams working on the case. Published in Dawn, September 28th, 2026

title: CM Afridi wants KP input included in counterterror policy
author: Muhammad Irfan Mughal
description: Afridi visits victims of Dera Ismail Khan attack alongside predecessor Ali Amin Gandapur; urges Centre to involve the province in decision-making, provide resources.
text: DERA ISMAIL KHAN: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Sunday called for better cooperation between the provincial and federal governments on security matters, saying the counterterrorism policy should reflect ground realities. The chief minister made these comments during his visit to Dera Ismail Khan to visit the wounded, a day after a deadly bombing targeting a police and customs check-post killed more than 12 people, including rescue officials, in Darazinda. He was received by his predecessor Ali Amin Gandapur, and the two subsequently visited the hospital where the injured were being treated. Addressing the media, Chief Minister Afridi said his government had warned about the deteriorating security situation in the province and added that people, police personnel and soldiers were bearing the brunt of violence. Afridi visits victims of Dera Ismail Khan attack alongside predecessor Ali Amin Gandapur; urges Centre to involve the province in decision-making, provide resources He said his government provided an additional Rs35 billion to the KP police in the previous financial year for maintaining peace and security. He claimed the province also made payments to federal agencies for the provision of modern weapons, equipment and armoured personnel carriers (APCs), but the required equipment had yet to be delivered. He demanded that the federal government provide APCs to the province without further delay and said the people of KP should be taken into confidence before making decisions about peace and security. “We are picking up coffins on a daily basis,” the CM said, calling for greater cooperation between the federal and provincial governments on security matters. “Peace cannot be established without taking the people of KP into confidence,” he said, adding that his government did not accept policies formulated behind ‘closed doors’. CM Afridi said that anyone taking up arms against Pakistan was a terrorist and expressed concern over the security situation in KP and Balochistan. He said families of those killed in acts of terrorism would be provided with a martyr package. The chief minister also launched a diatribe against ‘some elements’ in the federal government, accusing them of polarising the country. He said those threatening to impose governor’s rule in KP should go ahead and do it instead of issuing threats. Meanwhile, Customs official Farman Khan, who embraced martyrdom in the D.I. Khan suicide bombing, was laid to rest in Ghazni Khel in Lakki Marwat district on Sunday. His body was brought to his hometown from D.I. Khan early in the morning. The martyred official was known in the area for patronising and promoting sports and engaging in social and welfare work. The funeral prayers of the slain personnel were offered at the Ejaz Shaheed police lines on Saturday night. Besides Customs Havaldar Farman, Sepoy Osama and Rescue 1122 officials Imtiaz and Sharifullah were among the deceased. Police personnel presented a guard of honour, while officials laid floral wreaths. Our correspondent in Lakki Marwat also contributed to this report Published in Dawn, September 28th, 2026
