title: Mir Raza judicial commission proceedings adjourned till Oct 2 upon term expiry
author: Nasir Butt
description: Sindh govt to decide on its proposed extension on October 1
text: The judicial commission probing the murder of Mir Raza adjourned its proceedings until October 2 as its existing term expired and the Sindh government is yet to decide on a proposed extension. The Sindh Home Department on August 24 notified the formation of a judicial commission to probe the death of 25-year-old Mir Raza Ali, with Justice Omar Sial appointed as its head following his nomination by the Sindh High Court (SHC) chief justice through a letter dated the same day. The first hearing of the commission took place on September 1. A written order issued by the commission, headed by Justice Sial, said its term had expired on Monday. The commission had requested the Sindh government to extend its tenure until October 15. Read: Mir Raza commission rejects family's plea to summon top cops In response, the provincial government’s focal person Javed Ahmed Abro informed the commission that the summary seeking an extension had been approved by the chief minister and was forwarded to the Sindh Cabinet for a decision. The commission was also told that the cabinet is expected to meet on October 1. “It will be therefore appropriate to adjourn today’s (September 28) proceedings to October 2, 2026 at 10am,” the written order seen by The Express Tribune stated. The order further outlined that if the Sindh Cabinet did not approve an extension, no further witnesses would be summoned and the commission would prepare and submit its report “shortly thereafter” on the basis of statements recorded so far. If the tenure is extended, fresh notices will be issued to witnesses, the order added. The commission will also send questionnaires to three senior police officers as part of the proceedings. It is worth noting that during Monday’s hearing of the judicial commission, Investigation Officer DSP Siraj Lashari and a representative of the Citizens-Police Liaison Committee (CPLC) appeared before the commission to record their statements. However, neither of their statements was recorded as the commission’s term had expired on September 24. Two days earlier, the commission had rejected a request by Raza's family to summon senior police officers in person, directing them instead to submit their questions in writing. A day before that, on September 25, Advocate Jibran Nasir, counsel for the family of Mir Raza, alleged that police had failed to properly investigate the case and were instead attempting to establish the death as a suicide.

title: Israeli occupiers storm Al-Aqsa Mosque in East Jerusalem as Palestinian shops forced to close for ‘Jewish prayers’
author: Anadolu Agency
description: Dozens of Palestinian shopkeepers ordered to close their businesses to allow Jewish prayers during Sukkot
text: Scores of Israeli occupiers stormed Al-Aqsa Mosque in occupied East Jerusalem on Monday, as Israeli authorities forced Palestinian businesses in the Old City to close to allow Jewish prayers during the Sukkot holiday. Videos posted by occupiers on social media showed scores storming the flashpoint site and performing Talmudic rituals, prayers and singing. The rituals were concentrated in the eastern part of the mosque compound. On Sunday, more than 1,500 Israeli occupiers, including National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, forced their way into the Al-Aqsa Mosque to celebrate Sukkot under police protection, according to the Islamic Waqf Department in Jerusalem and Palestinian media. The incursion triggered widespread condemnation, with Palestinian presidential spokesman Nabil Abu Rudeineh describing it as “playing with fire and a dangerous provocation to the feelings of Muslims around the world.” He also warned of a “religious war” that Israel was seeking to ignite in the region. Al-Aqsa Mosque is the world's third-holiest site for Muslims. Jews call the area Temple Mount, claiming it was the site of two Jewish temples in ancient times. Read: Around 100 Israeli occupiers storm Al-Aqsa Mosque compound, perform Talmudic rituals The flashpoint site has seen an increase in occupier incursions since the start of the Jewish holidays, accompanied by Talmudic rituals and prayers inside its courtyards under heavy protection from Israeli police and forces. The Jewish holiday period began with Rosh Hashanah on September 12-13, followed by Yom Kippur on September 21-22. Sukkot runs from Sept. 26 to October 2, followed by Simchat Torah on October 3. Closures Monday’s intrusion came as Israeli authorities forced dozens of Palestinian shopkeepers to close their businesses and residents to remain inside their homes in the Cotton Merchants Market, which leads to Al-Aqsa Mosque, to allow Jewish prayers during Sukkot. “Dozens of Palestinian owners of shops, cafes and restaurants in the Cotton Merchants Market in Jerusalem’s Old City were forced to close them during the Jewish Sukkot holiday to make way for Jewish prayers in the market,” the Association for Civil Rights in Israel said in a statement. The authorities also ordered around 200 Palestinians living along the prayer route not to leave their homes while the prayers were being held, the association said. Traders said this was the first time they had been ordered to close their businesses throughout the holiday period, with previous closures limited to certain hours. The Cotton Merchants Market lies on a route leading to Al-Aqsa Mosque and contains 56 shops, cafes and restaurants, according to the association. Israeli police informed traders of the closure by phone last week before officers later visited the businesses and told owners directly that they had to close during most days of the holiday, it said. Read more: Far-right Israeli minister storms Al-Aqsa Mosque under police protection Police did not provide a written order or instructions regarding the closures, telling traders only that the measure was intended to allow Jewish prayers to be held in the market, according to the association. “The situation did not involve a security event that would justify restrictions of such severity for consecutive days,” it said, adding that police could instead alter the prayer route, shorten prayer hours or deploy forces to protect traders and their businesses. “It is unacceptable for dozens of Palestinian traders to be forced to close their businesses throughout the holiday period and for hundreds of residents to be told to remain in their homes to hold Jewish prayers in the Old City,” said Tal Hassin, an attorney with the association. “The police are turning things upside down: Instead of protecting residents, ensuring the continuation of their daily lives and protecting their property, they are making them pay the price,” she added. “These instructions must be cancelled immediately and the businesses allowed to open.” Palestinians regard East Jerusalem, where Al-Aqsa is located, as the capital of a future Palestinian state, based on international resolutions that do not recognise Israel’s occupation of the city in 1967 or its annexation in 1980.

title: CM Afridi hits back at Centre over criticism of K-P's counterterror response

Peace achieved after two decades of sacrifices was once again lost to unrest following the regime change operation. From the time terrorists moved into the mountains to their subsequent resettlement, we repeatedly warned the federal government, but federal ministers repeatedly dismissed our warnings as propaganda and lies. We repeatedly said that the state’s current policy is wrong and will once again lead to the bloodshed of Pakhtuns,” Afridi said while addressing a meeting on the security situation in the province. His remarks came after federal ministers Attaullah Tarar and Talal Chaudhry criticised the K-P government over its counterterrorism policies. Tarar accused the provincial government of facilitating terrorists for “political and financial interests”, while Chaudhry said the K-P leadership had “not stood united behind its security forces” and had deliberately maintained a “soft attitude” towards terrorists, creating space for them in society. CM Afridi said decisions concerning the province should not be made behind closed doors and called for the K-P government, administration, police and other stakeholders to be involved in formulating security policy. “If you implement that policy, there will be peace here, and our people will not be killed.” The chief minister said that he had repeatedly maintained that peace could be restored within 100 days if the policy he advocated was implemented, but said that the federal government had ignored the province’s position. “When they (terrorists) came down from the mountains, we again said, ‘Look, they are coming down but federal government nevertheless dismissed the warnings as propaganda and accused the provincial government of lying," he added. title: Rain-hit Asian Games battles scheduling logjam
author: REUTERS
description: Cricket quarter-finals are washed out, while tennis and surfing face delays
text: Asian Games organisers faced multiple scheduling headaches on Monday as persistent rain disrupted several competitions at the sprawling multi-sport event. Tennis, surfing and cricket were among sports hit by poor weather on day nine of full competition. Both the men's cricket quarter-finals between Pakistan-Hong Kong and India-Afghanistan were washed out after the playing field was drenched at Korogi Athletic Park on the outskirts of Nagoya. With no contingency built into the schedule, Pakistan and India advanced to the semi-finals of the T20 tournament by virtue of their higher ranking. It was a bitter pill for Afghanistan, which saw the gold medal go to India due to the rankings rule three years ago when their Hangzhou Games final was abandoned due to rain. "The rain started yesterday, so hard luck for us," said Afghanistan opener Mohammed Akram. "We would have been happy to play here with India – our players are in form. "But unfortunately the rain has ruined everything." Powerful typhoon Surigae lashed Japan's southern Okinawa prefecture on Monday and was projected to track northeast toward central Japan and the Tokyo region by midweek, raising the prospect of strong winds and heavy rain further disrupting the Games. Typhoon Dujuan hit the Games early on week one, causing equestrian events in Tokyo to be suspended, though most competitions were unaffected. The continental sporting showpiece is mainly based in the city of Nagoya and Aichi Prefecture but Tokyo is also hosting diving events while Osaka has soccer matches. The rain saw several tennis matches scrapped on Sunday and caused match delays on Monday. Fans hoping to catch Filipino headliner Alex Eala's opening match against Thai opponent Patcharin Cheapchandej were repeatedly frustrated at the Higashiyama Park Tennis Centre. Eala, the women's top seed, had her match shifted off centre court amid the scheduling logjam but was yet to start by mid-afternoon. Poor wave conditions saw the surfing called off early at the Long Beach venue southeast of Nagoya, with medal finals having already been pushed into the final scheduled day on Tuesday. India's Kishore Kumar Anbarasu was able to complete his heat before it was abandoned, beating China's Ma Wensong to make it into the quarter-finals on the sport's Asian Games debut. “It was not the easiest conditions. It was very hard to find the good waves," said Anbarasu. The Asian Games run until October 4.

title: Ravens grab last-second win in Rio
author: AFP
description: Baltimore seals a 34-31 thriller as Commanders stop Seahawks
text: The Baltimore Ravens beat the Dallas Cowboys 34-31 in the NFL's first-ever game in Rio de Janeiro as the Washington Commanders and backup quarterback Marcus Mariota stunned Seattle 33-31 Sunday. The first NFL game at Brazil's iconic Maracana, where the build-up had been dominated by concerns over the soccer stadium's patchy surface, proved to be a breathless thriller decided by a last-gasp 56-yard field goal from Baltimore's Tyler Loop as the clock expired. With Derrick Henry at his unstoppable best, rushing for two early touchdowns, the Baltimore Ravens opened a 24-13 lead in the third quarter. The Cowboys scored 15 without reply to edge ahead, before Ravens rookie Matt Hibner grabbed a touchdown back. Deep in the red zone, Dallas could not force a touchdown, but a field goal with seven seconds remaining appeared to force overtime. Instead, Baltimore quarterback Lamar Jackson hurled the ball 26 yards to Zay Flowers, and immediately called a timeout with one second left -- allowing Loop to kick the Ravens to victory. "Major, major credit to those guys straining all the way till the end," said Ravens coach Jesse Minter. "We felt like we had time to maybe get the ball in range. Unbelievable play by Lamar and Zay, and then obviously Tyler Loop." Earlier Sunday, reeling from two losses and an injury to franchise quarterback Jayden Daniels, the Washington Commanders turned to 32-year-old journeyman Mariota. He completed three passing touchdowns to hand the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks their first loss of the season, and snap Seattle's 12-game winning streak. Seattle's loss came despite their own star quarterback Sam Darnold returning from injury to pass for 379 yards and four touchdowns, with two interceptions. Mariota sent early touchdown passes Rachaad White and Treylon Burks, before his 30-yard hurl to Terry McLaurin opened a 14-point advantage. Seattle fought back to 24-24. But after a Commanders field goal, Darnold's pass was picked by Kain Medrano, a special teams player and backup linebacker, who raced 50 yards to make it 33-24. Seahawks pulled back a touchdown but Washington held on. "That was unbelievable... the more that adversity hits, the more that circumstances pin us against the wall, these guys find a way," said Mariota. Tight finishes On a Sunday packed with tight finishes, Jahmyr Gibbs and the Detroit Lions saw off a spirited Jets fightback, winning 31-24. New York's Garrett Wilson took a superb 4th down catch from Geno Smith that was ruled a touchdown on video review, tying the game 24-24. But the joy was short-lived. Gibbs rushed for his third touchdown, Wilson departed injured, and Jets quarterback Smith was sacked on 4th down to snuff out any hope. In the late game, the Denver Broncos recovered from a 16-0 half-time deficit to score a thrilling 30-26 defeat of the Los Angeles Rams. Denver quarterback Bo Nix stretched into the end zone for a close-range touchdown with 47 seconds remaining for what turned out to be the winning score. Earlier, Cleveland quarterback DeShaun Watson, making his home season debut after being booed by his own fans in the offseason, led the Browns to a last-gasp 21-18 win over Carolina. In the final year of a $230 million five-year contract ravaged by injuries and off-field controversy, Watson threw for two touchdowns, including a go-ahead 14-yard sling to Harold Fannin Jr. under two minutes left. Pittsburgh bagged a late win against Cincinnati. Veteran Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers shook off recent offensive woes with three touchdowns. The Bengals took a fourth-quarter lead, but two field goals and a late strip-sack of Joe Burrow sealed the Steelers win 30-27. The Indianapolis Colts needed a 53-yard field goal with 21 seconds remaining to beat the Houston Texans 19-17. Bills, Chiefs win The Buffalo Bills defeated the winless Los Angeles Chargers 24-16, despite committing five turnovers. The San Francisco 49ers never trailed the Arizona Cardinals in a 36-30 win featuring four touchdown passes from Brock Purdy and two endzone receptions for George Kittle. Kansas City were comfortable 24-10 winners over Miami, while New England -- last year's Super Bowl loser -- was thrashed 35-6 by Jacksonville. Quarterback Kyler Murray returned from concussion in a 23-16 Minnesota win at Tampa Bay, while Las Vegas beat New Orleans 35-27. The Tennessee Titans remain 0-3, as quarterback Cam Ward threw a disastrous interception on a potentially winning drive against the New York Giants, who won 12-7.

title: AJK police arrest 122 over attacks on law-enforcement personnel, property damage
author: Web Desk
description: IGP says 69 FIRs have been registered over unrest that left police, security personnel and civilians injured
text: At least 122 people have been arrested in cases related to attacks on police personnel, injuries to law-enforcement officials and damage to public property during unrest in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), Inspector General of Police (IGP) Captain (retd) Liaquat Ali Malik said on Monday. Speaking at a press conference alongside AJK Chief Secretary Khushal Khan in Muzaffarabad, Malik said 69 FIRs had been registered against groups involved in the unrest and that 122 “disruptive elements” had so far been arrested in connection with the 2025 Chamyati incidents. He said the cases related to attacks in which police personnel were killed or injured and public property was damaged, adding that the state had exercised “patience and restraint” while attempting to resolve the situation peacefully. The IGP said the press conference was held to pay tribute to police and other law-enforcement personnel who had been killed during the unrest, as well as to their injured colleagues and families. He said the personnel had sacrificed their lives for the security and peace of Kashmir while trying to prevent armed groups from disrupting public order and “Kashmiriyat”. According to Malik, some groups had used demands for public rights as a cover to pursue personal loyalties or act at someone else’s direction. He said such groups had repeatedly called for “total closure”, attempted to hold the state hostage, attacked law-enforcement agencies and burned government property. The state had repeatedly shown “patience and restraint” and given peace a chance, including during the latest unrest, he said. “Despite this, up to today, no entry or exit point has been closed. Life is continuing normally, traffic is moving, and markets are open,” he added. The IGP said the government had accepted demands it considered “reasonable” and “logical” and had continued efforts to maintain law and order peacefully. From October 1, 2025 to June 4, 2026, he said, the message accompanying every speech and activity had been “total closure”. The situation escalated again on the night of June 4-5, when law-enforcement personnel were attacked and several were killed, he said. “After that, to maintain the writ of the state, maintain law and order and exercise its authority, the state used the minimum use of force and tried to maintain peace,” he added. text: Eleven teenagers were wounded in a mass shooting at a birthday gathering in the US state of Georgia, with two of them in critical condition, media reports said on Monday. title: Padel takes Olympic step with Asian Games debut
author: AFP
description: The fast-paced sport attracts curious fans in Japan
text: Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Carlos Alcaraz are all obsessed with it, and on Monday the fast-growing racquet sport of padel made its Asian Games debut with officials hoping a place at the Olympics is getting closer. Padel, a cross between tennis and squash on courts surrounded by glass walls, is played by an estimated 38 million people and has ambitions to become a major global sport. It took another step towards that goal at the Asian Games in Nagoya after being added to the continent's biggest sporting spectacular as a medal event. After winning her opening match with doubles partner Danna Abad, Philippines player Joshea Malazarte told AFP: "Padel in Europe is really big and it has just started here, so we're just glad that they added padel." Padel originated in Latin America and has exploded in popularity in the last decade, notably in Europe. Officials say the sport is played in 170 countries and territories, with 85,000 courts around the globe. It is still relatively unknown in Games host Japan, and there was curiosity among some of the crowd at the modest Higashi Sports Centre. Tickets for the event were free, and one spectator told AFP that she and her friend had dropped in to take a look before heading off for lunch. Another, 60-year-old Yuko Hiraiwa, said she enjoyed the action but thought the crowd was "a bit quiet". "I play padel but this was the first time I've seen it live," she said. "It was really dynamic and exciting." Smash hit The sedate atmosphere in Nagoya was a far cry from padel's popularity in other parts of the world. The sport has a professional tour circuit and an event held at the Roland Garros tennis stadium in Paris this month attracted over 80,000 people. A galaxy of padel-playing sports stars including football icons Ronaldo and Messi and Formula One driver Max Verstappen have also given it a boost. Padel has already appeared at the European Games, and International Padel Federation (IPF) official Donatella Del Gaudio said the next goal is the Olympics. "We are working hard to make it happen soon," she said. "We just need to be patient, diligent and respect the Olympic timeline." Padel is usually played as a doubles game and uses solid rather than stringed racquets. The courts are much smaller than in tennis and enclosed by glass walls, which can be used to hit balls off similar to squash. Philippines player Malazarte said padel was "more like a chess match" than tennis. "You have to open up the angle in order to win, you don't rush the points," she said. "Whereas in tennis if you have a really good forehand, really good backhand, you can win a point." Fully booked Padel officials say the sport is enjoyed by people of all ages, and that 50 percent of the worldwide playing population are women. But not all sports that enjoy high playing numbers translate into successful spectator events. Despite millions of players around the world squash failed with four bids to become an Olympic sport until it was finally added to the programme for the 2028 Los Angeles Games. So is padel as much fun to watch as it is to play? "When I watch tournaments live, from the first rounds, every year is getting more and more full," said Kuwaiti player Mariam Al-Sarraj. "Now it's almost fully booked, so I feel like people like to watch it." The sport certainly won some new converts in Nagoya, with the crowd gasping in appreciation at some of the shots and rallies. Interest was raised by the involvement of Japan's Teruaki Ando and Shinnosuke Nakamura, who won a tense thriller against a pair from Lebanon. IPF official Del Gaudio said padel's Asian Games debut was "a source of pride" for everyone in the sport. "It's confirmation of padel's growth worldwide," she said. "It represents a closer step to the Olympics."

title: US forces exit Iraq after two decades, leaving opening for Iran, say experts
author: Reuters
description: BAGHDAD: US forces are set to pull out from their last bases in Iraq by Wednesday, a departure celebrated as a victory by Iran and its allies who now have deep influence in the country where 4,500 Americans died during more than two decades of war. Iraqi security experts say the withdrawal — agreed in 2024 under President Joe Biden and carried out by Donald Trump’s administration even as it wages war against Iran — could give Tehran and its powerful allies free rein, while also allowing other US enemies to stage a comeback, including Islamic State. “Iran stands to benefit strategically from the coalition’s departure because it removes a military presence that for years acted as a counterweight to Tehran’s influence in Iraq,” said Jasim al-Bahadli, an Iraqi security analyst. He predicted that the militia groups would not only portray the departure as a victory for their movement, but also “seek to translate that momentum into greater influence over security and political decision-making”. Abu Mojtaba al-Yasiri, a commander in the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, described the US withdrawal as “a historic victory for the Iraqi Islamic resistance groups and honourable Iraqis, and a crushing defeat for the American project”. US warns Iran over alleged involvement in Iraq unrest “On September 30, we will celebrate the turning of a black page in Iraq’s history and the failure of the occupation to impose its will on our country,” he told Reuters . “Iraq has proven that its sovereignty cannot be secured by foreign forces, but by the resistance and the will of its people.” Not ready While the eventual departure of US forces is broadly popular among Iraqis, those who worry about the strength of the groups fear the withdrawal is premature. “We believe Iraq is still not fully ready to take over the security file at this time,” Abdulrahman al-Zobaie, once a bastion of anti-American resistance, told Reuters . “All Iraqis aspire to full sovereignty, and no Iraqi would dispute that. But I believe that the (US-led coalition) leaving in this way and creating a vacuum is what all Iraqis fear.” American forces invaded Iraq in 2003 to topple Saddam Hussein, and went on to occupy the country before withdrawing at the end of 2011. Around twice as many Americans died in “Operation Iraqi Freedom” as in the parallel war in Afghanistan, which ended with an abrupt US withdrawal in 2021. US military says US, Saudi forces struck sites of Iran-backed groups in Iraq In recent years, Iraq has been the only country to maintain close political and military alliances with both the United States and Iran. The United States killed a top Iranian commander, Qasem Soleimani, with a strike on Baghdad Airport in 2020. Iran’s allies repeatedly fired on US bases, sometimes drawing reprisals. In this year’s war against Iran, 7 of the 18 US service members listed as killed were in Iraq, the last an army sergeant who died during the controlled detonation of a drone at a base near Erbil in July. Victory for Iran’s axis Iran, which says its ultimate aim is to force American forces to leave the entire Middle East, casts the US withdrawal from Iraq as a victory for its “axis of resistance” of allied armed groups across the region. “Lasting security will prevail in Iraq” once the Americans leave the country and the region, the deputy chairman of the National Security Commission of Iran’s Parliament, Amir Hayat Moqaddam, said on Monday. Iran “welcomes the withdrawal of American troops from Iraq and will undoubtedly support it,” he told Iran’s parliamentary news service. “Resistance groups are currently taking action, sometimes targeting and confronting American troops.” Iraq, Syria close airspace after Iran attacks Israel Washington has accused militia groups in Iraq of playing a role in the wider Middle East conflict by launching attacks on neighbouring countries at the direction of Tehran, most recently hitting a major Saudi oil pipeline this month. The Baghdad government says it is trying to curb their influence. New life for Islamic State? Some Iraqi security officials, both in the federal government and the semi-autonomous northern Kurdish region, say the US pullout also risks giving new life to Islamic State, who, despite the defeat of their self-proclaimed caliphate nearly a decade ago, retains a sleeper cell network. A lack of US intelligence, logistical support and drones will give Islamic State a chance to regroup, said Kurdish commander Sirwan Barzani. “For more than two weeks, we have noticed movement by (Islamic State) sleeper cells, after it was announced in the general media that there will be an official withdrawal of the international coalition from Iraq by the end of September,” he said. “This has boosted, in my opinion, the morale” of the fighters. Iraqi security forces said a suspected Islamic State cell was preparing suicide attacks to coincide with the pullout. The plot highlighted concerns that the militant group remains capable of exploiting security gaps despite years of military setbacks, said four Iraqi security and army officials. Islamic State “is seeking to send a message that the group is still powerful and capable of launching bloody attacks,” said Colonel Khalid al-Bayati, a senior security official in the strategic oil town of Kirkuk.

title: Bannu Division emerges as poliovirus epicentre with fourth case
author: BR Web Desk
description: The Regional Reference Laboratory for Polio Eradication on Tuesday confirmed a new polio case, fifth of Pakistan this year, from Bannu district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The affected child is a 17-month-old girl from Khandar Khankhel Union Council in Tehsil Domel of Bannu district. Out of the five total cases reported this year, four have emerged from Bannu Division, with three detected in Bannu district alone. Although overall transmission of the poliovirus across the country has declined since 2025, the presence and circulation of the virus in southern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa remains a persistent concern. Officials stated that due to the effective use of the polio vaccine, polio cases in Pakistan have been reduced by 99.8%—falling from an estimated 20,000 annual cases in the 1990s to 31 in 2025, and restricted to just five cases so far this year. However, the new case underscores the need to further tighten anti-polio campaigns and surveillance nationwide, as no child will be safe from polio until every child is protected. During 2026, four major national campaigns have already been conducted in Pakistan, administering drops to over 45 million children. Last week, a special campaign vaccinated 28 million children; however, the persistent presence of the virus continues to pose a threat to children. Polio is an infectious and incurable disease that can cause lifelong paralysis or death in children, though complete prevention is possible through safe and effective vaccines. Health experts and officials have urged parents, religious leaders, and the media to play their role in dispelling rumours and ensuring full vaccination of children.

title: US, Iran return to indirect diplomacy as Trump rejects proposal but seeks more talks
author: Reuters
description: Talks will focus on amended version of Iran's latest proposal.Iran foreign minister stayed in New York after UN General AssemblyIran vows to reopen Hormuz after US ends blockade, strikes, unfreezes assets.
text: US and Iranian officials spoke separately with mediators on Monday as part of a renewed effort to end seven months of war, according to officials of both countries. Any further talks are expected to focus on an amended version of a seven-day proposal that Iran presented last week on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, an official briefed on the negotiations told Reuters . The war began in late February with US and Israeli attacks on Iran, killing thousands of people over seven months and shocking global markets as vital waterways for oil remained choked. The US and Iran have twice previously agreed to ceasefires in mediated peace talks, in April and June. Those agreements quickly unravelled. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who remained in New York after attending the General Assembly, said Iran expected to receive the US response to its latest ceasefire proposals and its conditions for restoring passage of maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, according to state news agency IRNA . "If the Americans claim they are seeking an agreement or a peaceful solution, we have presented that solution," Araghchi said. US officials separately spoke with mediators on Monday, US President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House, without giving further details. Iran's seven-day plan envisages an end to all hostilities in Iran and Lebanon, the unfreezing of billions of dollars' worth of Iranian assets, an end to sanctions on Iranian oil and the lifting of the US blockade on Iranian ports. Iran would then allow the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for oil tankers, and the two sides would also resume talks on Iran's nuclear program and Trump's wish to seize or eliminate its highly enriched uranium. Trump said on Saturday he had rejected Iran's proposal, saying Iran wanted a swift agreement because of the crippling economic pressure it is under. However, he also told Axios on Sunday that he expected US negotiators to engage in further talks this week. Araghchi said on Sunday that mediators had not formally conveyed a US rejection, and that Iran was awaiting Washington's definitive position before deciding its next steps. "Our conditions are clear, and any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent on these conditions being met," he said on Sunday, adding that only a negotiated solution could resolve the impasse.

text: Saudi Arabia's defence minister invited the UAE's Vice President Mansour bin Zayed to visit the kingdom on Tuesday, in the first public invitation for a face-to-face meeting since a rift between the two over Yemen. "His Royal Highness Prince Khalid bin Salman bin Abdulaziz, Minister of Defence, extended an invitation to his brother, His Highness Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Vice President of the sisterly United Arab Emirates, Deputy Prime Minister and Head of the Presidential Court, to visit the Kingdom tomorrow, Tuesday," the defence ministry said in a statement on X. During the July detente, Saudi General Entertainment Authority chairman Turki Alalshikh posted a picture of bin Salman alongside Sheikh Mansour that he said was taken a few days ago. The Saudi olive branch came as the kingdom reels from weeks of Houthi attacks on its tankers, oil facilities, airports and even its capital, with the group taking control of the Red Sea coast from Saudi-backed government forces. The kingdom has for weeks been reaching out to international allies for help in Yemen. A source from the Yemeni leader's office told AFP earlier this week that he requested American support in a call with US President Donald Trump against the Iran-backed Houthis. The New York Times said the Saudi crown prince called Trump on Sunday "to implore him, again" to help counter the group's advances, and Axios has previously reported that Trump rebuffed a similar request last week. On Friday, meanwhile, the military chiefs of staff of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks on how to support Riyadh as Yemen's Houthis ramp up their attacks on the world's top crude exporter. The UAE and Saudi Arabia had a public falling out in December when the kingdom accused Abu Dhabi of threatening its national security by supporting southern Yemeni separatists who orchestrated a brief offensive. The pair have been at odds in their foreign policy from Yemen and Sudan to the Horn of Africa, where they have supported rival forces.

text: Schools across the Saudi capital Riyadh returned to in-person classes on Monday, as officials remained silent about a decision a day earlier to close schools that appeared to be reversed only hours later. "Please be advised that pursuant to a ministry directive just received, all Riyadh campuses will be open for in-person learning tomorrow. We look forward to welcoming students back on campus," read one message sent to parents late Sunday night. Parents in the Saudi capital told AFP the ordeal left them largely confused. "Both announcements came late at night. It was very confusing for parents and kids. We weren't prepared for Monday and the kids slept late thinking school would be online," one parent in Riyadh told AFP on the condition of anonymity. "What changed their minds so fast," asked another. The announcement on Sunday came a day after the Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted drones and ballistic missiles targeting the kingdom. text: British police were questioning five men on Monday on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences after they were detained near an air base that has been used by the US to strike Iran. Officers detained the five men in the early hours of Sunday after they received a tip-off that three large white vans had been seen heading to the military airfield of RAF Fairford in the west of England. US President Donald Trump said the suspects had been looking to do "big damage" and had been under investigation by British and US authorities. However, a local farmer said she had tipped off police after seeing a group of "hooded and masked men" running into the fields. British counterterrorism detectives have not yet publicly stated who they assessed was involved, but a source familiar with the investigation said an Iranian-linked motive was considered the most likely, while a Russian sabotage operation or a religious plot were also being looked at as possibilities. Defence minister Wes Streeting told BBC News on Monday that he would not speculate about motives of a live investigation. But he added on the general Iranian threat to the country: "We know that Iran and their proxies wish to do us harm. We know that they hate our democracy, and we know that we regularly have to thwart Iranian attempts to threaten either our interests or indeed our allies." In May, Britain sanctioned 12 individuals and entities linked to Iran, accusing them of involvement in hostile activity including plotting attacks and providing financial services to groups seeking to destabilise the UK and other countries. Iran has repeatedly denied involvement in attacks or plots in the UK and elsewhere. The British government had given authorisation to the US to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The government has said Prime Minister Andy Burnham is being regularly updated on the incident and he cancelled attending at least two events at his Labour Party's annual conference on Sunday. Iran's Revolutionary Guards had warned Britain in July not to allow US bombers to fly from Fairford, saying any base used to launch attacks would be a legitimate target. In Fairford, police have imposed a 400-metre cordon around the base and evacuated residents from 85 homes. A bomb disposal robot could be seen on Sunday operating around the three white vans, while security was stepped up around the base. Armed police stood guard at the main entrance while large machinery was used to block other access points. Security was also stepped up at other US bases in Britain.

title: Govt slashes petrol price by Rs1.49, HSD by Rs2.73 per litre
author: Saif ur Rehman
description: New fuel rates will be effective for September 30.Global oil volatility drives change in pricing mechanism.Govt adopts daily fuel price review mechanism.ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Tuesday reduced petrol and high-speed diesel prices...
text: ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Tuesday reduced petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) prices by Rs1.49 and Rs2.73 per litre, respectively, citing changes in international oil prices. After the reduction, petrol will be available at Rs387.54 per litre, while the price of HSD has been fixed at Rs402.24 per litre. According to a Petroleum Division notification, the revised fuel prices will take effect from September 30. Ogra has also begun publishing daily petroleum prices on its website to improve transparency and allow changes in international oil prices to be passed on to consumers more quickly. Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said the daily prices are based on a seven-day average of international market prices, in line with international practice. Amid volatility in global oil rates on the back of renewed hostilities in the Middle East, the government decided to switch to a daily fuel price review mechanism. The government had introduced a weekly fuel price review system after the conflict in the Middle East began on February 28, when Israel and the United States attacked Iran, leading Tehran to shut the Strait of Hormuz — the main route before the war for around a fifth of global energy supplies. Tensions have mounted since a fragile June truce between Tehran and Washington collapsed, reviving fears of full-scale war and disrupting energy flows through the Strait. Previously, the petroleum rates were revised fortnightly. An official document seen by Geo News has revealed key details of the federal cabinet-approved petroleum pricing mechanism, under which Ogra will issue daily ex-depot prices for petrol and high-speed diesel. Under the new framework, fuel prices will be determined using the average international market prices recorded over the previous seven days. The regulator will be authorised to announce daily prices without requiring prior approval from the prime minister or the federal government, while prices notified on Fridays will remain unchanged on Saturdays and Sundays. The document stated that Ogra will publish daily Platts reference prices from July 1, 2026. It also stipulated that the petroleum levy cannot exceed the limit approved by the federal cabinet, while any change in the levy rate will require approval from the Finance Division. The document further outlined revised fuel import arrangements for fiscal year 2026-27. Imports of high-speed diesel will be routed exclusively through Pakistan State Oil (PSO), while oil marketing companies will be allowed to import petrol in line with their market shares. Companies failing to meet import obligations or upliftment requirements will not be granted fresh import permissions for up to nine months. The document also stated that the prices of kerosene oil and light diesel oil would be determined on a daily basis and directed the relevant authorities to ensure the immediate implementation of the new pricing mechanism.

text: PESHAWAR: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Information Secretary Shaukat Yousafzai has urged the party leadership to further postpone the long march, now scheduled for October 4, warning that the risk of emergency rule made it imperative to delay the protest. In the letter addressed to PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar and other party leaders on Tuesday, Yousafzai said the march should be postponed in the wider national interest, particularly given the security situation and increased terrorist activity. He warned that the federal government could use certain issues as a pretext to impose emergency rule, and that a possible attack from Afghanistan could serve as justification for such a move. He said the federal government was building a narrative that the KP government was not cooperating, and that this could lead to attempts to dissolve the provincial government or accuse the party of supporting terrorism, potentially leading to a ban on PTI. He cited PTI founder Imran Khan's own precedent of ending a previous long march to protect workers' lives and urged the leadership to take his concerns seriously. He called for dialogue with the state rather than confrontation. The letter comes days after PTI announced that its long march towards Islamabad, originally scheduled for September 27, had been postponed to October 4. The former ruling party was preparing for a major protest and march on Islamabad, demanding the release of its jailed founder Imran Khan and the “restoration” of constitutional supremacy. Meanwhile, PTI Chairman Gohar rejected the suggestion and reaffirmed the long march decision, saying the party had no intention of dissolving the KP provincial assembly and that Chief Minister Sohail Afridi could not be disqualified under any circumstances. He said no consultation had taken place regarding finding an alternative to Afridi and that reports to the contrary were fabricated. He said Afridi had the full confidence of PTI founder Imran Khan and would remain chief minister. Separately, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said the government had not refused talks with PTI but objected to the party making Imran Khan's release a precondition for dialogue, saying the forum for his release was the courts, not the government. He said while legal and constitutional channels existed, PTI wanted to secure the founder's release through rallies, processions and marching on cities, which was not possible. On the Supreme Court's order regarding Imran's transfer to a private hospital, Tarar said the court had ordered a medical examination which was completed, and that any shortcomings in implementation were for the court to examine — not for street protests to resolve. Meanwhile, PTI Senator Ali Zafar said the postponement of the long march to October 4 now gave the government an opportunity to hold talks, saying if the government took one step, negotiations could begin. He said the meeting between the opposition leader and the government before September 27 could not be called negotiations, and that proper talks should be held through committees in closed rooms. He said the October 4 long march was final and that the government was afraid of it. Meanwhile, opposition leaders held a meeting with Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Parliamentarians Secretary General Nayyar Bukhari at party's central secretariat in Islamabad, according to a press release issued by Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ayn-e-Pakistan. The opposition leaders, including Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, Senator Zeeshan and TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai, invited the PPP to attend an all parties conference. Addressing the media after the meeting, Bukhari said the opposition had proposed an All Parties Conference and that he had given assurances to speak with the party chairman Bilawal Bhutto. Abbas said political parties come together in times of crisis, describing the current moment as difficult and stressing the need for unity and eliminating despondency. Gohar said several proposals had been placed before the meeting, that work on an APC was ongoing, that an invitation had been extended by the united opposition and that provincial autonomy was critical in a democracy. He reiterated that the long march decision remained intact and that political parties, despite differences, were united for democracy.

text: ISLAMABAD: Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Tuesday called on the Afghan Taliban regime to move out of its "militant mindset" and adopt the approach of a responsible state. Speaking at a seminar in Islamabad on Afghanistan's situation and progress towards peace, Tarar said that Kabul's circumstances were "highly complex" and required a lasting solution. "Pakistan believes in peace, dialogue and peaceful coexistence," the minister said, adding that Islamabad had sent several high-level delegations to Afghanistan to help resolve the issue. He recalled that talks on Afghanistan had also been held in Turkiye's Istanbul and Qatar's Doha. Relations between the two countries have remained tense in recent years amid persistent terror attacks in Pakistan, which Islamabad says are largely carried out by militant groups operating from Afghanistan. Pakistan has witnessed a sharp rise in cross-border terrorist incidents, particularly in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, since the Afghan Taliban returned to power in 2021. Islamabad has repeatedly urged Kabul to prevent its territory from being used by militant organisations to carry out attacks inside Pakistan. The two neighbouring nations have engaged in border clashes on several occasions in recent months over the terror incidents, which have claimed the lives of civilians and security personnel in Pakistan. Despite many rounds of talks, both countries failed to reach an agreement to counter cross-border terrorism due to the Afghan Taliban regime's reluctance to take action against militant outfits. Meanwhile, Tarar maintained that many of the problems facing Afghanistan were the result of a "militant mindset", saying the country had significant potential for promoting trade and regional connectivity. He said that peace in Afghanistan could help open trade routes between Central Asia and Pakistan, adding that Central Asian states could gain access to warm waters through Afghanistan. "For peaceful coexistence, we must adopt the principle of live and let others live," Tarar said, adding that only peace could provide the foundation for prosperity. The information minister also expressed concerns over safe havens for terrorists and members of banned organisations in Afghanistan. He said that some sections of Afghanistan's population were not being provided opportunities to play a role in economic development. Tarar said that the Afghan people should be given basic rights and the authority to decide their own future. Regarding talks with Kabul, Tarar said that Pakistan supported negotiations for an amicable solution to the Afghan issue. "Peace will increase prospects for stability and development across the region." However, the information minister warned that Pakistan's desire for peace should not be interpreted as weakness. In May this year, Pakistan received $1.32 billion from the IMF after its Executive Board completed the third review under the EFF, the central bank had said. Pakistan’s 37-month EFF arrangement was approved on September 25, 2024, and is aimed at building resilience and enabling sustainable growth. Key priorities include entrenching macroeconomic stability through sound policy implementation, rebuilding foreign exchange reserves, and broadening the tax base. Meanwhile. the IMF review mission reached the federal capital after spending the last week in Karachi, where it discussed monetary policy, inflation and the exchange rate with the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) high-ups, according to The New s. text: Pakistan has reported its fifth polio case of 2026, with the latest infection identified in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Bannu district, the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) confirmed on Tuesday. According to the NEOC, four of the country's five polio cases recorded this year have been detected in the Bannu division, including three in Bannu district. The latest case involves a 17-month-old girl from Khandar Khankhel Union Council in Tehsil Domel, Bannu district. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa remains the country's hardest-hit province for poliovirus transmission. Of the 31 polio cases reported nationwide in 2025, 20 were recorded in the province, while Sindh reported nine cases and Punjab and Gilgit-Baltistan recorded one case each. Authorities said that polio eradication is a collective responsibility, while Pakistan’s dedicated frontline workers ensure that vaccines reach every child; parents and caregivers play a crucial role by making sure their children receive all recommended doses, including routine immunisations. The authorities added that communities, religious leaders, and the media also play a vital role in promoting vaccination, countering misinformation, and ensuring that every child in Pakistan is protected. Together, we can achieve a polio-free future for every child, in Pakistan and worldwide. The NEOC claimed Pakistan has reduced polio cases by 99.8% through the use of safe and effective vaccines, bringing the annual caseload down from an estimated 20,000 in the early 1990s to 31 in 2025, and five reported so far this year. The NEOC said overall poliovirus transmission has declined since 2025, but the virus continues to circulate persistently in southern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

title: US forces exit Iraq after two decades, leaving opening for Iran
author: Reuters
description: Iran to benefit strategically from coalition's departure, says analyst.Lack of US intelligence to help Daesh regroup: Kurdish fighter.Over 4,500 US troops killed in more than two decades of Iraq war.BAGHDAD: US forces are set to pull...
text: BAGHDAD: US forces are set to pull out from their last bases in Iraq by Wednesday, a departure celebrated as a victory by Iran and its allies who now have deep influence in the country where 4,500 Americans died during more than two decades of war. Iraqi security experts say the withdrawal — agreed in 2024 under President Joe Biden and carried out by Donald Trump's administration even as it wages war against Iran — could give Tehran and its powerful allies free rein, while also allowing other US enemies to stage a comeback, including Daesh. "Iran stands to benefit strategically from the coalition's departure because it removes a military presence that for years acted as a counterweight to Tehran's influence in Iraq," said Jasim al-Bahadli, an Iraqi security analyst. He predicted that the pro-Iranian militia groups would not only portray the departure as a victory for their movement, but also "seek to translate that momentum into greater influence over security and political decision-making". Abu Mojtaba al-Yasiri, a commander in an Iran-backed armed faction, described the US withdrawal as "a historic victory for the Iraqi resistance groups and honourable Iraqis, and a crushing defeat for the American project". "On September 30, we will celebrate the turning of a black page in Iraq’s history and the failure of the occupation to impose its will on our country," he told Reuters . "Iraq has proven that its sovereignty cannot be secured by foreign forces, but by the resistance and the will of its people." While the eventual departure of US forces is broadly popular among Iraqis, those who worry about the strength of the Iran-backed groups fear the withdrawal is premature. "We believe Iraq is still not fully ready to take over the security file at this time," Abdulrahman al-Zobaie, a tribal leader in Fallujah, once a bastion of anti-American resistance, told Reuters . "All Iraqis aspire to full sovereignty, and no Iraqi would dispute that. But I believe that the (US-led coalition) leaving in this way and creating a vacuum is what all Iraqis fear." American forces invaded Iraq in 2003 to topple Saddam Hussein, and went on to occupy the country. They returned less than three years later to help Iraqi forces defeat Daesh in a major war from 2014 to 2017. Around twice as many Americans died in "Operation Iraqi Freedom" as in the parallel war in Afghanistan, which ended with an abrupt US withdrawal in 2021. In recent years, Iraq has been the only country to maintain close political and military alliances with both the United States and Iran, which sometimes used Iraqi territory as a proxy battlefield. The United States killed a top Iranian commander, Qasem Soleimani, with a strike on Baghdad Airport in 2020. Iran's allies repeatedly fired on US bases, sometimes drawing reprisals. In this year's war against Iran, 7 of the 18 US service members listed as killed were in Iraq, the last an army sergeant who died during the controlled detonation of a drone at a base near Erbil in July. Iran, which says its ultimate aim is to force American forces to leave the entire Middle East, casts the US withdrawal from Iraq as a victory for its "axis of resistance" of allied armed groups across the region. "Lasting security will prevail in Iraq" once the Americans leave the country and the region, the deputy chairman of the National Security Commission of Iran's Parliament, Amir Hayat Moqaddam, said on Monday. Iran "welcomes the withdrawal of American troops from Iraq and will undoubtedly support it," he told Iran's parliamentary news service. "Resistance groups are currently taking action, sometimes targeting and confronting American troops." Washington has accused Iran-backed militia groups in Iraq of playing a role in the wider Middle East conflict by launching attacks on neighbouring countries at the direction of Tehran, most recently hitting a major Saudi oil pipeline this month. The Baghdad government says it is trying to curb their influence. At their height, the fighters occupied a third of Iraq and killed thousands of people, including hundreds they videotaped themselves gunning down inside a former US military base. A lack of US intelligence, logistical support and drones will give Daesh a chance to regroup, said Kurdish commander Sirwan Barzani. "For more than two weeks, we have noticed movement by (Daesh) sleeper cells, after it was announced in the general media that there will be an official withdrawal of the international coalition from Iraq by the end of September," he said. "This has boosted, in my opinion, the morale" of the fighters. Iraqi security forces said a suspected Daesh cell was preparing suicide attacks to coincide with the pullout. The plot highlighted concerns that the militant group remains capable of exploiting security gaps despite years of military setbacks, said four Iraqi security and army officials. Daesh "is seeking to send a message that the group is still powerful and capable of launching bloody attacks," said Colonel Khalid al-Bayati, a senior security official in the strategic oil town of Kirkuk.

title: Lahore police get remand of two suspects in Azeri woman's gang-rape case
author: Web Desk
description: Court bars police from arresting female suspect in rape case. Azeri woman records statement before judicial magistrate.Foreign woman alleges Nimra received money from Mohsin.LAHORE: A local court in Lahore on Tuesday granted police a six-day...
text: LAHORE: A local court in Lahore on Tuesday granted police a six-day physical remand of two suspects in the alleged gang rape of an Azerbaijani woman. The Azerbaijani woman had travelled to Pakistan for business purposes and was allegedly gang-raped by three men at a rented flat in Lahore’s Defence area on the night between Friday and Saturday. At the outset of today’s hearing, the case's investigating officer (IO) told the court of Judicial Magistrate Azhar Mahmood that the suspects’ DNA tests had to be conducted, while the arrest of one nominated female suspect was still pending. The IO said the female suspect would be produced before the court tomorrow. After hearing the arguments, the court handed the suspect over to police for a six-day physical remand and adjourned the hearing. Meanwhile, Additional Sessions Judge Riffaqat Ali barred the police from arresting the female suspect in the alleged rape case until October 5 while hearing her petition for interim bail. The court also directed the suspect to join the investigation and ordered police to submit an investigation report. The Azerbaijani woman, 22, earlier alleged before the judicial magistrate that she was sexually assaulted by three men after being made to drink alcohol, The woman recorded her statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before a judicial magistrate on Monday, it emerged on Tuesday. Police have arrested two suspects in the case, while raids are being conducted to arrest third suspect. Police said the two mobile phones belonging to the foreign national have yet to be recovered. According to her statement recorded before the magistrate a day ago, the woman said she had travelled from Istanbul to Islamabad on the 13th. She then went to Faisalabad, where she stayed for five days, before travelling to Lahore with plans to visit Skardu. She said she was unable to continue travelling alone and messaged two women, Nimra and Muskan, suggesting that they meet. According to her statement, she went alone to a cafe at around 11pm, where she met Muskan. Muskan then told her that Nimra was waiting for them, and they went to meet her. The woman said they had food at around 2am when two men arrived in a vehicle, and Nimra invited them to join them. She alleged that Nimra received Rs20,000 to Rs30,000 from a man identified as Mohsin and offered the money to her, but she refused to take it. According to the statement, Mohsin then took her to a separate room where three other men were present. When she asked about Nimra and Muskan, she was told they had left. Azeri woman said she asked to leave but was told she could not go because her friends had taken money. She offered to pay Rs30,000 but was told that they had taken more money. According to the statement, Ali Aziz then allegedly told her that she did not know what they were capable of and attempted to blackmail her. She said Ali Aziz then threatened to call the police on emergency number 15. “I told him to make the call. “When the police did not come for five minutes, I again asked them to let me go,” she said in her statement before the magistrate. According to her statement, the three men then offered her alcohol. “They said they had ordered alcohol and asked me to drink with them. “I asked, ‘If I drink, will you let me go?’ They said yes.” She alleged that after she drank, the men told her to sleep there until the effects wore off. “After that, Mohsin, Ahmed and Ali Aziz sexually assaulted me,” she told the magistrate. The woman said she was subsequently taken somewhere in a vehicle. “I had Rs200,000 in Pakistani currency and an iPhone with me.” According to her statement, the men told her belongings would only be returned if she did not complain to the police. The woman said she was later pushed out of the vehicle and left without her belongings. She then sought help from people nearby and called the police.

title: Shehbaz becomes first Pakistani PM to open trading at London Stock Exchange
author: APP
description: LONDON: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday became the first Pakistani chief executive to open a trading session at the London Stock Exchange .During his visit to the stock exchange, the prime minister formally inaugurated...
text: LONDON: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday became the first Pakistani chief executive to open a trading session at the London Stock Exchange (LSE). During his visit to the stock exchange, the prime minister formally inaugurated Pakistan’s landmark $3 billion dual-tranche sovereign Eurobond. In his address at the LSE headquarters in Paternoster Square, the prime minister highlighted Pakistan’s immense potential to attract high-yield, safe and mutually beneficial foreign investments. He said in recent years, they had worked very hard to strengthen Pakistan’s economy. “As I speak, we have strengthened our macroeconomic indicators, which are very promising and augur well for the future,” he added. The ceremony was attended by LSE Group CEO David Schwimmer, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Advisor on Privatisation Mohammad Ali, Pakistan High Commissioner Tipu Usman, members of the Pakistani delegation and relevant British authorities. The prime minister’s visit to the stock exchange underscored Pakistan’s return to global capital markets and reflected renewed international investor confidence in the country’s economic trajectory. The prime minister, in his remarks, further said that the latest contribution of their finance minister and his team to arrange $3 billion worth of dual-tranche sovereign Eurobonds spoke volumes about their hard work, deep-rooted structural changes, the digitisation of the economy, and taking all the necessary measures to put their national economy back on track. He mentioned the privatisation of Pakistan International Airlines and First Women Bank and informed that the government was now moving towards offloading many other state enterprises, stressing that these must be run by the private sector. He also suggested that this was an area where Pakistan and the UK could work very closely. The prime minister opined that if the Gulf crisis hadn’t erupted, the country would have really taken off. “Like other emerging economies, we are negotiating this challenge while also playing an important role as a peacemaker, mediating between the United States and Iran. I hope that we will continue in this direction,” he added. He also commended the efforts of the finance minister and other related economic ministers, secretaries and government officials who had done a remarkable job in rebuilding Pakistan’s economy. Referring to the Gulf crisis, he emphasised learning new lessons as the investors were now trying to evaluate and assess safer markets. Addressing the CEO of LSE, the prime minister said that they would definitely like to seek his guidance and advice on how to further engage international financial markets to play a role in Pakistan, not just in terms of sovereign debt but through very attractive investments. The prime minister expressing his happiness on his participation to open LSE session, said that it was most definitely not only a moment of great happiness for all of them but also a step towards rebuilding their wonderful connection with the LSE. He also invited Schwimmer to visit Pakistan. The issuance, Pakistan’s largest-ever international bond transaction, attracted nearly $6 billion in global investor demand, almost twice the amount raised, from a broad and geographically diversified institutional investor base. The transaction marks the first issuance under Pakistan’s renewed Global Medium-Term Note (GMTN) Programme, following the country’s successful inaugural Panda Bond and successive sovereign credit-rating upgrades. It forms part of Pakistan’s broader debt-management strategy to diversify funding sources, extend maturities, and reduce refinancing risk.

title: Ali, Samad lead stirring fightback as Pakistan clinch first point at Fifa Asean Cup
author: Faizan Lakhani
description: BANDUNG: Ali Akbar Khan scored his first international goal to spark a stirring fightback as Pakistan came from two goals down in the first half to hold the Philippines to a 2-2 draw in the Fifa Asean Cup on Tuesday, with Abdul Samad Arshad...
text: BANDUNG: Ali Akbar Khan scored his first international goal to spark a stirring fightback as Pakistan came from two goals down in the first half to hold the Philippines to a 2-2 draw in the Fifa Asean Cup on Tuesday, with Abdul Samad Arshad getting the leveller. Nolberto Solano’s men had suffered a 4-0 reverse in their Division I Group B opener against Thailand but they showed incredible powers of recovery in a gritty performance as they got their first goals and the first point in their first-ever appearance in a Fifa competition. Pakistan, ranked 198th, were put under pressure early on by the 136th-ranked Philippines, with the defence having to deal with a barrage of crosses. Mohibullah Afridi put his body on the line to put a low cross behind for a corner while goalkeeper Yousuf Butt denied Andre Leipold one-on-one. Philippines eventually got on the scoresheet with a scrappy goal in the 24th minute. Mohibullah, on the line, turned a header onto the bar but Sandro Reyes was the quickest to react to the rebound and bundled it in. Pakistan had their first effort on goal minutes later; Ali Akbar broke through the Philippines defence only to see his effort saved by a diving Kevin Ray Mendoza. It was a chance missed, and two minutes past the half-hour mark, Philippines made it 2-0. A handball by Mohammad Fazal inside the box led to a penalty being awarded, and Bjorn Kristensen sent Yousuf the wrong way with a spot-kick. Philippines continued to attack with centre-back Haris Zeb blocking a diving header, and Yousuf was called into action minutes later. In the closing moments of the first half, Pakistan went forward on a counterattack, but midfielder Alamgir Ghazi shot high from distance. Head coach Nolberto Solano made two changes at halftime, with Ali Agha and Hayyan Khattak coming on for Alamgir and Umar Nawaz, and Pakistan pulled one back two minutes into the second half. Ali Akbar was found on the left by skipper Abdullah Iqbal, and after weaving past a defender, he scored with a shot between Mendoza’s legs. Moments later, Pakistan went up again with Hayyan eventually shooting wide. On the hour mark, Pakistan breached the Philippines’ defensive line, but Hayyan’s cutback couldn’t reach Ali Akbar. It was soon 2-2. Abdul Samad Arshad won the ball on the right and drove into the box before cutting to his left and shooting past a helpless Mendoza for his second international goal. Solano handed left-back Abdul Rehman and Abdul Samad Khan their international debuts when he brought them on in place of Fazal and Ali Uzair, with Pakistan continuing in the same attacking vein. At the other end, the team effort continued with Mohibullah blocking a shot from point blank on a Philippines counter. With a number of Pakistan fans in the stands cheering them on, Pakistan pressed for a winner, but the Philippines held on.

title: Can the Centre send a provincial govt home?
author: Zebunnisa Burki
description: KARACHI: An elected provincial government in Pakistan cannot simply be dismissed because the federal government has fallen out with it, wants a change of administration or believes it is governing badly. But the constitution does...
text: KARACHI: An elected provincial government in Pakistan cannot simply be dismissed because the federal government has fallen out with it, wants a change of administration or believes it is governing badly. But the constitution does provide several routes through which an elected provincial government can cease to function, or temporarily lose the exercise of its executive powers, before the provincial assembly's normal five-year term. The key distinction, according to constitutional lawyers, is between mechanisms that remove a government through the provincial assembly and exceptional provisions under which the federation can temporarily assume provincial functions. As lawyer Salaar Khan puts it, the post-18th Amendment position leaves "a fairly short list, and all of it runs through the House. A chief minister goes if a fifth of the assembly moves against him and a majority of the total membership votes him out. He goes if the governor, having concluded that he has lost the House, summons it and he cannot win its confidence. He goes if he dissolves the assembly himself, which happens within forty-eight hours of his advice whether or not the governor signs, as we saw in Punjab in January 2023. And he goes if he loses his seat, whether by disqualification or by defection. So, a government can certainly fall without a no-confidence vote. What it cannot do is fall without the House having a say". Lawyer Abdul Moiz Jaferii, however, distinguishes between removing the chief minister and removing the entire provincial government. He says the "only complete removal" of a provincial government is by way of removal of the chief minister through a majority vote of no-confidence under Article 136. Pakistan's constitutional history includes periods when a governor, with presidential approval, possessed much wider powers to dissolve a provincial assembly. Per Khan, "Not too long ago, a provincial government could be sent home by two signatures. The old Article 112(2)(b), the provincial version of Article 58(2)(b), allowed a governor, with the president’s approval, to dissolve an assembly if in his opinion, the province could not be governed in accordance with the constitution and ‘an appeal to the electorate’ was necessary. The 13th Amendment did away with that in 1997; Musharraf brought it back in 2002; the 18th Amendment removed it again in 2010. A governor today simply has no power to dissolve an assembly unless its chief minister has already lost a vote of no-confidence, and even then, only if nobody else can put together a majority, and only with the president's approval". Barrister Ali Tahir similarly says that since the 18th Amendment, "Pakistan’s constitution does not give a governor a general power to sack an elected provincial government or dissolve an Assembly merely because the centre wants a different government". Tahir points to the 1988 dissolution of the Punjab Assembly and cabinet as an illustration: “In 1988, under the then-existing Article 112(2)(b), the Punjab Assembly and cabinet were dismissed along with other assemblies. In Muhammad Sharif v Federation of Pakistan, PLD 1988 Lahore 725, the Lahore High Court found the grounds for dissolution of the national and Punjab assemblies legally unsustainable. It did not ultimately restore them because elections were already approaching, but the important constitutional principle was clear: even a supposedly discretionary dissolution power could not be exercised merely on ‘wish or whim’; there had to be objective constitutional grounds”. Coming to Article 234, Barrister Rida Hosain explains: "Article 234 engages if the president, on receipt of a report from the governor, is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the provincial government cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the constitution. The president may, or if a resolution in this behalf is passed by each house of parliament 'shall' assume to himself or direct the governor of the province to assume on his behalf all or any of the functions of the provincial government". Khokhar and Khan stress that Article 234 requires a report from the governor, presidential action and parliamentary approval for continuation beyond two months, with a maximum constitutional period of six months. Tahir points to its use in Punjab in 2009 and Balochistan in 2013. Hosain describes the constitution as operating in "two modes": ordinary constitutional governance and an exceptional emergency mode. Under Article 232, she says, "a proclamation of emergency may be issued upon a grave threat to the security of Pakistan by war, external aggression, or internal disturbance beyond the provincial government’s capacity to control. In cases of internal disturbance, the constitution contemplates a resolution from the provincial assembly. If the president acts independently, the proclamation must be laid before parliament within ten days". The consequences can be sweeping, adds Hosain: "The federal government may, by order, assume to itself, or direct the governor to assume on its behalf all or any of the functions of the provincial government. Parliament acquires the power to legislate for the province on matters ordinarily outside its legislative competence. The constitutional balance between the federation and the province is altered". On the threshold for an Article 232 emergency based on internal disturbance, high court advocate Hassan Abdullah Niazi says that, particularly in the context of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, "the only available ground is 'internal disturbance', and it must genuinely exceed the provincial government’s capacity to control. This has to be proved through material facts. Political polarisation or an anticipated protest does not meet that threshold under constitutional law, and a proclamation on that basis would be vulnerable to constitutional challenge. Since the 18th Amendment, an emergency on the grounds of 'internal disturbance' requires a resolution of the provincial assembly as a condition precedent". So, can federal intervention remove the chief minister? This question has been tested before the courts. Khan points to the Supreme Court’s decision in Pir Sabir Shah's case in 1994 and the Lahore High Court's decision in Manzoor Wattoo's case in 1996, saying both courts held that a proclamation could suspend a chief minister but could not remove him. Tahir similarly argues that if the question is whether a chief minister continues to command a majority, the constitution provides a direct mechanism for answering it, adding that "what the constitution does not provide is a general power for the governor or federal government simply to 'dismiss' an elected provincial government because of political disagreement, bad relations with the centre, policy differences or a change in political preference. If the real question is whether the chief minister still has a majority, Article 130(7) provides the answer: call the Assembly and count the votes. And if the opposition wants to remove the chief minister, Article 136 provides the answer: move and win a vote of no-confidence". Niazi warns that any such step "will also create a dangerous precedent where the federation can simply dismiss troublesome provincial governments over political differences. This would send us back to the 90s when a succession of federal governments were dismissed on a whim. The PML-N and PPP were the chief victims of this and it is a travesty that they hope to invoke something similar now". Jaferii is sceptical about the effectiveness of judicial safeguards in the current constitutional landscape, saying: "there used to be, but now we have a constitutional court in a post-constitutional order, so all bets are off". Tahir similarly notes the changes following the 26th and 27th Amendments, although "the written constitution still contains mechanisms for constitutional review". Hosain sums up the democratic concern behind these safeguards: "if an elected provincial government can effectively be displaced whenever the federal government considers provincial governance inadequate, the electoral mandate of the province becomes subordinate to the political judgment of the centre. This is not democracy and this is why the emergency powers are time-bound, exceptional powers".
